Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the leg back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The hanging straight leg raise is an advanced core exercise performed by hanging from a pull-up bar and lifting one straight leg at a time in front of the body. It primarily targets the abdominal muscles and also engages the hip flexors.

name: hanging straight twisting leg hip raise
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended and your legs straight.
Engage your core and lift your legs up towards your chest, keeping them straight.
Once your legs are parallel to the ground, twist your hips to one side, bringing your legs towards that side.
Pause for a moment, then return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement, but this time twist your hips to the opposite side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The hanging straight twisting leg hip raise is a challenging core exercise that targets the abs, obliques, and hip flexors. It requires hanging from a pull-up bar, lifting the legs, and twisting the hips to engage the entire core.

name: hip raise (bent knee)
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place your hands by your sides, palms facing down.
Engage your core and lift your feet off the ground, bringing your knees over your hips and curling your hips off the floor so your feet point towards the ceiling.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips and feet back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The hip raise (bent knee) is a bodyweight exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, especially the lower abs. It involves lying on your back, lifting the bent legs and curling the hips off the ground toward the chest.

name: hyperextension (on bench)
instructions: Lie face down on a flat bench so that your hips are at the end of the bench and your upper body hangs off it, legs extended along the bench (have a partner hold your ankles if needed).
Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands behind your head.
Slowly lower your upper body towards the ground while keeping your back straight.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then raise your upper body back up until it is in line with your legs.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The hyperextension (on bench) is a bodyweight exercise that targets the spinal erectors and lower back, while also engaging the glutes and hamstrings. It is performed lying face down on a flat bench with the upper body off the end, lowering and raising the upper body while keeping the back straight.

name: hyperextension
instructions: Adjust the hyperextension bench so that your upper thighs are resting on the pad and your feet are secured.
Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands behind your head.
Lower your upper body towards the ground while keeping your back straight.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then raise your upper body back up until it is in line with your legs.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The hyperextension is a bodyweight exercise that targets the spinal erectors and lower back, with secondary emphasis on the glutes and hamstrings. It is performed on a hyperextension bench and involves lowering and raising the upper body while keeping the back straight.

name: incline close-grip push-up
instructions: Place your hands close together on an elevated surface, such as a fixed bar or bench, narrower than shoulder-width apart.
Extend your legs behind you, resting on the balls of your feet, with your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest towards the elevated surface by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The incline close-grip push-up is a bodyweight exercise that targets the triceps, with secondary emphasis on the chest and shoulders. It is performed by placing the hands on an elevated surface, keeping the elbows close to the body, and performing a push-up motion.

name: incline leg hip raise (leg straight)
instructions: Lie on an incline bench with your head at the top end, your back flat against the bench and your legs extended straight out in front of you.
Reach behind your head and grip the top of the bench for support.
Engaging your abs, lift your legs off the bench, keeping them straight, until they point to the ceiling and your hips lift off the bench.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The incline leg hip raise (leg straight) is an abdominal exercise performed on an incline bench. It targets the abs and also works the hip flexors. The movement requires you to lift your straight legs upward while lying on an incline, emphasizing core control and strength.

name: decline push up depth jump
instructions: Place two low steps shoulder-width apart in front of a bench.
Rest your feet on the bench and place one hand on each step, arms extended and body in a straight line from head to heels.
Drop your hands off the steps to the floor between them, absorbing the landing by bending your elbows and lowering your chest towards the floor.
Push explosively through your palms so your hands leave the floor.
Land with your hands back on the steps, arms slightly bent, and stabilize.
Repeat the drop and push for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The incline push up depth jump is a plyometric push-up performed with the feet elevated on a bench and the hands dropping from two low steps to the floor. It targets the chest, triceps, shoulders, and core, and develops upper body explosiveness.

name: incline push-up
instructions: Place your hands on an elevated surface, such as a bench or step, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Extend your legs behind you, resting on the balls of your feet, creating a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lower your chest towards the elevated surface by bending your elbows, keeping your body in a straight line.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The incline push-up is a bodyweight exercise that targets the pectoral muscles by performing a push-up with the hands elevated on a surface such as a bench or step. This variation reduces the load compared to a standard push-up, making it more accessible for beginners.

name: incline reverse grip push-up
instructions: Grip a fixed bar at about hip height, such as a Smith machine bar, with an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Extend your legs behind you, resting on the balls of your feet, creating a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lower your chest towards the bar by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the starting position by extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The incline reverse grip push-up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the pectorals, performed with hands on an elevated surface and palms facing towards you (reverse grip). It emphasizes the upper chest and triceps while requiring stability and control.

name: incline twisting sit-up
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Lie down on the bench with your feet secured under the foot pads.
Place your hands behind your head or across your chest.
Engage your abs and lift your upper body off the bench, curling forward.
As you curl up, twist your torso to one side, bringing your elbow towards the opposite knee.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat the movement, this time twisting your torso to the other side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The incline twisting sit-up is an abdominal exercise performed on an incline bench, targeting the abs and obliques by adding a rotational movement to the traditional sit-up.

name: inverse leg curl (bench support)
instructions: Kneel on the pad of a back-extension or glute-ham bench with your ankles hooked under the rollers.
Keep your hips bent and your torso leaning forward over your knees, hands resting on your thighs or crossed on your chest.
Slowly lower your upper body forward and down over the front of the pad, letting your knees extend.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then contract your hamstrings to pull your body back up to the kneeling starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The inverse leg curl (bench support) is a bodyweight exercise targeting the hamstrings, performed kneeling on a bench pad with the ankles anchored while the upper body lowers forward and is pulled back up by the hamstrings.

name: inverted row v. 2
instructions: Grab a high pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Swing your legs up and hook them over the bar so you hang upside down, head pointing to the floor.
Start with your arms extended and your body hanging below the bar.
Keep your core tight and pull your chest up towards the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The inverted row v. 2 is an advanced bodyweight exercise targeting the upper back, performed hanging upside down from a high bar and pulling the chest up toward it. It also engages the biceps, forearms and core.

name: inverted row with straps
instructions: Set up a suspension trainer or straps at chest height.
Stand facing the anchor point and grab the handles with an overhand grip.
Walk your feet forward, leaning back until your body is at an angle.
Keep your body straight and engage your core.
Pull your chest towards the handles, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The inverted row with straps is a bodyweight exercise targeting the upper back, performed using suspension straps. It requires pulling your chest towards the handles while maintaining a straight body position.

name: inverted row
instructions: Set up a bar at waist height or use a suspension trainer.
Stand facing the bar or suspension trainer, with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grab the bar or handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lean back, keeping your body straight and your heels on the ground.
Pull your chest towards the bar or handles, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The inverted row is a bodyweight exercise that targets the upper back and also works the biceps and forearms. It involves pulling your chest up to a bar or suspension trainer while keeping your body straight, making it an effective movement for building upper body strength and improving posture.

name: isometric wipers
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands wider than shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest until it is just above the floor.
Holding this low position, shift your body towards your right hand, bending the right elbow more while the left arm straightens slightly.
Pause for a moment, then shift back through the center without rising.
Repeat the movement, this time shifting towards your left hand.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Isometric wipers are a challenging bodyweight exercise that targets the pectorals while also engaging the shoulders, triceps, and core. You hold the bottom of a wide push-up and shift your body from side to side without pushing up.

name: burpee with overhead jump
instructions: Start in a standing position with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower your body into a squat position, placing your hands on the ground in front of you.
Kick your feet back, landing in a plank position with your arms straight.
Hold the plank briefly, keeping your body in a straight line.
Jump your feet forward, landing in a squat position.
Jump up explosively, reaching your arms overhead.
Land softly and immediately lower back into the squat position to begin the next repetition.
description: The jack burpee is a high-intensity, full-body exercise that combines a squat, a plank kick-back and a jump to elevate heart rate and improve cardiovascular fitness while also engaging multiple muscle groups.

name: jackknife sit-up
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your legs extended and your arms overhead.
Engage your core and lift your legs and upper body simultaneously, reaching your hands towards your toes.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs and upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The jackknife sit-up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the abdominal muscles. It involves simultaneously lifting the legs and upper body to meet in the middle, engaging the core and hip flexors.

name: janda sit-up
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Cross your arms in front of your chest.
Engaging your abs, slowly lift your upper body off the ground, curling forward until your torso is almost upright.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The Janda sit-up is an advanced abdominal exercise that emphasizes the abs while minimizing hip flexor involvement. It requires significant core strength and proper technique to perform safely and effectively.

name: jump squat v. 2
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
Jump explosively, extending your hips and knees fully.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and immediately lower your body back into a squat position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The jump squat v. 2 is a plyometric lower body exercise that targets the glutes, quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. It involves explosive jumping from a squat position and landing softly before repeating the movement.

name: jump squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back, bringing your hands together in front of your chest.
Jump explosively off the ground, extending your hips, knees, and ankles.
While in mid-air, let your arms swing down to your sides.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and immediately go into the next repetition.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The jump squat is a plyometric exercise that targets the glutes and also works the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. It involves squatting down and then jumping explosively, making it effective for building lower body power and explosiveness.

name: kettlebell advanced windmill
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Hold a kettlebell in your right hand, with your arm extended overhead and your palm facing forward.
Place your left hand on your left hip or lower back.
Keeping both legs straight, bend your torso sideways to the left.
Keep your right arm extended vertically overhead and your eyes on the kettlebell.
Keep your hips stable and avoid twisting your torso as you bend.
Lower your torso to the side as far as you comfortably can while the kettlebell stays locked out above you.
Pause for a moment, then engage your obliques to return to the upright starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The kettlebell advanced windmill is a challenging exercise that targets the abs and obliques while also engaging the shoulders. It requires balance, coordination, and strength, particularly in the core and shoulders, as you hold a kettlebell overhead and bend your torso to the side.

name: kettlebell alternating hang clean
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Allow the kettlebells to hang in front of your body with your arms fully extended.
In one fluid motion, explosively extend your hips, shrug your shoulders, and pull the kettlebells up towards your shoulders.
As the kettlebells reach shoulder height, rotate your wrists and catch the kettlebells in the rack position, with your palms facing inward and the kettlebells resting on the outside of your forearms.
Lower the kettlebells back down to the starting position and repeat the movement with the opposite arm.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell alternating hang clean is a dynamic exercise targeting the forearms, with significant involvement of the shoulders, traps, and core. It requires coordination, explosive power, and proper technique to safely transition the kettlebell from the hang to the rack position while alternating arms.

name: kettlebell alternating press on floor
instructions: Start by lying on your back on the floor with your legs extended straight.
Hold a kettlebell in each hand, with your palms facing towards your feet and your arms extended straight up towards the ceiling.
Lower one kettlebell down towards your shoulder while keeping the other kettlebell extended straight up.
Press the lowered kettlebell back up to the starting position, then lower the other kettlebell down towards your shoulder.
Continue alternating the press motion with each kettlebell for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell alternating press on floor is a chest exercise performed while lying on the floor, pressing kettlebells alternately with each arm. This movement targets the pectorals and also works the shoulders and triceps.

name: kettlebell alternating press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at shoulder height.
Press one kettlebell overhead, fully extending your arm.
Lower the kettlebell back to shoulder height.
Repeat with the other arm.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell alternating press is a shoulder exercise where you press one kettlebell overhead at a time, alternating arms. This movement targets the deltoids and also engages the triceps and core for stability.

name: kettlebell alternating renegade row
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands gripping the kettlebells and your feet hip-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Pull one kettlebell up towards your chest, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Lower the kettlebell back down to the starting position and repeat with the other arm.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell alternating renegade row is a compound exercise that targets the upper back while also engaging the core and shoulders. It requires maintaining a plank position while performing alternating rows with kettlebells, challenging both strength and stability.

name: kettlebell alternating row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a kettlebell in each hand with your palms facing your body.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull one kettlebell up towards your chest, keeping your elbow close to your body and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower the kettlebell back down to the starting position and repeat with the other arm.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell alternating row is a compound exercise targeting the upper back, performed by alternating rowing movements with kettlebells while maintaining a bent-over position.

name: kettlebell arnold press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height with your palm facing towards you.
Engage your core and press the kettlebell overhead, rotating your palm to face forward as you extend your arm.
Pause at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the kettlebell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The kettlebell Arnold press is a shoulder exercise that involves pressing kettlebells overhead while rotating the wrists, targeting the deltoids and engaging the triceps and upper back. It requires coordination and control due to the rotational movement and the instability of kettlebells.

name: kettlebell bent press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in your right hand racked at your shoulder.
Keep your right elbow tucked against your side and your eyes on the kettlebell.
Shift your weight onto your right leg and start bending your torso sideways to the left.
Slide your left hand down the side of your left leg as your torso lowers.
As your body moves under the kettlebell, let your right arm straighten until it is locked out vertically overhead.
Keep your chest lifted and your eyes on the kettlebell throughout.
Engage your core and obliques to return to an upright position, bringing the kettlebell back to your shoulder.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The kettlebell bent press is a complex movement that targets the abs while also engaging the shoulders, triceps, and obliques. It requires strength, coordination, and mobility to perform safely and effectively.

name: kettlebell bottoms up clean from the hang position
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand with an overhand grip.
Keep your back straight and your chest up.
Allow the kettlebell to hang down at your side, with your arm fully extended.
In one fluid motion, extend your hips and knees while pulling the kettlebell up in front of your body.
As the kettlebell rises, rotate your wrist so that the bottom of the kettlebell is facing up.
Catch the kettlebell in front of your shoulder with your elbow bent, your forearm vertical, and the bottom of the kettlebell pointing to the ceiling.
Lower the kettlebell back down to the starting position by reversing the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The kettlebell bottoms up clean from the hang position is a dynamic exercise that targets the biceps while also engaging the forearms and shoulders. It requires coordination, grip strength, and control to stabilize the kettlebell in the bottoms-up position.

name: kettlebell double alternating hang clean
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Allow the kettlebells to hang straight down in front of your body.
Explosively extend your hips and knees while pulling one kettlebell up; keep the other kettlebell hanging.
Pull the working kettlebell close to your body towards your shoulder, keeping the elbow close.
Catch it at shoulder height with your palm facing inward, then lower it back to the hang.
Repeat with the other arm and keep alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell double alternating hang clean is a dynamic exercise that targets the biceps while also engaging the forearms and shoulders. It involves explosive hip and knee extension to lift one kettlebell at a time from a hanging position to shoulder height, alternating sides.

name: kettlebell double jerk
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at shoulder height.
Engage your core and keep your elbows close to your body.
Bend your knees slightly in a quick dip.
Explosively extend your hips and knees, driving the kettlebells upward.
As the kettlebells rise, step one foot forward and the other back into a split stance, dropping under the weights.
Lock out your arms and catch the kettlebells overhead in the split stance.
Bring your feet back together while keeping the kettlebells overhead, then lower them to your shoulders.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating the front leg if you wish.
description: The kettlebell double jerk is a dynamic overhead pressing movement that involves using two kettlebells. It requires explosive power, coordination, and proper technique to safely drive the weights overhead using a combination of leg and upper body strength.

name: kettlebell double push press
instructions: Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at shoulder height.
Bend your knees slightly and engage your core.
Initiate the movement by explosively extending your hips, knees, and ankles, driving the kettlebells overhead.
As the kettlebells reach the top, press them fully overhead, locking out your arms.
Lower the kettlebells back to the starting position by bending your elbows and bringing them back down to shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell double push press is a compound movement that targets the shoulders (delts) and involves explosive power from the lower body to drive two kettlebells overhead. It requires coordination, strength, and proper technique to perform safely.

name: kettlebell double snatch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at arm's length in front of your thighs.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back flat and chest up.
In one explosive motion, extend your hips, knees, and ankles, and simultaneously pull the kettlebells up towards your shoulders.
As the kettlebells reach shoulder level, rotate your wrists and punch the kettlebells overhead, fully extending your arms.
Lower the kettlebells back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell double snatch is a dynamic, full-body movement that targets the shoulders (delts) and also engages the trapezius, forearms, and core. It requires explosive power, coordination, and proper technique to perform safely and effectively.

name: kettlebell double windmill
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand.
Extend your right arm overhead, keeping your eyes on the top kettlebell, and let the left kettlebell hang at your side.
Rotate your left foot 45 degrees to the left and your right foot 90 degrees to the right.
Bend at the waist to the left, keeping your right arm extended overhead.
Lower the left-hand kettlebell along your left leg towards your left foot.
Pause for a moment, then engage your core and push through your right foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The kettlebell double windmill is a dynamic exercise that targets the abs while also engaging the shoulders and hamstrings. It requires holding one kettlebell overhead and another in the low hand while bending at the waist, demanding core strength, shoulder stability, and hamstring flexibility.

name: kettlebell extended range one arm press on floor
instructions: Start by lying on your back on the floor with your legs extended straight and your free arm out to the side.
Hold a kettlebell in one hand, with your palm facing towards your feet.
Extend your arm straight up towards the ceiling, keeping your elbow locked and your wrist straight.
Slowly lower the kettlebell back down to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
description: The kettlebell extended range one arm press on floor is a unilateral chest exercise performed on the floor, emphasizing the pectorals while also engaging the triceps and shoulders. It requires stability, control, and strength to press the kettlebell through an extended range of motion.

name: kettlebell figure 8
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Pass the kettlebell between your legs, switching hands as it reaches the back of your legs.
As the kettlebell comes forward, pass it to the other hand between your legs.
Continue passing the kettlebell between your legs in a figure 8 motion.
Maintain a steady pace and engage your core throughout the exercise.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell figure 8 is a dynamic core exercise that involves passing a kettlebell between your legs in a figure 8 pattern, engaging the abs, shoulders, and forearms while also challenging coordination and stability.

name: kettlebell front squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
Hold a kettlebell in each hand in the rack position at your shoulders, elbows tucked close to your body.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you lower your hips down and back, as if sitting into a chair.
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Drive through your heels to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell front squat is a lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps and also works the glutes, hamstrings, and calves. It involves holding two kettlebells in the front-rack position at the shoulders and performing a squat, emphasizing core engagement and an upright torso.

name: kettlebell goblet squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell close to your chest with both hands.
Keeping your chest up and core engaged, lower your body down into a squat position by bending at the knees and hips.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell goblet squat is a lower body exercise that targets the glutes while also engaging the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. It involves holding a kettlebell close to the chest and performing a squat, making it a great movement for building strength and improving squat technique.

name: kettlebell hang clean
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in front of your thighs.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Lower the kettlebell towards the ground, allowing it to swing between your legs.
Quickly extend your hips and knees, using the momentum to swing the kettlebell up to shoulder height.
As the kettlebell reaches shoulder height, rotate your wrists and catch the kettlebell in the rack position, with your elbow tucked in and the kettlebell resting on your forearm.
Lower the kettlebell back down to the starting position between your legs, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell hang clean is a dynamic exercise that targets the hamstrings and also works the glutes, quadriceps, and calves. It involves swinging a kettlebell from between the legs up to the rack position at the shoulder, requiring explosive hip extension, coordination, and proper technique to perform safely.

name: kettlebell lunge pass through
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in your left hand at your side.
Take a step with your left foot to place it in front, lowering your body into a lunge until your back knee is close to the floor.
At the bottom, pass the kettlebell under your left thigh from your left hand to your right hand.
Push off to return to the standing position, holding the kettlebell in your right hand.
Repeat the lunge with your right leg in front, passing the kettlebell under your right thigh to your left hand.
Continue alternating lunges and passing the kettlebell between hands for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell lunge pass through is a dynamic lower body exercise that combines a traditional lunge with a kettlebell hand-off beneath the front thigh, challenging balance, coordination, and strength.

name: kettlebell one arm clean and jerk
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand with an overhand grip.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips, lowering the kettlebell between your legs.
Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles, using the momentum to swing the kettlebell up to shoulder height.
As the kettlebell reaches shoulder height, rotate your wrist and punch your hand straight up, locking out your arm overhead.
Lower the kettlebell back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell one arm clean and jerk is a dynamic, compound exercise that targets the deltoids while also engaging the triceps and core. It requires coordination, explosive power, and proper technique to perform safely and effectively.

name: kettlebell one arm jerk
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height.
Bend your knees slightly and engage your core.
Press the kettlebell overhead in a straight line, fully extending your arm.
As you press the kettlebell overhead, simultaneously dip your knees and quickly straighten them to generate momentum.
As the kettlebell reaches its highest point, quickly drop underneath it by bending your knees and hips.
Catch the kettlebell with a slight bend in your knees and hips, and your arm fully extended overhead.
Stand up straight, fully extending your knees and hips, and stabilize the kettlebell overhead.
Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position by bending your knees and hips, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell one arm jerk is a dynamic overhead pressing movement that involves using the legs and hips to help drive a kettlebell overhead with one arm. It requires coordination, timing, and strength, especially in the shoulders, triceps, and core.

name: kettlebell one arm military press to the side
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height.
Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Press the kettlebell overhead, extending your arm fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the kettlebell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The kettlebell one arm military press to the side is a unilateral overhead pressing movement that targets the deltoids, with secondary emphasis on the triceps and core for stabilization. It requires balance, coordination, and shoulder strength.

name: kettlebell one arm push press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand at shoulder level.
Bend your knees slightly and engage your core.
Press the kettlebell overhead by extending your arm and fully extending your legs.
Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position by bending your knees and bringing the kettlebell back to your shoulder.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The kettlebell one arm push press is a compound exercise that targets the deltoids while also engaging the triceps and core. It involves pressing a kettlebell overhead with one arm, using a slight leg drive to assist the movement.

name: kettlebell one arm row
instructions: Stand in a staggered stance with one foot forward, holding a kettlebell in the hand opposite the front leg.
Hinge forward at the hips, rest your free hand on your front thigh, and keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the kettlebell up towards your hip, keeping your elbow close to your body and squeezing your shoulder blade back.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the kettlebell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and repeat with the other arm.
description: The kettlebell one arm row is a unilateral pulling exercise that targets the upper back, with secondary emphasis on the biceps and forearms. It requires maintaining a stable hip hinge position while rowing the kettlebell with one arm, promoting strength and muscle development in the upper back and improving core stability.

name: kettlebell one arm snatch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand between your legs.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips, lowering the kettlebell towards the ground.
Explosively extend your hips and knees, using the momentum to swing the kettlebell up towards your shoulder.
As the kettlebell reaches shoulder height, rotate your hand and punch it straight up overhead, fully extending your arm.
Lower the kettlebell back down between your legs and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell one arm snatch is a dynamic, full-body exercise that targets the shoulders (delts) and also engages the trapezius, forearms, and core. It requires explosive power, coordination, and proper technique to perform safely and effectively.

name: kettlebell pirate supper legs
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand in front of your thighs.
Keep your torso upright and your core engaged.
Raise the kettlebell in front of you with your arm straight, keeping a slight bend in the elbow.
Continue the arc until the kettlebell is overhead.
Lower the kettlebell along the same path back to the starting position in front of your thighs.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The kettlebell pirate supper legs exercise targets the deltoids and involves raising a kettlebell with a straight arm in an arc from the thighs to overhead, requiring shoulder strength and stability.

name: kettlebell pistol squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in front of your chest with both hands.
Lift your left foot off the ground and extend it forward, keeping it parallel to the ground.
Slowly lower your body down into a squat position, keeping your right foot flat on the ground and your left leg extended.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the squat, then push through your right heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The kettlebell pistol squat is a challenging single-leg squat variation that targets the glutes, quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. It requires significant strength, balance, and mobility, as well as experience with both pistol squats and kettlebell handling.

name: kettlebell plyo push-up
instructions: Start in a high plank position with one hand on a kettlebell and the other hand on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
Lower your chest towards the ground, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Push through your hands explosively and shift your body sideways over the kettlebell.
Land with the other hand on the kettlebell and the first hand on the floor, then immediately lower your chest for the next repetition.
Repeat, alternating sides, for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell plyo push-up is an explosive push-up variation performed with one hand on a kettlebell, targeting the chest, triceps, shoulders, and core. It requires significant upper body strength, stability, and coordination, as well as explosive power to switch hands over the kettlebell and land safely.

name: kettlebell seated press
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and spread wide, keeping your back straight.
Hold a kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height and extend your free arm out to the side.
Press the kettlebell overhead, fully extending your arm.
Lower the kettlebell back to shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The kettlebell seated press is a shoulder exercise performed while seated on the floor, pressing a kettlebell overhead with one arm to target the deltoids, with secondary emphasis on the triceps and core.

name: kettlebell seesaw press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at shoulder height.
Press one kettlebell overhead while keeping the other kettlebell at shoulder height.
Lower the pressed kettlebell back to shoulder height while simultaneously pressing the other kettlebell overhead.
Continue alternating the pressing motion, creating a seesaw-like movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell seesaw press is a shoulder exercise that involves pressing kettlebells overhead in an alternating fashion, challenging both strength and coordination.

name: kettlebell sumo high pull
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing outwards.
Hold a kettlebell with both hands in front of your body, arms extended downwards.
Bend your knees and lower your hips into a squat position, keeping your back straight.
Drive through your heels and explosively extend your hips and knees, pulling the kettlebell up towards your chin.
As you pull the kettlebell up, keep your elbows high and wide, and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower the kettlebell back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell sumo high pull is a compound exercise that targets the traps and also works the shoulders, glutes, and hamstrings. It involves a wide-stance squat combined with an explosive pull of the kettlebell to chin height.

name: kettlebell swing
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward.
Hold the kettlebell with both hands in front of your body, arms extended.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips, pushing your butt back.
Swing the kettlebell back between your legs, keeping your arms straight and maintaining a flat back.
Drive your hips forward and swing the kettlebell up to shoulder height, using the momentum generated by your hips.
Allow the kettlebell to swing back down between your legs and repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell swing is a dynamic exercise that targets the glutes and also engages the hamstrings and core. It involves swinging a kettlebell between the legs and up to shoulder height using hip drive and momentum.

name: kettlebell thruster
instructions: Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand in the rack position at your shoulders.
Lower into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back, keeping your chest up and your back straight.
As you reach the bottom of the squat, explosively drive through your heels to stand up, simultaneously pressing the kettlebells overhead.
Lock out your arms at the top of the movement, fully extending your elbows.
Lower the kettlebells back to your shoulders by bending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell thruster is a compound exercise that combines a squat with an overhead press, targeting the shoulders while also engaging the quadriceps, glutes, and core. It requires coordination, strength, and some experience with kettlebell handling.

name: kettlebell turkish get up (squat style)
instructions: Start by lying on your back with your legs extended and the kettlebell held in your right hand, arm fully extended above your shoulder.
Bend your right knee and place your right foot flat on the ground, keeping your left leg extended.
Pressing through your right foot, lift your hips off the ground, coming into a bridge position.
Slide your left leg underneath your body, bending your left knee and placing your left foot flat on the ground.
Rotate your torso to the left, bringing your left hand to the ground for support.
Pressing through your right foot and left hand, lift your torso off the ground, coming into a kneeling position.
From the kneeling position, stand up, keeping the kettlebell extended overhead.
Reverse the movement to return to the starting position.
Repeat the exercise on the other side, starting with the kettlebell in your left hand.
description: The kettlebell Turkish get up (squat style) is a complex, full-body movement that targets the glutes and also works the quadriceps, hamstrings, and core. It requires strength, coordination, balance, and mobility, making it a challenging exercise.

name: kettlebell two arm clean
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips, lowering the kettlebells between your legs.
Explosively extend your hips and knees, using the momentum to pull the kettlebells up towards your shoulders.
As the kettlebells reach shoulder height, rotate your wrists and catch them in the rack position, with your elbows tucked in and each kettlebell resting on the back of your forearm.
Lower the kettlebells back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell two arm clean is a dynamic movement that targets the deltoids while also engaging the traps and forearms. It requires coordination, explosive power, and proper technique to safely bring two kettlebells from between the legs to the rack position.

name: kettlebell two arm military press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at shoulder level with your palms facing forward.
Engage your core and press the kettlebells overhead, fully extending your arms.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the kettlebells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell two arm military press is a shoulder exercise that involves pressing two kettlebells overhead from shoulder level, targeting the deltoids and engaging the triceps and upper back.

name: kettlebell windmill
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in your right hand overhead.
Rotate your left foot outwards about 45 degrees and keep your right foot pointing forward.
Bend your torso to the left side, keeping your right arm extended overhead and your eyes on the kettlebell.
Lower your torso as far as you can while keeping your right arm straight and your left arm extended to the side.
Pause for a moment, then return to the starting position by pushing through your right foot and engaging your obliques.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The kettlebell windmill is a compound exercise that targets the abs and obliques while also engaging the shoulders and improving overall core stability and mobility. It requires holding a kettlebell overhead and bending at the waist, demanding strength, balance, and coordination.

name: kick out sit
instructions: Stand with your back against a wall and slide down until your knees are bent at a 90-degree angle and your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Extend your arms out to the sides at shoulder height and keep your back flat against the wall.
Lift one foot off the ground and extend that leg straight out in front of you.
Pause for a moment, then bend the knee and place the foot back on the ground.
Repeat with the other leg, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kick out sit is a bodyweight exercise performed in a wall sit that targets the quadriceps, hamstrings and glutes. It involves holding a seated position against a wall and alternately extending one leg straight out in front of you.

name: kipping muscle up
instructions: Start by hanging from a pair of gymnastic rings with your arms extended and your knees bent.
Engage your core and use a swinging motion to generate momentum.
As you swing, pull your chest towards the rings, keeping them close to your body and using your lats and biceps to initiate the movement.
Continue the upward motion until your chest reaches the rings, then transition into a dip position by pushing down on the rings and extending your arms.
Lower yourself back down to the starting position by bending your arms and controlling the descent.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kipping muscle up is a dynamic bodyweight exercise performed on gymnastic rings that combines a pull-up with a dip, using momentum to transition from below to above the rings. It primarily targets the lats and requires significant upper body strength, coordination, and explosive power.

name: landmine 180
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the free end of the barbell with both hands, arms extended, in front of your hips.
Keeping your arms straight, rotate your torso to the right and bring the end of the barbell to the outside of your right hip, pivoting your back foot.
Reverse the motion and rotate your torso to the left, moving the barbell in an arc in front of your body to the outside of your left hip.
Continue this twisting motion, alternating sides, for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The landmine 180 is a rotational core exercise performed with a barbell anchored at one end. It targets the abs and obliques, requiring the lifter to move the barbell in an arc from hip to hip, engaging the core, hips, and legs for stability and power.

name: leg pull in flat bench
instructions: Lie on your back on a flat bench with your hips near the end and your legs extended straight out.
Grip the sides of the bench beside your hips for support.
Engage your abs and bring your knees towards your chest.
Pause for a moment, then slowly extend your legs back out to the starting position without letting them drop.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The leg pull in flat bench is an abdominal exercise performed lying on a flat bench using only body weight. It targets the abs and also works the hip flexors. The movement involves extending the legs out and pulling the knees toward the chest, requiring core strength and stability.

name: lever alternating narrow grip seated row
instructions: Adjust the seat height and footplate position to ensure proper alignment.
Sit on the machine with your back straight and feet flat on the footplate.
Grasp the handles with a narrow grip, palms facing each other.
Keep your chest up and shoulders back throughout the exercise.
Pull one handle towards your torso while keeping the other handle stationary.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
Slowly return the handle to the starting position and repeat with the other side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever alternating narrow grip seated row is a machine-based exercise targeting the upper back, performed by alternately pulling each handle towards the torso while maintaining proper posture.

name: lever assisted chin-up
instructions: Adjust the leverage machine to your desired resistance level.
Kneel on the assistance pad and grip the handles with an underhand grip, about shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms fully extended, keeping your body straight.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the handles, leading with your chest.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the handles.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever assisted chin-up is a machine-based exercise that helps users perform chin-ups with assistance, making it easier to build strength in the lats, biceps, and forearms. It is ideal for those who are not yet able to perform unassisted chin-ups.

name: lever back extension
instructions: Adjust the machine to fit your body size and range of motion.
Sit on the machine with your upper back against the pad and your feet secured.
Cross your arms over your chest.
Engage your core and slowly lean forward, allowing your back to round slightly.
Pause for a moment at the bottom position, feeling a stretch in your lower back.
Using your back muscles, slowly push back against the pad to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever back extension is a machine-based exercise targeting the muscles of the lower back (spine extensors), with secondary emphasis on the glutes and hamstrings. It is performed by sitting on a leverage machine, securing the feet, and extending the back against resistance.

name: lever bent over row
instructions: Stand next to the loaded end of a barbell anchored to the floor, feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Grip the bar just inside the plate with both hands close together.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Pull the end of the barbell towards your torso, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever bent over row is a compound strength exercise targeting the upper back, performed with a barbell anchored at one end. It requires good posture, core stability, and proper technique to avoid injury.

name: lever bicep curl
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back against the pad.
Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and keep your elbows close to your sides.
Exhale and curl the handles upward, contracting your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever bicep curl is a machine-based exercise targeting the biceps, with secondary emphasis on the forearms. It is performed using a leverage machine, which provides guided resistance and stability, making it accessible for most users.

name: lever chest press
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back flat against the pad.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended, exhaling during the movement.
Pause briefly at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position, inhaling as you do so.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever chest press is a machine-based exercise that targets the pectoral muscles, with secondary emphasis on the triceps and shoulders. It is performed on a leverage machine, providing guided movement for safety and stability.

name: lever chest press
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back flat against the pad.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended, exhaling during the movement.
Pause briefly at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position, inhaling as you do so.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever chest press is a machine-based exercise targeting the pectoral muscles. It provides a controlled pressing movement, making it suitable for building chest strength with added support and stability from the machine.

name: lever deadlift
instructions: Load the machine and stand inside it with your feet hip-width apart, the handles at your sides.
Bend your hips and knees to lower yourself until you can grasp the handles with a neutral grip.
Keep your chest up, your back straight and your arms extended.
Drive through your heels to stand up, extending your hips and knees together.
Keep your shoulders from rounding throughout the lift.
At the top, stand tall and squeeze your glutes.
Lower the weight back down in a controlled manner by bending your hips and knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever deadlift is a standing machine exercise targeting the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the quadriceps and hamstrings. You lift a plate-loaded lever by its side handles, which guides the path and makes the pattern accessible to a wide range of users.

name: lever front pulldown
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your knees under the pads and your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Sit upright with your chest lifted and your shoulders back, maintaining a slight arch in your lower back.
Engage your lats and pull the handles down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly release the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever front pulldown is a machine-based exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi (lats) and is commonly used to build back strength and muscle mass. It involves pulling handles down towards the chest while seated, using a leverage machine.

name: lever gripless shrug
instructions: Adjust the shoulder pads to your height and stand under them with your feet hip-width apart.
Place your shoulders under the pads and let your arms hang, hands resting lightly on the bar without gripping.
Keeping your back straight, exhale and elevate your shoulders as high as possible.
Hold the contraction for a brief moment, then inhale and slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever gripless shrug is performed on a leverage machine to target the trapezius muscles by elevating the shoulders without gripping the handles. This isolates the traps and minimizes forearm involvement.

name: lever high row
instructions: Adjust the seat height and foot platform to a comfortable position.
Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the foot platform.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Pull the handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement, then slowly release the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever high row is a machine-based exercise targeting the upper back, with secondary emphasis on the biceps and rear deltoids. It is performed by sitting on a leverage machine, gripping the handles, and pulling them towards the body while keeping the chest against the pad.

name: lever kneeling leg curl
instructions: Adjust the machine to fit your body and select the desired weight.
Kneel on the machine with one knee on the pad, your forearms on the front support and the working ankle under the footpad.
Grasp the handles or the sides of the machine for stability.
Keeping your upper body stationary, exhale and curl the working leg up towards your glutes by flexing the knee.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your hamstrings.
Inhale and slowly lower the leg back to the starting position, fully extending the knee.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The lever kneeling leg curl is an isolation exercise targeting the hamstrings, performed one leg at a time on a leverage machine while kneeling. It primarily works the hamstrings and also engages the glutes as secondary muscles.

name: lever kneeling twist
instructions: Kneel on the rotating platform with your knees on the pads and your upper body upright, facing forward.
Grasp the fixed handles at chest height to keep your upper body still.
Keeping your core engaged, rotate your hips and knees to one side as far as comfortably possible while your chest stays facing forward.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat the rotation to the opposite side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever kneeling twist is an abdominal exercise performed on a leverage machine, targeting the abs with secondary emphasis on the obliques and lower back. The movement involves twisting the torso from side to side while kneeling, engaging the core muscles.

name: lever lateral raise
instructions: Adjust the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivot and sit with your back against the pad.
Place your upper arms against the pads and hold the handles with a neutral grip, elbows bent about 90 degrees.
Exhale and raise your arms out to the sides, leading with the elbows, until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever lateral raise is a machine-based exercise targeting the deltoid muscles of the shoulders. It involves raising the arms out to the sides against resistance, primarily working the lateral deltoids, with secondary emphasis on the traps and upper back. The machine provides stability, making it accessible for those with less experience.

name: lever leg extension
instructions: Adjust the seat height and backrest of the machine to fit your body.
Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet on the footpad.
Grasp the handles or sidebars for stability.
Extend your legs forward by straightening your knees, lifting the weight.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the weight back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever leg extension is an isolation exercise performed on a leverage machine to target the quadriceps. It involves extending the knees to lift a weight, primarily working the front of the thighs.

name: lever lying leg curl
instructions: Adjust the machine to fit your body and select the desired weight.
Lie face down on the machine with your legs straight and your heels against the padded lever.
Grasp the handles or the sides of the machine for stability.
Keeping your upper body stationary, exhale and curl your legs up as far as possible without lifting your hips off the pad.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your hamstrings.
Inhale and slowly lower the lever back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever lying leg curl is an isolation exercise targeting the hamstrings, performed on a leverage machine. It involves curling the legs upward against resistance while lying face down, emphasizing hamstring contraction and control.

name: lever military press
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back against the backrest.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Push the handles upward until your arms are fully extended, but do not lock your elbows.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the handles back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever military press is a shoulder exercise performed on a leverage machine, primarily targeting the deltoid muscles. It also engages the triceps and upper chest as secondary muscles. The machine provides stability, making it suitable for those developing strength and technique.

name: lever narrow grip seated row
instructions: Adjust the seat height and footrests to ensure proper form.
Sit on the machine with your feet flat on the footrests and your knees slightly bent.
Grasp the handles with a narrow grip, palms facing each other.
Keep your back straight and lean slightly forward.
Pull the handles towards your torso, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement.
Slowly release the handles and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever narrow grip seated row is a machine-based exercise targeting the upper back, with secondary emphasis on the biceps and forearms. It involves pulling handles towards the torso while seated, focusing on squeezing the shoulder blades together.

name: lever one arm bent over row
instructions: Anchor one end of a barbell on the floor, load the free end and stand beside it with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight, and grasp the bar just below the plate with one hand.
Let the bar hang with your arm fully extended.
Pull the end of the bar up towards the side of your torso, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blade at the top of the movement.
Lower the bar back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The lever one arm bent over row is a unilateral back exercise performed with a barbell anchored at one end (landmine). It targets the upper back and also works the biceps and forearms, rowing the loaded end of the bar with one arm from a stable bent-over position.

name: lever one arm shoulder press
instructions: Load the lever and stand facing it with your feet hip-width apart, close enough to hold the handle at shoulder height.
Grasp the lever handle with one hand, elbow bent and tucked below the handle.
Brace your core and press the lever up and forward along its path until your arm is fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the lever back to shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
description: The lever one arm shoulder press is a machine-based exercise targeting the deltoid muscles of the shoulder. It is performed one arm at a time, allowing for focused muscle engagement and unilateral strength development. The exercise also involves the triceps and upper back as secondary muscles.

name: lever overhand triceps dip
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles sit at about chest height and sit with your thighs secured under the roller pad.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, elbows bent and pointing back.
Push the handles down by extending your elbows, keeping your upper arms close to your sides.
Continue until your arms are fully extended beside your hips.
Pause for a moment, then let the handles rise slowly until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever overhand triceps dip is a machine-based exercise targeting the triceps, with secondary emphasis on the chest and shoulders. It involves lowering and raising the body using a leverage machine, which provides stability and controlled resistance.

name: lever preacher curl
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the leverage machine.
Place your upper arms on the pad and grip the handles with an underhand grip.
Keep your back straight and your elbows positioned on the pad.
Exhale and curl your forearms towards your upper arms, contracting your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever preacher curl is a strength training exercise performed on a leverage machine, primarily targeting the biceps with secondary activation of the forearms. It involves curling the handles upward while keeping the upper arms supported on a pad, which isolates the biceps and minimizes cheating.

name: lever reverse hyperextension
instructions: Adjust the machine to fit your body and lie face down with your torso on the pad and your hips at its rear edge.
Let your legs hang down off the back of the pad and hook your ankles under the roller pad.
Grasp the handles at the front of the machine to hold your upper body in place.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings to lift your legs upward until they are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever reverse hyperextension is a machine-based exercise targeting the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the hamstrings and lower back. It involves lying face down on a leverage machine and lifting the legs upward using the glutes and hamstrings.

name: lever seated calf raise
instructions: Sit on the machine and adjust the pad so it rests on your lower thighs with your knees bent about 90 degrees.
Place the balls of your feet on the footplate with your heels hanging off the edge.
Grasp the handles or the pad for stability.
Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever seated calf raise is a machine-based exercise that targets the calf muscles, particularly the gastrocnemius and soleus. It is performed while seated, using a leverage machine to provide resistance as you raise and lower your heels.

name: lever seated crunch (chest pad)
instructions: Adjust the seat height and chest pad position so the pad rests on your upper chest.
Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet hooked under the foot rollers.
Grasp the handles for stability.
Engage your abs and curl your torso forward and down, pushing the chest pad with you.
Pause for a moment at the maximum contraction, feeling the tension in your abs.
Slowly return to the upright starting position under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever seated crunch (chest pad) is an abdominal exercise performed on a leverage machine. It primarily targets the abs and also engages the obliques. The movement involves controlled flexion and extension of the torso against resistance, making it suitable for building core strength.

name: lever seated fly
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back against the pad.
Grasp the handles with a pronated grip and keep your elbows slightly bent.
Exhale and push the handles forward, bringing them together in front of your chest.
Pause for a moment, squeezing your chest muscles.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position, allowing your chest muscles to stretch.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever seated fly is a machine-based exercise targeting the pectoral muscles, performed by bringing the handles together in front of the chest while seated.

name: lever seated hip abduction
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your knees are at a 90-degree angle.
Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet on the footrests.
Place your hands on the side handles for stability.
Engage your abductors and slowly push your legs apart, away from the midline of your body.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly bring your legs back together to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever seated hip abduction is a machine-based exercise that targets the hip abductor muscles. It is performed while seated, pushing the legs apart against resistance provided by the machine.

name: lever seated hip adduction
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back against the backrest.
Place your feet on the footrests and grasp the handles for stability.
Engage your adductor muscles and slowly bring your legs together, squeezing your inner thighs.
Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever seated hip adduction is a machine-based exercise targeting the adductor muscles of the inner thighs. It is performed by bringing the legs together against resistance while seated.

name: lever seated leg curl
instructions: Adjust the machine to fit your body and sit on it with your back against the backrest and the thigh pad snug over your knees.
Rest the backs of your lower legs on the padded lever, just above your ankles, with your legs extended.
Grasp the handles on the sides of the machine for support.
Keeping your upper legs stationary, exhale and curl your legs down and back under the seat as far as possible.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your hamstrings.
Inhale and slowly let the lever return until your legs are extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever seated leg curl is a machine-based exercise that targets the hamstrings. It involves curling your lower legs against resistance while seated, isolating the hamstrings and minimizing involvement from other muscle groups.

name: lever seated leg raise crunch
instructions: Sit on the leverage machine with your back against the backrest and your feet on the footrests.
Grasp the handles or sidebars for stability.
Engage your abs and slowly raise your legs up towards your chest, curling your torso forward at the same time.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs and torso back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever seated leg raise crunch is an abdominal exercise performed on a leverage machine. It targets the abs and also works the hip flexors. The movement involves raising the legs and curling the torso forward simultaneously, providing a challenging core workout.

name: lever seated reverse fly (parallel grip)
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with a parallel grip, palms facing each other, and keep your arms slightly bent.
Exhale and squeeze your shoulder blades together as you pull the handles back and outward, away from your body.
Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever seated reverse fly (parallel grip) is a machine-based exercise targeting the rear deltoids, with secondary emphasis on the trapezius and rhomboids. It involves pulling the handles back and outward while seated, focusing on squeezing the shoulder blades together.

name: lever seated reverse fly
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and keep your arms slightly bent.
Exhale and squeeze your shoulder blades together as you pull the handles back and outward, away from your body.
Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever seated reverse fly is a machine-based exercise targeting the rear deltoids, with secondary emphasis on the trapezius and rhomboids. It is performed seated, using a leverage machine, which provides stability and helps isolate the target muscles.

name: lever shoulder press
instructions: Stand facing the loaded end of the lever with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the handles at shoulder height.
Squat down, keeping your chest up and the handles at your shoulders.
Drive through your feet to stand up and, as you rise, press the handles up and forward until your arms are fully extended without locking your elbows.
Pause for a moment at the top, then lower the handles back to your shoulders and sink into the next squat under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever shoulder press is a standing exercise on an anchored lever bar that targets the deltoids, with secondary emphasis on the triceps, upper chest and legs. You start from a squat and use the drive of the legs to press the lever up and forward along its fixed path.

name: lever shrug
instructions: Load the machine and stand inside it with your feet hip-width apart, the handles at your sides.
Grasp the handles with a neutral grip and stand up tall with your arms straight.
Keeping your back straight, lift your shoulders up towards your ears as high as possible.
Hold the contraction for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever shrug is a machine-based exercise targeting the trapezius muscles. It involves elevating the shoulders while keeping the arms straight, using a leverage machine for resistance.

name: lever standing calf raise
instructions: Adjust the machine to your height and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Place your shoulders under the pads and hold onto the handles for stability.
Raise your heels as high as possible by extending your ankles.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever standing calf raise is a strength exercise performed on a leverage machine, targeting the calves. It involves raising and lowering the heels while standing, using resistance provided by the machine.

name: lever t bar row
instructions: Load the lever and step onto the foot platform, straddling the bar with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips until your torso is inclined forward.
Grasp the handles with a neutral grip, palms facing each other, arms extended.
Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Pull the handles towards your torso, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever T bar row is a standing bent-over row on a T-bar lever, targeting the upper back with secondary emphasis on the biceps and forearms. The lever's fixed path lets you row heavy loads while holding a stable hip hinge.

name: lever triceps extension
instructions: Adjust the seat height so your upper arms rest flat on the arm pad in front of you, with your chest close to it.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and fully extend your arms along the pad.
