Keeping your upper arms on the pad, slowly let the handles come back towards your forehead by bending your elbows.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the handles back to the starting position by extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever triceps extension is an isolation exercise performed on a leverage machine to target the triceps. It involves extending the arms against resistance, focusing on triceps activation while minimizing shoulder involvement.

name: london bridge
instructions: Hang a rope from a high anchor point.
Stand facing the rope with your feet braced against a low bar or the floor in front of the anchor.
Grasp the rope with both hands, one above the other.
Walk your hands down the rope while leaning back until your body is low and your arms are extended, keeping your core engaged.
Climb back up hand over hand, squeezing your shoulder blades, until your body is upright.
Pause for a moment at the top, then walk your hands down the rope under control to the low position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The London Bridge is a bodyweight rope exercise for the upper back, biceps and grip. Facing a rope hanging from a high anchor with your feet braced, you climb hand over hand from a low lean-back position up to standing.

name: lying (side) quads stretch
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs straight.
Bend your top leg and grab your ankle or foot with your hand.
Gently pull your ankle or foot towards your glutes until you feel a stretch in your quads.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Release the stretch and repeat on the other side.
description: A static stretch performed lying on your side to target the quadriceps, often used to improve flexibility and reduce muscle tightness.

name: lying leg raise flat bench
instructions: Lie flat on a flat bench with your back pressed against it.
Place your hands under your glutes for support.
Keep your legs straight and together, and lift them up towards the ceiling.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lying leg raise flat bench is an abdominal exercise performed on a flat bench using only body weight. It primarily targets the abs and also engages the hip flexors. The movement involves lifting straight legs up towards the ceiling while lying flat, then lowering them back down under control.

name: march sit (wall)
instructions: Stand with your back against a wall and your feet hip-width apart.
Slowly slide your back down the wall until your knees are bent at a 90-degree angle.
Lift your right foot off the ground and bring your knee towards your chest.
Lower your right foot back down and lift your left foot off the ground, bringing your knee towards your chest.
Continue alternating between lifting your right and left foot for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The march sit (wall) is a lower body exercise performed with body weight, targeting the glutes and also engaging the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. It involves holding a wall sit position while alternately lifting each knee towards the chest, mimicking a marching motion.

name: mixed grip chin-up
instructions: Grab the pull-up bar with a mixed grip, one palm facing you and the other facing away, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your feet off the ground.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, switching which hand faces you between sets.
description: The mixed grip chin-up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the lats, with secondary emphasis on the biceps and forearms. It involves pulling your body up to a bar using a mixed grip, which challenges grip strength and upper body pulling power.

name: monster walk
instructions: Place a resistance band around your ankles.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly bend your knees.
Take a step to the side with your right foot, maintaining tension on the resistance band.
Follow with your left foot, stepping to the side to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The monster walk is a lower body exercise that targets the glutes and also works the hamstrings and quadriceps. It is typically performed with a resistance band around the ankles to increase intensity. The movement involves stepping side-to-side while maintaining tension in the band and a slight knee bend.

name: mountain climber
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Engage your core and bring your right knee towards your chest, then quickly switch and bring your left knee towards your chest.
Continue alternating legs in a running motion, keeping your hips low and your core engaged.
Maintain a steady pace and breathe evenly throughout the exercise.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Mountain climbers are a dynamic bodyweight exercise that targets the cardiovascular system while also engaging the core, shoulders, and triceps. The movement mimics a running motion in a plank position, making it effective for both cardio and muscular endurance.

name: muscle up
instructions: Start by hanging from gymnastic rings with a false grip (wrists over the rings) and your arms fully extended.
Engage your core and pull explosively until the rings reach your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
At the top of the pull, lean your chest forward over the rings and rotate your elbows back to transition into a dip position.
Press up until your arms are fully extended with your body supported above the rings.
Reverse the movement by slowly lowering yourself back down to the hanging position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The muscle up is a challenging bodyweight exercise that combines a pull-up with a dip, requiring significant upper body strength, coordination, and explosive power. It targets the lats primarily, with secondary engagement of the biceps, triceps, shoulders, and chest.

name: negative crunch
instructions: Lie back on a decline bench with your knees bent and your feet hooked under the foot rollers.
Cross your arms over your chest.
Engaging your abs, curl your upper body up off the bench until your torso is at about a 45-degree angle.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The negative crunch is an abdominal exercise focusing on the eccentric (lowering) phase of the crunch to increase core strength and control.

name: oblique crunches floor
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs stacked and your knees slightly bent.
Place your top hand behind your head and rest your bottom arm across your waist.
Engage your obliques and lift your upper shoulder and torso sideways towards your hip.
Pause for a moment, then lower your upper body back down to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: Oblique crunches on the floor target the abdominal muscles, especially the obliques, with a sideways crunch performed lying on your side. It uses only body weight and is suitable for most fitness levels.

name: olympic barbell hammer curl
instructions: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the bar by its parallel handles with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Let the bar hang at arm's length in front of your thighs.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to raise the barbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the barbell is at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Inhale and slowly begin to lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The olympic barbell hammer curl is a strength exercise targeting the biceps and forearms. It involves curling an Olympic barbell with a neutral grip, emphasizing both the biceps and brachialis muscles.

name: olympic barbell triceps extension
instructions: Sit upright on the end of a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor and hold the barbell with an overhand grip.
Raise the barbell above your head, fully extending your arms.
Keeping your upper arms close to your head, slowly lower the barbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The olympic barbell triceps extension is a strength exercise targeting the triceps, performed seated by holding an Olympic barbell overhead and lowering it behind the head before extending the arms back up.

name: one arm chin-up
instructions: Stand facing a pull-up bar with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Reach up and grab the bar with an underhand grip, with one hand gripping the bar and the other hand holding your wrist for support.
Hang from the bar with your arm fully extended, keeping your body straight and your core engaged.
Pull yourself up towards the bar by bending your elbow and squeezing your back muscles.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar, then slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms and repeat.
description: The one arm chin-up is a highly advanced bodyweight exercise that targets the latissimus dorsi (lats) and requires significant strength, coordination, and grip power. It is performed by pulling your body up to a bar using only one arm, with the other hand optionally supporting the wrist.

name: one arm dip
instructions: Sit beside a bench or chair with your legs extended in front of you.
Place one hand on the bench next to your hip, fingers pointing forward.
Lift your legs off the floor, keeping them straight, and reach your free arm forward for balance.
Bend your elbow and lower your body towards the ground, keeping your torso close to the bench.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your palm to straighten your arm and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and repeat with the other arm.
description: The one arm dip is a challenging bodyweight exercise that targets the triceps, with secondary emphasis on the chest and shoulders. It requires significant upper body strength, balance, and coordination, as you support your body weight with one arm while performing the dip motion.

name: one arm slam (with medicine ball)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the medicine ball with one hand in front of your waist.
Bend your knees slightly and engage your core.
Raise the medicine ball above your head, fully extending your arm.
Forcefully slam the medicine ball down to the ground, using your core and shoulders to generate power.
Catch the medicine ball on the bounce and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The one arm slam with a medicine ball is a dynamic exercise targeting the abs, shoulders, and back. It involves forcefully slamming a medicine ball to the ground with one arm, requiring core strength, power, and coordination.

name: otis up
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding a weight plate against your chest with both hands.
Brace your core and keep the plate close to your chest.
Sit all the way up while pressing the plate straight overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Pause at the top, then lower your torso back down while bringing the plate back to your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The Otis Up is a weighted sit-up that targets the abs, with the hip flexors and shoulders assisting. Holding a weight plate on the chest, you sit all the way up while pressing the plate overhead, then lower back down with control.

name: outside leg kick push-up
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
After pushing back up, rotate your hips and sweep one leg under your body and out to the opposite side, lifting the opposite hand off the floor as your chest turns open.
Bring the leg back under your body to the plank position and repeat the push-up, alternating legs with each repetition.
Continue alternating leg kicks and push-ups for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The outside leg kick push-up is a dynamic bodyweight exercise that combines a traditional push-up with a lateral leg kick, targeting the glutes and engaging the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. This movement challenges upper body strength, core stability, coordination, and lower body mobility.

name: overhead triceps stretch
instructions: Stand or sit upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend one arm overhead, bending at the elbow so that your hand reaches towards the opposite shoulder blade.
With your other hand, gently pull the elbow of the extended arm towards the opposite side of your head, feeling a stretch in your triceps.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then release.
Repeat on the other side.
description: The overhead triceps stretch is a static stretching exercise that targets the triceps and also stretches the shoulders. It is performed by extending one arm overhead, bending at the elbow, and using the opposite hand to gently pull the elbow for a deeper stretch.

name: power clean
instructions: Start with the barbell on the ground in front of you, with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend down and grip the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and chest up as you lift the barbell off the ground, extending your hips and knees.
As the barbell reaches your mid-thigh, explosively pull it upwards, shrugging your shoulders and pulling your elbows high and to the sides.
As the barbell reaches its highest point, quickly drop underneath it, rotating your elbows around and catching the barbell on your shoulders in a front squat position.
Stand up with the barbell, fully extending your hips and knees.
Lower the barbell back down to the starting position, keeping control of the weight throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The power clean is a compound Olympic weightlifting movement that involves lifting a barbell from the floor to the shoulders in one explosive motion. It targets the hamstrings, glutes, quadriceps, and calves, and requires significant strength, coordination, and technique.

name: pull-in (on stability ball)
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands on the floor under your shoulders and your shins resting on a stability ball.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to feet with your core braced.
Engage your abs and pull your knees towards your chest, rolling the ball forward.
Pause for a moment, then slowly extend your legs to roll the ball back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The pull-in on a stability ball is an abdominal exercise that also engages the hip flexors. From a plank with your shins on the ball, you tuck your knees toward your chest while keeping your body stable.

name: pull up (neutral grip)
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and your arms fully extended.
Engage your core and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Pull your body up towards the bar by bending your elbows and driving your elbows down towards your hips.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The neutral grip pull-up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi (lats) and also engaging the biceps and forearms. It is performed by hanging from a pull-up bar with palms facing each other, pulling the chin above the bar, and lowering back down with control.

name: pull-up
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with your palms facing away from you and your arms fully extended.
Engage your core and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Pull your body up towards the bar by bending your elbows and bringing your chest towards the bar.
Pause at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The pull-up is a bodyweight exercise that primarily targets the latissimus dorsi muscles of the back. It also engages the biceps and forearms as secondary muscles. The movement requires significant upper body strength, coordination, and control, making it a challenging exercise for many individuals.

name: push-up (bosu ball)
instructions: Place the bosu ball on the ground with the flat side facing up.
Position yourself in a push-up position with your hands on the outer edges of the bosu ball.
Engage your core and lower your body down towards the bosu ball by bending your elbows.
Push yourself back up to the starting position by extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The push-up (bosu ball) is a variation of the traditional push-up performed with hands on a BOSU ball, increasing instability and engaging more core and stabilizer muscles.

name: push-up (on stability ball)
instructions: Place the stability ball on the ground and position yourself facing down with your hands on the ball, shoulder-width apart.
Extend your legs straight out behind you, balancing on your toes.
Engage your core and lower your chest towards the ball by bending your elbows, keeping your body in a straight line.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The push-up on a stability ball is a challenging variation of the traditional push-up that requires additional balance and core engagement. By placing your hands on a stability ball, you increase the instability of the movement, forcing your chest, triceps, shoulders, and core to work harder to maintain proper form.

name: push-up (on stability ball)
instructions: Kneel in front of a stability ball and place your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Walk your hands forward and rest your shins or the tops of your feet on the ball, forming a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Push through your hands to straighten your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The push-up on a stability ball is a challenging variation of the traditional push-up that increases instability, requiring greater core engagement and balance. It primarily targets the pectorals, with significant involvement from the triceps, shoulders, and core.

name: push-up (wall) v. 2
instructions: Stand facing a wall, about arm's length away.
Place your hands on the wall at shoulder height, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step back with your feet, keeping them hip-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest towards the wall, keeping your body straight.
Pause for a moment, then push yourself back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The wall push-up is a beginner-friendly variation of the traditional push-up, performed standing and pressing against a wall. It primarily targets the pectorals, with secondary emphasis on the triceps and shoulders. This exercise is ideal for those new to strength training or individuals seeking a low-impact alternative to floor push-ups.

name: push-up (wall)
instructions: Stand facing a wall, about arm's length away.
Place your hands on the wall at shoulder height, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step back a few feet, keeping your body straight and your feet hip-width apart.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest towards the wall, keeping your body in a straight line.
Push back up to the starting position, straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The wall push-up is a beginner-friendly variation of the traditional push-up, performed standing and pressing against a wall. It primarily targets the pectorals, with secondary emphasis on the triceps and deltoids. This exercise is ideal for those new to strength training or individuals needing a low-impact alternative.

name: push-up close-grip off dumbbell
instructions: Stand one dumbbell upright on the floor and place both hands together on its top end.
Extend your legs behind you into a push-up position, keeping your body in a straight line.
Bend your elbows, keeping them close to your body, and lower your chest toward the dumbbell.
Push back up until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The close-grip push-up off a dumbbell is a push-up variation that targets the triceps, with additional emphasis on the chest and shoulders. Both hands rest on the top end of a single dumbbell standing upright on the floor, which narrows the base and challenges stability.

name: push-up inside leg kick
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
As you push back up, lift one leg off the ground and kick it out to the side, keeping it straight.
Lower your leg back down and repeat the push-up, then switch to the other leg.
Continue alternating leg kicks with each push-up repetition.
description: The push-up inside leg kick is a dynamic bodyweight exercise that combines a standard push-up with a lateral leg kick, targeting the glutes and engaging the core, quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. It requires coordination, balance, and strength.

name: push-up
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together.
Engage your core and lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your body in a straight line.
Pause for a moment when your chest is just above the ground, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The push-up is a classic bodyweight exercise that targets the pectoral muscles, triceps, deltoids, and core. It is performed by lowering and raising the body using the arms while maintaining a straight line from head to heels.

name: push-up medicine ball
instructions: Start in a high plank position with one hand on the medicine ball and the other hand on the floor, about shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your back straight.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch the ball to the other hand.
description: The medicine ball push-up is a variation of the traditional push-up performed with one hand on a medicine ball and the other on the floor. The uneven, unstable support increases the demand on the chest, triceps, shoulders, and core.

name: push-up to side plank
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your core engaged.
Push back up to the starting position.
Shift your weight onto your left hand and rotate your body to the right, lifting your right arm towards the ceiling.
Hold the side plank position for a few seconds, then return to the starting position.
Repeat the push-up and side plank on the opposite side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The push-up to side plank is a compound bodyweight exercise that combines a traditional push-up with a rotational movement into a side plank. This exercise targets the abs while also engaging the shoulders, chest, and triceps, and challenges core stability and balance.

name: raise single arm push-up
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, then push back up to straighten your arms.
At the top, shift your weight onto one hand and raise the other arm straight forward and up, keeping your hips square.
Return the hand to the floor and perform the next push-up, then raise the opposite arm.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The raise single arm push-up is a challenging bodyweight exercise that targets the pectorals while also engaging the triceps, shoulders, and core. After each push-up, one straight arm is lifted forward and up off the floor, forcing the core to resist rotation.

name: rear decline bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent.
Place your arms by your sides with your palms facing down.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings, and lift your hips off the ground until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Hold this position for a few seconds, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The rear decline bridge is a bodyweight exercise targeting the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the hamstrings and lower back. It involves lifting the hips off the ground while lying on your back, engaging the posterior chain.

name: rear deltoid stretch
instructions: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend your right arm across your chest, placing your left hand on your right elbow.
Gently pull your right arm towards your left shoulder, feeling a stretch in your right shoulder.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then release.
Repeat on the other side.
description: The rear deltoid stretch is a bodyweight exercise targeting the deltoid muscles, particularly the rear (posterior) delts. It also stretches the trapezius and rhomboids. This movement is commonly used to improve shoulder flexibility and relieve tension.

name: rear pull-up
instructions: Grab the pull-up bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The rear pull-up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi (lats) and also engaging the biceps and forearms. It involves pulling your body up to a bar with an overhand grip, focusing on back strength and control.

name: prone press-up
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your legs extended and your hands on the floor beside your chest.
Push through your hands and extend your elbows to lift your chest and upper torso, keeping your hips and legs on the floor.
Pause briefly with your arms straight, then bend your elbows to lower your chest back to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The reverse dip is a bodyweight exercise performed lying face down on the floor, pressing the upper body up with the arms while the hips stay down. It works the triceps, with the chest and shoulders assisting.

name: reverse grip machine lat pulldown
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your knees under the pads and your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Sit upright with your chest out and shoulders back, maintaining a slight arch in your lower back.
Pull the handles down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly release the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The reverse grip machine lat pulldown targets the latissimus dorsi using a leverage machine and an underhand grip, also engaging the biceps and forearms. It is performed seated with controlled movement, focusing on pulling the handles down to the chest and squeezing the shoulder blades together.

name: reverse grip pull-up
instructions: Grab the pull-up bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The reverse grip pull-up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the lats, performed by pulling the body up to a bar with an underhand grip. It also engages the biceps and forearms.

name: reverse hyper extension (on stability ball)
instructions: Lie face down on a stability ball with your hips resting on the ball and your legs extended straight behind you.
Place your hands on the ground in front of you for stability.
Engaging your glutes and hamstrings, lift your legs up towards the ceiling as high as you can.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The reverse hyper extension on a stability ball targets the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the hamstrings and lower back. It requires balance and core stability due to the use of the stability ball, making it more challenging than a floor-based version.

name: ring dips
instructions: Grip the rings and press up into a support position with your arms straight and the rings close to your sides.
Keeping the rings stable and your body upright, bend your elbows to lower yourself until your shoulders are slightly below your elbows.
Push through your palms to straighten your arms and return to the support position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Ring dips are a challenging bodyweight exercise performed on gymnastic rings, primarily targeting the triceps, with significant engagement of the chest and shoulders. The instability of the rings requires considerable strength, balance, and coordination.

name: rocky pull-up pulldown
instructions: Grab the pull-up bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms fully extended and your core engaged.
Pull yourself up, tilting your head slightly forward so the bar passes behind your head.
Continue until the back of your neck is close to the bar.
Lower yourself under control until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The rocky pull-up pulldown is a bodyweight exercise targeting the lats, with secondary emphasis on the biceps and forearms. It involves pulling the body up to a bar and lowering it under control, requiring significant upper body strength and coordination.

name: rope climb
instructions: Stand facing the rope with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grab the rope with both hands, palms facing towards you.
Bend your knees slightly and engage your core.
Begin pulling yourself up the rope by alternating hand-over-hand movements.
Use your legs to assist in the upward movement.
Continue climbing until you reach the desired height or the top of the rope.
To descend, reverse the hand-over-hand movement while controlling your descent.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The rope climb is a challenging upper body exercise that targets the upper back, forearms, biceps, and shoulders. It requires significant grip strength, coordination, and core stability, as well as the ability to use both the upper and lower body to ascend and descend a rope safely.

name: run (equipment)
instructions: Stand on the side rails of the treadmill and set a comfortable starting speed.
Step onto the moving belt and begin walking, then increase the speed to a run.
Run with an upright posture, landing under your hips and swinging your arms naturally.
Keep the pace for the planned time or distance.
Reduce the speed gradually to cool down before stepping off.
description: Running on a treadmill is a cardiovascular exercise that elevates the heart rate and improves overall endurance. The moving belt sets a steady pace, making it easy to control speed and duration.

name: run
instructions: Start by standing upright with your feet hip-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your upper body relaxed.
Begin jogging in place, lifting your knees up towards your chest and landing softly on the balls of your feet.
Maintain a steady pace and continue jogging for the desired duration or distance.
Remember to breathe deeply and maintain good posture throughout the exercise.
description: Running is a fundamental cardiovascular exercise that involves jogging or running in place or over a distance. It primarily targets the cardiovascular system and also engages the lower body muscles.

name: russian twist
instructions: Sit on the ground with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Lean back slightly while keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Hold your hands together in front of your chest or hold a weight if desired.
Keep your heels on the floor throughout the movement.
Twist your torso to the right, bringing your hands or weight towards the right side of your body.
Pause for a moment, then twist your torso to the left, bringing your hands or weight towards the left side of your body.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The Russian twist is a core exercise that targets the abdominal muscles and obliques. It involves rotating the torso from side to side while balancing on the sit bones, often with the feet lifted off the ground.

name: scapular pull-up
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip and your arms fully extended.
Keeping your elbows straight, pull your shoulder blades down and back to lift your body slightly.
Hold the contraction for a moment.
Relax your shoulder blades and return to a full hang under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The scapular pull-up is a bodyweight exercise that targets the trapezius muscles and helps improve scapular control and shoulder stability. It is performed by hanging from a pull-up bar and retracting the shoulder blades without bending the elbows.

name: seated leg raise
instructions: Sit on the edge of a flat bench and place your hands on the bench beside or behind your hips.
Lean your torso back slightly and lift your feet off the floor, knees bent.
Draw your knees toward your chest by contracting your abs.
Extend your legs forward without letting your feet touch the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The seated leg raise is an abdominal exercise performed while sitting on the edge of a bench. It targets the abs and hip flexors by drawing the bent knees toward the chest and extending them again under control.

name: seated overhead lat stretch
instructions: Sit upright on a chair with your feet flat on the floor.
Rest one hand on your thigh or the seat.
Raise the other arm straight overhead and reach up as high as you can until you feel a stretch along your lat and the side of your torso.
Hold the stretch for 15–30 seconds while breathing deeply.
Lower the arm and repeat on the other side.
description: A gentle stretch performed while seated on a chair, reaching one arm straight overhead to lengthen the lats and the side of the torso. It is suitable for improving flexibility and relieving tension in the upper body.

name: seated side crunch (wall)
instructions: Stand with your back against a wall and your feet about hip-width apart, a little in front of you.
Slide down the wall until your knees are bent about 90 degrees, as if sitting on a chair.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows out to the sides.
Keeping your back against the wall, bend your torso to one side, bringing your elbow toward your hip.
Return to the upright position.
Bend to the other side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions while holding the wall sit.
description: The seated side crunch (wall) is an abdominal exercise performed in a wall-sit position with your back against a wall. It targets the abs and obliques by bending the torso from side to side while the legs hold the squat.

name: self assisted inverse leg curl (on floor)
instructions: Kneel on a mat and anchor your ankles under a bench or a stable support.
Keep your body straight from knees to head and cross your arms over your chest.
Slowly lean forward from the knees, resisting the descent with your hamstrings.
Lower as far as you can control, then uncross your arms to catch yourself in a push-up position.
Push off the floor lightly to help start the return.
Pull yourself back to the upright kneeling position with your hamstrings.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The self assisted inverse leg curl (on floor) is a Nordic-style bodyweight exercise targeting the hamstrings. Kneeling with the ankles anchored, you lean forward with a straight body and catch yourself with your hands, using them to help push back up as needed.

name: self assisted inverse leg curl
instructions: Kneel on the pad of the station and secure your ankles under the foot rollers.
Keep your body straight from knees to head.
Slowly lean forward, resisting the descent with your hamstrings for as long as possible.
Catch yourself with your hands and push off lightly to help return to the upright position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The self assisted inverse leg curl is a Nordic-style bodyweight exercise targeting the hamstrings, with secondary emphasis on the glutes and calves. Kneeling with the ankles secured in a station, you lower your straight body forward and use your hands to assist the return.

name: shoulder tap push-up
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
As you push back up, lift your right hand off the ground and tap your left shoulder.
Return your right hand to the ground and repeat the push-up, this time lifting your left hand and tapping your right shoulder.
Continue alternating shoulder taps with each push-up repetition.
Maintain a stable core and avoid excessive hip rotation throughout the exercise.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The shoulder tap push-up is a bodyweight exercise that combines a standard push-up with an alternating shoulder tap at the top of each rep. This movement challenges the chest, triceps, and core while also requiring balance and coordination to stabilize the body during the shoulder tap.

name: side bridge v. 2
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs extended and stacked on top of each other.
Place your forearm on the ground directly below your shoulder, with your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the ground, creating a straight line from your head to your feet.
Hold this position for the desired amount of time.
Lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side.
description: The side bridge v. 2 is a core stability exercise performed on the floor using only body weight. It targets the abs, with secondary emphasis on the obliques and glutes. The movement involves holding a side plank position, which challenges core strength and stability.

name: side hip (on parallel bars)
instructions: Support yourself on the parallel bars or station with your forearms on the pads and your legs hanging.
Bend your knees and raise them up and diagonally toward one side, twisting slightly at the waist.
Lower your legs under control back to the hanging position.
Repeat the raise toward the opposite side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The side hip (on parallel bars) is a challenging core exercise that targets the abs, obliques, and hip flexors. Supported on the bars, you raise your bent knees diagonally toward one side and then the other.

name: side hip abduction
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs straight and stacked, propped up on your forearm.
Keep your hips stacked and your core engaged.
Lift your top leg straight up as high as you can without rotating your hips.
Pause briefly, then lower the leg under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: Side hip abduction is a bodyweight exercise performed lying on your side that targets the hip abductors, strengthening the outer thighs and hips. It also engages the glutes and is commonly used for strengthening, mobility, and rehabilitation.

name: side push neck stretch
instructions: Stand or sit up straight with your shoulders relaxed.
Tilt your head to the right, bringing your right ear towards your right shoulder.
Place your right hand on the left side of your head and gently apply pressure to increase the stretch.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds.
Repeat on the other side, tilting your head to the left and applying pressure with your left hand.
Repeat the stretch 2-3 times on each side.
description: The side push neck stretch is a gentle stretching exercise targeting the levator scapulae and other neck muscles. It helps improve flexibility and relieve tension in the neck and upper shoulders.

name: side push-up
instructions: Lie on your side with your knees bent and your legs stacked.
Keep your hips on the floor and your bottom shoulder relaxed.
Place your top hand on the floor in front of your chest, fingers pointing toward your head.
Push through your top hand and extend the elbow to lift your upper torso off the floor.
Slowly bend the elbow to lower your torso back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The side push-up is a bodyweight exercise that primarily targets the triceps, while also engaging the shoulders and chest. Lying on your side with your knees bent, you press your upper body up with the top hand placed on the floor in front of your chest.

name: side-to-side chin
instructions: Grab the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms fully extended and your core engaged.
Pull yourself up until your chin is above the bar.
At the top, shift your body toward one hand, bringing your chin close to it.
Shift across to the other hand, then lower yourself under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The side-to-side chin is a bodyweight exercise targeting the lats, performed by pulling yourself up to a bar and shifting your chin from one side to the other at the top of the movement. This variation increases the challenge to the lats and requires greater strength and control than a standard chin-up.

name: side wrist pull stretch
instructions: Stand or sit upright and extend one arm straight in front of you at shoulder height.
With the opposite hand, grasp the fingers of the extended hand.
Gently pull the hand back toward your body until you feel a stretch in the forearm.
Hold for 15–30 seconds while breathing normally.
Release and repeat with the other arm.
description: The side wrist pull stretch is a bodyweight exercise that targets the forearms and helps improve flexibility in the wrists and hands. It is performed by extending one arm in front of you and gently pulling the hand back toward the body with the opposite hand.

name: single arm push-up
instructions: Get into a push-up position with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart.
Place one hand on the floor under your chest and put the other hand behind your back.
Keeping your body straight, bend the elbow to lower your chest toward the floor.
Push through your hand to straighten the arm and return to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The single arm push-up is a challenging bodyweight exercise that targets the pectorals while also engaging the triceps, shoulders, and core. It requires significant strength, balance, and coordination, making it suitable for advanced practitioners.

name: single leg calf raise (on a dumbbell)
instructions: Place a dumbbell on the floor inside a Smith machine and stand with the ball of one foot on it, heel toward the floor.
Hold the Smith machine bar with your hand for balance and lift the other foot off the floor.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can.
Slowly lower your heel for a full stretch.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The single leg calf raise (on a dumbbell) is a lower leg exercise that targets the calves, with secondary emphasis on the ankles and feet. You stand on one leg with the ball of the foot on a dumbbell lying on the floor, holding a bar for balance, which increases the range of motion.

name: single leg platform slide
instructions: Lie on your back with both legs extended and your arms by your sides.
Keeping your heel in contact with the floor, slide one foot toward your glutes by bending the knee.
Pause when your knee is fully bent.
Slide the heel back out until the leg is straight again.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The single leg platform slide is a bodyweight exercise performed lying on your back, sliding one heel along the floor to bend and straighten the knee. It targets the hamstrings, with secondary emphasis on the glutes and quadriceps, and is often used for mobility and rehabilitation.

name: sit-up v. 2
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Place your hands across your chest or beside your head.
Engage your abs and curl your torso up off the floor until it is upright.
Slowly lower your torso back to the floor under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The sit-up v. 2 is a bodyweight abdominal exercise that targets the abs and also engages the hip flexors. It involves curling the torso up from a lying position until it is upright, then lowering back down.

name: sled 45° calf press
instructions: Adjust the sled machine to a 45-degree angle.
Place your feet on the sled platform with your toes pointing forward.
Push the sled platform away from you by extending your ankles and calves.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the sled platform back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The sled 45° calf press is a machine-based exercise that targets the calves by pressing a weighted sled away using the balls of your feet, focusing on ankle extension.

name: sled 45° leg press
instructions: Adjust the seat and footplate of the sled machine to a comfortable position.
Sit on the sled machine with your back against the backrest and your feet shoulder-width apart on the footplate.
Grip the handles on the sides of the seat for stability.
Push the footplate away from your body by extending your legs, keeping your heels on the footplate.
Continue pushing until your legs are almost fully extended, but without locking your knees.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the footplate back towards your body by bending your knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The sled 45° leg press is a compound lower body exercise performed on a sled machine. It primarily targets the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. The exercise involves pushing a weighted footplate away from the body while seated at a 45-degree angle, making it a popular choice for building lower body strength.

name: sled 45° leg wide press
instructions: Adjust the sled machine to a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the sled machine with your back against the pad and your feet on the foot platform.
Position your feet wider than shoulder-width apart.
Push against the foot platform to extend your legs and straighten your knees.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly bend your knees to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The sled 45° leg wide press is a compound lower body exercise performed on a sled machine set at a 45-degree angle. It targets the glutes primarily, with significant involvement from the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. The wide stance emphasizes the glutes and inner thighs more than a standard leg press.

name: sled closer hack squat
instructions: Load the sled and adjust the shoulder pads to your height.
Stand on the platform with your back against the pad and your feet close together in the middle of the platform.
Place your shoulders under the pads and grip the handles.
Release the safety handles and straighten your legs.
Bend your knees and hips to lower the sled until your thighs are about parallel to the platform.
Push through your feet to extend your legs and return to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The sled closer hack squat is a lower body exercise performed on a sled machine, primarily targeting the glutes while also engaging the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. It involves squatting with your back against a pad and feet on a platform, moving the weight by extending and flexing the knees and hips.

name: sled forward angled calf raise
instructions: Adjust the sled machine to a comfortable weight and position yourself on the machine with your toes on the platform and your heels hanging off.
Place your hands on the handles or the sides of the machine for support.
Engage your calves and slowly raise your heels as high as possible, pushing against the resistance of the sled.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The sled forward angled calf raise is a resistance exercise performed on a sled machine, targeting the calf muscles. The movement involves raising and lowering the heels while the toes remain on the platform, using the sled machine for added resistance.

name: sled hack squat
instructions: Adjust the sled machine to a comfortable position for your height.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform, toes slightly pointed outwards.
Hold onto the handles or bars for stability.
Lower your body by bending your knees and hips, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Pause for a moment, then push through your heels to raise your body back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The sled hack squat is a lower body strength exercise performed on a sled machine. It primarily targets the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. The movement involves squatting down with the support of the sled machine, which helps guide the motion and provides stability.

name: sled lying squat
instructions: Adjust the sled machine to a comfortable weight.
Lie on your back on the sled machine with your feet on the footplate.
Position your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly angled outwards.
Grip the handles of the sled machine for stability.
Engage your glutes and core muscles.
Push through your heels and extend your legs to lift the sled.
Lower the sled back down by bending your knees and hips.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The sled lying squat is a lower body exercise performed on a sled machine, targeting the glutes as the primary muscle group. It also engages the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. The movement involves lying on your back, pushing the sled upward with your legs, and then lowering it back down in a controlled manner.

name: smith back shrug
instructions: Set the Smith bar at about mid-thigh height.
Stand with your back to the bar and grip it behind you with your hands about shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar and let it hang at arm's length behind your thighs, standing tall.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as you can.
Pause and squeeze your traps, then lower your shoulders under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith back shrug is a strength exercise targeting the trapezius muscles, performed using a smith machine. It involves lifting the shoulders straight up towards the ears while holding a barbell, focusing on squeezing the traps at the top of the movement.

name: smith behind neck press
instructions: Place a bench inside the Smith machine and set the bar just above head height when seated.
Sit on the bench with your back upright and your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar and lower it behind your head to the base of your neck.
Press the bar straight up until your arms are extended.
Pause at the top.
Lower the bar under control behind your neck.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith behind neck press is a seated shoulder exercise performed on a smith machine, targeting the deltoids with secondary emphasis on the triceps and upper back. Seated on a bench, you press the bar from behind the neck to overhead, which requires good shoulder mobility and stability.

name: smith bench press
instructions: Adjust the height of the smith machine bar to chest level.
Lie flat on the bench with your feet firmly planted on the ground.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar and lower it towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Pause for a moment when the bar touches your chest.
Push the bar back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith bench press is a chest exercise performed on a smith machine, which provides a guided bar path for pressing movements. It primarily targets the pectorals, with secondary emphasis on the triceps and shoulders. The smith machine offers additional stability compared to a free-weight bench press, making it accessible for those with less experience or those seeking a safer alternative to heavy pressing.

name: smith bent knee good morning
instructions: Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward.
Place the barbell across your upper back, resting it on your traps.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Lower your torso until it is parallel to the ground, feeling a stretch in your hamstrings.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings to raise your torso back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith bent knee good morning is a lower body exercise performed on a Smith machine. It primarily targets the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the hamstrings and lower back. The movement involves hinging at the hips with a slight knee bend, lowering the torso while keeping the back straight, and then returning to the starting position.

name: smith chair squat
instructions: Adjust the height of the smith machine bar to a comfortable position.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
Place the barbell across your upper back, resting it on your traps.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you slowly lower your body by bending your knees and hips.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith chair squat is a lower body exercise performed using a smith machine. It primarily targets the quadriceps, with secondary emphasis on the glutes, hamstrings, and calves. The guided bar path of the smith machine provides stability, making it suitable for those developing squat technique or seeking a safer alternative to free-weight squats.

name: smith close-grip bench press
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the barbell with a close grip, slightly narrower than shoulder-width apart.
Lower the barbell towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith close-grip bench press is a compound exercise performed on a smith machine, targeting the triceps with secondary emphasis on the chest and shoulders. It involves pressing a barbell with a close grip, which increases triceps activation.

name: smith deadlift
instructions: Set up the smith machine with the bar at hip height.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Bend at the hips and knees, keeping your back straight and chest up, and grip the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and lift the bar by extending your hips and knees, keeping the bar close to your body.
Stand up straight, fully extending your hips and knees.
Lower the bar back down by bending at the hips and knees, maintaining control and keeping your back straight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith deadlift is a compound lower body exercise performed using a smith machine. It primarily targets the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the hamstrings, quadriceps, and lower back. The smith machine provides a guided bar path, which can help with stability and form for those learning the deadlift movement.

name: smith decline bench press
instructions: Adjust the decline bench to the desired angle.
Lie down on the bench with your feet secured under the foot pads.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith decline bench press is a chest exercise performed on a decline bench using a smith machine. It primarily targets the pectoral muscles, with secondary emphasis on the triceps and shoulders. The smith machine provides guided movement, making it safer and more stable than a free-weight decline bench press.

name: smith decline reverse-grip press
instructions: Adjust the smith machine to a decline position.
Lie down on the bench with your feet secured under the foot pads.
Grasp the barbell with a reverse grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith decline reverse-grip press is a chest exercise performed on a smith machine in a decline position, using a reverse (underhand) grip to target the lower pectorals and engage the triceps and shoulders.

name: smith hack squat
instructions: Set the Smith bar at about knee height.
Stand with your back to the bar and your feet hip-width apart.
Squat down and grip the bar behind you with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Stand up to unrack it, holding the bar at arm's length behind your thighs.
Keeping your chest up, bend your knees and hips to lower until the bar nears the back of your calves.
Push through your feet to stand back up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith hack squat is a lower body exercise performed on a smith machine with the bar held behind the legs at arm's length. It targets the glutes and quadriceps, with secondary emphasis on the hamstrings and calves.

name: smith hip raise
instructions: Set the Smith bar at a height you can reach with your feet while lying on your back underneath it.
Lie on your back with your hips under the bar and your arms on the floor by your sides.
Raise your legs vertically, place the soles of your feet against the bar and unrack it.
Contract your abs to lift your hips off the floor, pushing the bar straight up with your feet.
Lower your hips back to the floor under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith hip raise is an exercise performed lying under a smith machine that primarily targets the abdominal muscles. With your legs vertical and the soles of your feet against the bar, you push it upward by lifting your hips off the floor.

name: smith incline bench press
instructions: Adjust the bench to a 30-45 degree incline.
Sit on the bench with your back flat against the pad and feet firmly on the ground.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your upper chest, keeping your elbows slightly tucked in.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith incline bench press is a chest exercise performed on a smith machine with the bench set at a 30-45 degree incline. It primarily targets the upper pectorals, with secondary emphasis on the shoulders and triceps. The smith machine provides stability, making it accessible for those with less experience, but still requires proper form and control.

name: smith incline reverse-grip press
instructions: Set an incline bench inside the Smith machine at 30–45 degrees.
Lie back on the bench with your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar with an underhand (reverse) grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar and hold it above your chest with your arms extended.
Lower the bar under control to your upper chest.
Press the bar back up until your arms are extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith incline reverse-grip press is a chest exercise performed on a smith machine with an incline bench. It targets the pectoral muscles using a reverse (underhand) grip, which also engages the triceps and shoulders. The smith machine provides stability, but the reverse grip and incline angle require good coordination and some experience.

name: smith incline shoulder raises
instructions: Set an incline bench inside the Smith machine.
Lie back on the bench with your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip about shoulder-width apart and unrack it with your arms extended above your chest.
Keeping your elbows locked, push the bar up by moving your shoulder blades forward and apart.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower the bar a few centimeters by squeezing your shoulder blades together, without bending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Smith incline shoulder raises target the serratus anterior and are performed lying on an incline bench in a smith machine. Holding the bar with straight arms, you push it up a few centimeters by spreading the shoulder blades and lower it by squeezing them together.

name: smith leg press
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor under the Smith machine, with your hips roughly under the bar.
Raise your legs and place the soles of your feet on the bar, about hip-width apart.
Unrack the bar and press it up until your legs are almost straight.
Bend your knees to lower the bar toward your chest under control.
Stop when your knees are bent about 90 degrees.
Press the bar back up by extending your knees and hips, without locking your knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then re-rack the bar.
description: The smith leg press is a lower body exercise performed lying on your back under a smith machine, pressing the bar up with the soles of your feet. It targets the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves.

name: smith narrow row
instructions: Set the Smith bar at about knee height and grip it with an overhand grip narrower than shoulder-width.
Unrack the bar, then hinge at the hips with your knees slightly bent until your torso is close to parallel with the floor, arms extended.
Pull the bar toward your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your body and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower the bar under control until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith narrow row is a machine-based rowing exercise targeting the upper back, performed with a narrow grip to emphasize the upper back muscles and rear deltoids. It is performed on a Smith machine, which provides guided movement for added stability.

name: smith rear delt row
instructions: Set the Smith bar at about knee height and grip it with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack the bar, then hinge at the hips with your knees slightly bent until your torso is close to parallel with the floor, arms extended.
Pull the bar toward your upper chest with your elbows flared out to the sides, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower the bar under control until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith rear delt row is a standing bent-over row on a smith machine targeting the rear deltoids, with secondary emphasis on the trapezius, rhomboids, and biceps. A wide grip with flared elbows shifts the work toward the rear delts.

name: smith reverse calf raises
instructions: Adjust the smith machine bar to a height just below your shoulders.
Step under the bar, rest it across your upper back and grip it with both hands.
Place the balls of your feet on the edge of a step or platform, with your heels hanging off, and unrack the bar.
Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Raise your heels as high as possible, lifting your body weight onto the balls of your feet.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith reverse calf raises is a lower leg exercise performed on a smith machine, primarily targeting the calves and secondarily engaging the hamstrings. The movement involves raising and lowering the heels while standing on a step with the bar across the upper back.

name: smith reverse-grip press
instructions: Place a flat bench inside the Smith machine so the bar lines up with your lower chest.
Lie on the bench with your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar with an underhand (reverse) grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar and hold it above your chest with your arms extended.
Lower the bar under control to your lower chest.
Pause briefly.
Press the bar back up until your arms are extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith reverse-grip press is a chest exercise performed on a smith machine using a reverse (underhand) grip. This variation targets the upper chest and also engages the triceps and shoulders. The smith machine provides stability, making it suitable for those looking to focus on form and muscle activation.

name: smith seated shoulder press
instructions: Place a bench with a backrest inside the Smith machine.
Sit on the bench with your back against the backrest and your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar and lower it to the front of your shoulders.
Press the bar straight up until your arms are extended.
Lower the bar under control back to shoulder level.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith seated shoulder press is a machine-based exercise targeting the deltoid muscles of the shoulders. It provides stability and support, making it suitable for those looking to build shoulder strength with reduced risk of losing balance. The movement also engages the triceps and upper back as secondary muscles.

name: smith shoulder press
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the smith machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the bar off the rack and position it at shoulder level, with your elbows bent and palms facing forward.
Press the bar upward until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the bar back down to shoulder level.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith shoulder press is a compound exercise performed on a smith machine that targets the deltoid muscles of the shoulders. It provides stability for the lifter, making it easier to focus on pressing strength and muscle development.

name: smith shrug
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your arms straight and your shoulders relaxed.
Lift your shoulders up towards your ears, squeezing your traps at the top.
Hold for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith shrug is an exercise performed on a Smith machine to target the trapezius muscles. It involves lifting the shoulders towards the ears while holding a barbell, focusing on squeezing the traps at the top of the movement.

name: smith single leg split squat
instructions: Place a bench about two feet behind the Smith machine.
Position the bar across your upper back and grip it with both hands.
Step forward with one foot and rest the top of your rear foot on the bench behind you.
Unrack the bar and lower your body by bending your front knee until your thigh is about parallel to the floor.
Push through your front heel to return to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The smith single leg split squat is a lower body exercise performed using a smith machine. It targets the quadriceps while also engaging the glutes and hamstrings. The exercise requires balance and unilateral strength, as one leg is elevated behind you on a bench or step.

name: smith sprint lunge
instructions: Position the Smith bar across your upper back and grip it with both hands.
Unrack the bar and step into a split stance, one foot forward and the other back on the ball of the foot.
Keep your torso upright and your core engaged.
Bend both knees to lower your rear knee toward the floor.
Stop just before the knee touches the floor, with your front thigh about parallel to it.
Drive through your front foot to rise back up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The smith sprint lunge is a lower body exercise performed in a smith machine with the bar across the upper back. It targets the glutes primarily, with secondary emphasis on the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves, as you lower the rear knee toward the floor from a split stance and drive back up.

name: smith squat
instructions: Set up the smith machine with the barbell at an appropriate height for your squat.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
Position yourself under the barbell, resting it on your upper traps and shoulders.
Grip the barbell with a wide grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and unrack the barbell, stepping back to clear the rack.
Keeping your chest up and back straight, initiate the squat by bending at the hips and knees.
Lower your body until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then drive through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith squat is a lower body exercise performed using a smith machine. It primarily targets the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. The guided bar path of the smith machine provides stability, making it suitable for those learning proper squat form or looking to focus on muscle activation without balancing a free barbell.

name: smith standing back wrist curl
instructions: Set the Smith bar at about mid-thigh height.
Stand with your back to the bar and grip it behind you with your palms facing back, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar and let it hang at arm's length behind your thighs.
Keeping your arms straight, curl your wrists to lift the bar up.
Pause briefly, then lower the bar under control by relaxing your wrists.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith standing back wrist curl is an isolation exercise targeting the forearms, performed using a smith machine. It involves holding the bar behind your thighs and curling the wrists upward, focusing on forearm and grip strength.

name: smith standing behind head military press
instructions: Adjust the seat height of the smith machine so that the bar is at shoulder level.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the bar off the rack and step back, maintaining a stable stance.
Position the bar behind your head, resting on your upper traps.
Keep your core engaged and your chest lifted throughout the exercise.
Press the bar overhead by extending your arms, fully straightening them.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the bar back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith standing behind head military press is a shoulder exercise performed using a smith machine. The movement targets the deltoids and involves pressing a barbell from behind the head to overhead while standing.

name: smith standing leg calf raise
instructions: Set the Smith bar at about hip height.
Stand close to the bar with your feet hip-width apart and grip it with your hands about shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar and hold it at arm's length at hip level, standing tall.
Raise your heels as high as you can, coming onto your toes.
Slowly lower your heels back to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith standing leg calf raise is a lower leg exercise performed using a smith machine. It primarily targets the calves, with secondary emphasis on the hamstrings and glutes. The movement involves raising the heels to stand on the toes while holding the bar at arm's length, then lowering back down.

name: smith standing military press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the barbell off the rack and bring it down to shoulder level, with your palms facing forward.
Press the barbell upward until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to shoulder level.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The Smith standing military press is a compound exercise targeting the deltoid muscles of the shoulders, performed using a Smith machine for added stability. It also engages the triceps and upper back as secondary muscles. The fixed bar path of the Smith machine can make the movement more accessible for those learning the overhead press, but it still requires good shoulder mobility and core stability.

name: smith upright row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing the smith machine.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the barbell up towards your chin, leading with your elbows.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith upright row is a shoulder exercise performed on a smith machine, targeting the deltoids and also engaging the traps and biceps. It involves pulling a barbell upwards towards the chin while keeping the elbows higher than the wrists.

name: snatch pull
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the barbell over your midfoot.
Squat down and grip the bar with a wide (snatch) overhand grip, back flat and chest up.
Drive through your legs to lift the bar off the floor, keeping it close to your body.
As the bar passes your knees, extend your hips and knees explosively until you stand tall with the bar at your hips.
Finish the pull with a shrug of the shoulders, keeping your arms straight.
Lower the bar under control to the floor and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The snatch pull is a compound Olympic weightlifting movement that develops explosive power and strength in the lower body, particularly targeting the quads, hamstrings, and glutes. It requires coordination, balance, and proper technique to perform safely and effectively.

name: spell caster
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand beside one hip.
Rotate your torso and sweep both dumbbells across your body and up to shoulder height on the opposite side.
Bring the dumbbells down beside the other hip.
Sweep them back across and up toward the starting side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The spell caster is a rotational core exercise performed with two dumbbells, targeting the abs and obliques. Standing tall, you rotate your torso and sweep the dumbbells from one hip across your body to shoulder height, alternating sides.

name: spider crawl push up
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together.
Bring your right knee towards your right elbow, keeping it off the ground.
As you bring your right knee back, simultaneously lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows.
Push back up to the starting position and repeat with your left knee towards your left elbow.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The spider crawl push up is a challenging bodyweight exercise that combines a push-up with a dynamic knee drive, targeting the glutes, core, chest, and shoulders. It requires coordination, strength, and stability.
