name: squat jerk
instructions: Rack the barbell on the front of your shoulders with your feet hip-width apart.
Dip by bending your knees slightly, keeping your torso upright.
Drive explosively through your legs to propel the bar upward.
Push yourself under the bar, widening your feet and dropping into a deep squat as you lock your arms overhead.
Stabilize the bar overhead at the bottom of the squat.
Stand up with the bar overhead.
Lower the bar to your shoulders and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The squat jerk is an advanced Olympic weightlifting movement that combines a squat and a jerk, requiring explosive power, coordination, and balance. It targets the quads primarily, with significant involvement from the glutes, hamstrings, calves, and core.

name: standing behind neck press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the barbell behind your neck with an overhand grip.
Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Press the barbell overhead by extending your arms, fully extending your elbows.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The standing behind neck press is a barbell exercise targeting the deltoids, performed by pressing a barbell from behind the neck to overhead while standing. It also engages the triceps and upper back.

name: standing lateral stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Place one hand behind your head and let the other arm hang by your side.
Bend your torso sideways toward the hanging arm, sliding that hand down your leg.
Hold the stretch for 15–30 seconds, feeling it along the opposite side of your torso.
Return to the upright position.
Switch arms and repeat on the other side.
description: The standing lateral stretch is a bodyweight exercise that stretches the sides of the torso and the lats, also engaging the obliques. It is performed standing with one hand behind the head and the other arm hanging, bending the torso toward the hanging arm.

name: standing single leg curl
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your hips.
Shift your weight onto your left leg and lift your right foot off the ground, bending your knee.
Slowly curl your right heel towards your glutes, squeezing your hamstring.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your right foot back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The standing single leg curl is a bodyweight exercise targeting the hamstrings and glutes. It involves balancing on one leg while curling the opposite heel toward the glutes, emphasizing hamstring activation and single-leg stability.

name: standing wheel rollerout
instructions: Start by standing tall with your feet shoulder-width apart and the wheel roller in front of you.
Bend at your waist and slowly roll the wheel forward, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Continue rolling forward until you feel a stretch in your abs and your body is extended as far as possible.
Pause for a moment, then slowly roll the wheel back towards your body, returning to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The standing wheel rollout is an advanced core exercise that primarily targets the abdominal muscles, while also engaging the lower back and shoulders. It requires significant core strength, balance, and control to perform safely and effectively.

name: stationary bike walk
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position on the stationary bike to ensure proper alignment.
Place your feet on the pedals and secure them with the straps if available.
Start pedaling at a comfortable pace, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Maintain a steady rhythm and increase the resistance level if desired.
Continue pedaling for the desired duration of your cardio workout.
Cool down by gradually reducing your pace and resistance level.
Stretch your leg muscles after the workout to prevent tightness and promote recovery.
description: The stationary bike walk is a cardiovascular exercise performed on a leverage machine (stationary bike). It primarily targets the cardiovascular system and also engages the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. The exercise involves pedaling at a steady pace, with the option to adjust resistance for increased intensity.

name: superman push-up
instructions: Lie face down with your legs extended and your arms stretched forward overhead, hands on the floor.
Brace your core and glutes so your body stays rigid.
Press through your hands to lift your whole body off the floor, keeping it in a straight line.
Hold briefly at the top.
Lower yourself back to the floor under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The superman push-up is a challenging bodyweight exercise that targets the pectorals while also engaging the core and shoulders. Starting face down with your arms stretched far overhead, you push your whole body off the floor, which demands great strength and core stability.

name: suspended abdominal fallout
instructions: Attach a suspension trainer to a high anchor point and adjust the straps to waist height.
Stand facing away from the anchor point and hold the handles with your arms extended in front of you.
Lean forward at the waist, keeping your body straight and your core engaged.
Lower your body as far as you can while maintaining control and tension in your abs.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly raise your body back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The suspended abdominal fallout is a challenging core exercise performed with a suspension trainer. It targets the abs and also engages the obliques and hip flexors. The movement requires significant core strength, stability, and control to maintain proper form while leaning forward and returning to the starting position.

name: suspended push-up
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer so the handles hang a few centimeters above the floor.
Grip the handles and get into a push-up position, hands under your shoulders and legs extended behind you.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels and engage your core.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the handles, keeping them stable.
Push back up until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The suspended push-up is a challenging variation of the traditional push-up performed using a suspension trainer. This exercise increases instability, requiring greater core engagement and upper body strength.

name: suspended reverse crunch
instructions: Place your feet in the foot cradles of the suspension trainer and get into a push-up position with your hands under your shoulders.
Keep your body in a straight line and engage your core.
Draw your knees toward your chest, then extend your legs back to the plank position under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The suspended reverse crunch is an advanced core exercise performed in a plank position with your feet in the straps of a suspension trainer, tucking the knees toward the chest. It targets the abdominal muscles and hip flexors.

name: suspended row
instructions: Set up a suspension trainer at an appropriate height.
Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing each other.
Lean back, keeping your body straight and your heels on the ground.
Pull your chest towards the handles, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The suspended row is a bodyweight exercise performed using a suspension trainer. It targets the upper back and also engages the biceps and shoulders. The movement requires pulling your chest towards the handles while maintaining a straight body position, making it effective for building upper body strength and stability.

name: suspended split squat
instructions: Stand facing away from the suspension trainer and place the top of one foot in the foot cradle behind you.
Hop forward until you are in a split-squat stance, with your rear leg extended behind you.
Bend your front knee and lower your body until your rear knee is close to the floor.
Push through your front heel to return to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The suspended split squat is a lower body exercise that targets the quads, with secondary emphasis on the glutes, hamstrings, and calves. It is performed using body weight and a suspension trainer, requiring balance, strength, and coordination.

name: trap bar deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and the trap bar on the ground in front of you.
Bend at the hips and knees to lower yourself down and grip the handles of the trap bar with an overhand grip.
Keep your back straight and chest up as you begin to lift the trap bar off the ground by extending your hips and knees.
As you lift, focus on driving through your heels and squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Lower the trap bar back down to the ground by bending at the hips and knees, keeping your back straight throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The trap bar deadlift is a compound lower body exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, quadriceps, and lower back. It is performed using a trap bar, which allows for a more upright torso and can be easier on the lower back compared to a conventional barbell deadlift.

name: triceps dip (bench leg)
instructions: Place two benches parallel, about a leg's length apart.
Sit on the edge of one bench with your hands next to your hips and rest your heels on the other bench, legs extended.
Slide your hips off the bench and bend your elbows to lower your body until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Push through your palms to straighten your arms and return to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The triceps dip (bench leg) is a bodyweight exercise targeting the triceps, with the chest and shoulders as secondary muscles. You lower and raise your body with your hands on one bench and your legs extended with the heels on a second bench.

name: triceps dip (between benches)
instructions: Place two benches parallel to each other, slightly wider than your hips.
Stand between them, place one hand on each bench beside your hips and extend your legs in front of you with your heels on the floor.
Bend your elbows to lower your body between the benches until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Push through your palms to straighten your arms and lift your body back up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The triceps dip (between benches) is a bodyweight exercise targeting the triceps, performed with one hand on each of two parallel benches and the legs extended on the floor. You lower and raise your body between the benches.

name: triceps dip
instructions: Grip the parallel bars and press yourself up until your arms are straight, bending your knees behind you.
Keep your torso upright and your elbows close to your body.
Bend your elbows to lower your body until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Push through your palms to straighten your arms and return to the top.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The triceps dip is a bodyweight exercise that targets the triceps and also engages the chest and shoulders. It is performed on parallel bars, lowering and raising the body with an upright torso.

name: triceps dips floor
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and your feet flat.
Place your hands on the floor behind your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Straighten your arms to lift your hips off the floor.
Bend your elbows to lower your hips toward the floor without letting them touch it.
Extend your elbows to lift your hips back up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: A bodyweight exercise targeting the triceps, performed sitting on the floor with the hands behind the hips and the knees bent. Extending the elbows lifts the hips off the floor, with the chest and shoulders as secondary muscles.

name: triceps press
instructions: Set a Smith machine bar at about chest height and grip it with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Step your feet back so your body leans forward in a straight line, arms extended.
Bend your elbows to lower your head under the bar, keeping your elbows pointing forward.
Extend your elbows to push your body back to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The triceps press is a bodyweight exercise targeting the triceps, with secondary emphasis on the shoulders. Leaning on a bar set at about chest height, you bend your elbows to bring your head under the bar and extend them to push your body back up.

name: cross-body shoulder stretch
instructions: Stand or sit upright with your shoulders relaxed.
Bring one arm straight across your chest at shoulder height.
Hook the opposite hand or forearm over the arm, just above the elbow.
Gently pull the arm toward your chest until you feel a stretch in the back of the shoulder, and hold for 15–30 seconds.
Release and repeat with the other arm.
description: A static stretch for the back of the shoulder and upper arm, performed by bringing one straight arm across the chest and gently pulling it closer with the opposite arm.

name: twin handle parallel grip lat pulldown
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself facing the cable machine.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Sit down and position your thighs under the thigh pads, keeping your feet flat on the floor.
Lean back slightly and keep your chest up, maintaining a neutral spine.
Pull the handles down towards your upper chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, feeling the contraction in your lats.
Slowly release the handles and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The twin handle parallel grip lat pulldown is a cable machine exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi, with secondary emphasis on the biceps, rhomboids, and rear deltoids. It involves pulling parallel handles down towards the chest while seated, focusing on squeezing the shoulder blades together.

name: vertical leg raise (on parallel bars)
instructions: Place your forearms on the pads of the station, grip the handles and rest your back against the backrest.
Let your legs hang straight down.
Bend your knees and raise them until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Lower your legs under control back to the hanging position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The vertical leg raise (on parallel bars) is an abdominal exercise performed with your forearms on the pads and your back against the backrest of a knee-raise station. Raising the bent knees to hip height targets the abs and hip flexors.

name: weighted bench dip
instructions: Place two benches parallel, about a leg's length apart.
Sit on the edge of one bench with your hands beside your hips and rest your heels on the other bench, legs extended.
Place a weight plate on your thighs, then slide your hips off the bench.
Bend your elbows to lower your body until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, then push back up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted bench dip is an upper body exercise that targets the triceps, with secondary emphasis on the chest and shoulders. You lower and raise your body with your hands on one bench, your heels on another and a weight plate on your thighs for added resistance.

name: weighted crunch
instructions: Lie on your back and raise your legs in the air, knees slightly bent.
Hold a weight plate with both hands and extend your arms straight toward the ceiling.
Engage your abs and curl your shoulders off the floor, pushing the plate up toward your feet.
Lower your shoulders back down under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted crunch is an abdominal exercise that adds resistance to strengthen the abs and obliques. It is performed lying on your back with your legs raised, holding a weight plate with your arms extended toward the ceiling, and curling your upper body upward.

name: weighted donkey calf raise
instructions: Stand facing a bench with your feet hip-width apart and bend at the hips until your torso is about parallel to the floor, hands on the bench.
Have a partner sit on your hips or lower back.
Keeping your knees almost straight, raise your heels as high as you can.
Slowly lower your heels back to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted donkey calf raise is a calf exercise performed bent over at the hips with your hands on a bench while a partner sits on your lower back for added load. It targets the calves, with the hamstrings and glutes working as stabilizers.

name: weighted front raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate with both hands in front of your thighs.
Keeping your arms straight, raise the plate in front of you to shoulder height.
Pause briefly, then lower it under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted front raise is a shoulder exercise that targets the deltoids by lifting a weight plate held with both hands in front of the body. The movement requires control and proper form to avoid swinging or using momentum.

name: weighted hyperextension (on stability ball)
instructions: Lie face down on a stability ball with the ball under your hips and your legs extended behind you, toes on the floor.
Hold a weight plate against your chest.
Lower your upper body over the ball.
Extend your back to lift your chest until your body forms a straight line.
Lower back down under control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted hyperextension on a stability ball targets the spinal erectors and is performed lying face down on a stability ball with your legs extended and toes on the floor, extending the back while holding a weight at your chest. It also engages the glutes and hamstrings.

name: weighted overhead crunch (on stability ball)
instructions: Lie with your back on a stability ball, feet flat on the floor and knees bent about 90 degrees.
Hold a weight plate with both hands and extend your arms toward the ceiling.
Engage your abs and curl your shoulders up off the ball, pushing the plate upward.
Lower your shoulders back onto the ball under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted overhead crunch on a stability ball targets the abdominal muscles while also engaging the obliques. Lying with your back on the ball and holding a weight plate with your arms extended toward the ceiling, you curl your torso up against the extra resistance.

name: weighted pull-up
instructions: Grab the pull-up bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted pull-up is an advanced variation of the standard pull-up, where additional weight is used to increase resistance. This exercise primarily targets the latissimus dorsi (lats) and also engages the biceps and forearms. It requires significant upper body strength, coordination, and experience to perform safely and effectively.

name: weighted round arm
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate by its edges with both hands.
Extend your arms in front of you at shoulder height.
Keeping your arms straight, sweep the plate in an arc toward one side.
Bring it back through the center.
Sweep it toward the other side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted round arm is a shoulder exercise that targets the deltoids while also engaging the core. Holding a weight plate with straight arms in front at shoulder height, you sweep it in an arc from one side to the other.

name: weighted russian twist (legs up)
instructions: Sit on the ground with your knees bent and feet lifted off the ground, keeping your legs together.
Hold the weight with both hands in front of your chest, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Lean back slightly to engage your core muscles.
Twist your torso to the right, bringing the weight towards the ground on your right side.
Pause for a moment, then twist your torso to the left, bringing the weight towards the ground on your left side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted Russian twist (legs up) is a core exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, particularly the obliques, while also engaging the hip flexors. The movement involves twisting the torso from side to side while holding a weight and keeping the legs elevated, which increases the challenge to balance and core stability.

name: weighted russian twist
instructions: Sit on the ground with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Hold a weight or medicine ball with both hands in front of your chest.
Lean back slightly, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Slowly twist your torso to the right, bringing the weight or medicine ball towards the floor on your right side.
Pause for a moment, then twist your torso to the left, bringing the weight or medicine ball towards the floor on your left side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted Russian twist is a core exercise that targets the abs and obliques, performed by twisting the torso while holding a weight or medicine ball.

name: weighted seated bicep curl (on stability ball)
instructions: Sit on a stability ball with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Hold a medicine ball in one hand with your arm extended and your palm facing up.
Keep your upper arm still and your elbow close to your side.
Curl the medicine ball up toward your shoulder.
Lower it back down under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: A bicep curl performed while seated on a stability ball, using a medicine ball for resistance. This variation challenges core stability and balance in addition to targeting the biceps.

name: weighted seated twist (on stability ball)
instructions: Sit on a stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell with both hands close to your chest.
Engage your core and slowly rotate your torso to one side, keeping your hips stable.
Pause for a moment at the end of the rotation, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat the rotation to the other side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted seated twist on a stability ball is an exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, particularly the obliques, while also engaging the lower back. It requires core strength, balance, and coordination due to the instability of the ball and the added resistance from the weight.

name: weighted side bend (on stability ball)
instructions: Lie sideways over a stability ball with your hip on the ball, legs extended and feet staggered on the floor.
Hold a weight next to your head.
Lower your upper body sideways toward the floor over the ball.
Contract your obliques to lift your torso sideways as high as you can.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The weighted side bend on a stability ball targets the abdominal muscles, particularly the obliques, and also engages the lower back. The use of a stability ball increases the balance and core activation required, while the added weight increases resistance for strength gains.

name: weighted sissy squat
instructions: Stand next to a support such as an incline bench, holding a weight plate against your chest with one hand and gripping the support with the other.
Rise onto the balls of your feet.
Push your knees forward and lean your torso back, keeping a straight line from knees to head.
Lower until your knees are well bent and your thighs approach parallel to the floor.
Drive your knees back to return to the upright position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted sissy squat is a challenging lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps while also engaging the glutes, hamstrings, and calves. It requires balance, strength, and coordination, especially when performed with added weight.

name: weighted squat
instructions: Attach a weight plate to a dip belt around your hips and stand with one foot on each of two benches, the plate hanging between them.
Extend your arms in front of you at shoulder height for balance.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you lower your hips down and back, as if sitting into a chair.
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the benches, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Push through your heels to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: A weighted squat performed standing on two benches with a weight plate hanging from a belt between your legs. It targets the glutes, quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves while keeping the load off the spine.

name: weighted standing curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate by its top edge in one hand at your side.
Keep your elbow close to your torso and exhale as you curl the plate up toward your shoulder.
Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale as you slowly lower the plate back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The weighted standing curl is a strength exercise targeting the biceps, performed standing while curling a weight plate gripped by its rim with one hand. It also engages the forearms through the grip.

name: weighted standing hand squeeze
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Pinch a weight plate between your fingers and thumb with one hand.
Let the arm hang straight by your side, holding the plate off the floor.
Squeeze hard and hold for the planned time, keeping your shoulders level.
Set the plate down and repeat with the other hand.
description: The weighted standing hand squeeze is a grip exercise targeting the forearms, performed by pinching a weight plate in one hand and holding it at your side. It improves grip strength and forearm endurance.

name: weighted svend press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a weight plate in front of your chest with both hands.
Keep your elbows slightly bent and your palms facing each other.
Press the weight plate straight out in front of you, fully extending your arms.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly bring the weight plate back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted Svend press is a chest exercise performed by pressing a weight plate out in front of the body, emphasizing the pectoral muscles while also engaging the shoulders and triceps.

name: wheel rollout
instructions: Kneel on the floor and place the wheel roller in front of you.
Place your hands on the handles of the wheel roller and extend your arms straight out in front of you.
Engage your core muscles and slowly roll the wheel forward, keeping your back straight and your abs tight.
Continue rolling forward until your body is fully extended and your arms are overhead.
Pause for a moment, then slowly roll the wheel back towards your knees, maintaining control and keeping your abs engaged.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The wheel rollout is an advanced core exercise that targets the abdominal muscles and also engages the lower back. It requires significant core strength, stability, and control to perform safely and effectively.

name: wind sprints
instructions: Grab a pull-up bar with an overhand grip and hang with your arms fully extended.
Engage your core to keep your body from swinging.
Drive one knee up toward your chest while the other leg stays extended.
Switch legs quickly, as if running in the air.
Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions or time.
description: Wind sprints are performed hanging from a pull-up bar and driving the knees up alternately in a running motion. They primarily target the abs, with the hip flexors helping to lift the legs.

name: wrist rollerer
instructions: Attach a weight to one end of a rope or bar.
Hold the other end of the rope or bar with both hands, palms facing down.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms fully extended in front of you.
Slowly roll the weight up towards your hands by flexing your wrists.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the weight back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The wrist roller is an exercise that targets the forearms by using a weighted rope or bar. It involves rolling a weight up and down using wrist flexion and extension, which helps build forearm strength and endurance.

name: cable kickback
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the cable handle with your right hand and step back to create tension in the cable.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Keep your upper arm close to your body and your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle.
Extend your forearm backward, straightening your arm fully.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The cable kickback is an isolation exercise targeting the triceps, performed using a cable machine. It involves extending the arm backward against resistance to work the triceps, with some secondary engagement of the shoulders.

name: cable seated row
instructions: Sit on the cable row machine with your feet flat on the footrests and your knees slightly bent.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, keeping your back straight and your shoulders relaxed.
Pull the handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement, then slowly release the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable seated row is a strength exercise that targets the upper back, with secondary emphasis on the biceps and forearms. It is performed using a cable row machine and involves pulling handles towards the torso while maintaining a straight back and squeezing the shoulder blades together.

name: cable twist (up-down)
instructions: Set a cable pulley to a high position and stand side-on to the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handle with both hands above the shoulder nearest the machine, arms slightly bent.
Engage your core and pull the handle diagonally down and across your body toward the opposite hip, rotating your torso.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement.
Slowly return the handle up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The cable twist (up-down) is an exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, especially the obliques and lower back, by using a cable machine to add resistance to rotational movements of the torso.

name: dumbbell lying external shoulder rotation
instructions: Lie on your side on the floor with your upper arm against your side and your elbow bent 90 degrees.
Hold a dumbbell in your hand with your palm facing down.
Keeping your upper arm against your side, slowly rotate your forearm upward as far as possible.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your forearm back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The dumbbell lying external shoulder rotation is an exercise that targets the deltoid muscles and the rotator cuff, helping to improve shoulder stability and strength. It is performed lying on your side, rotating the forearm upward while keeping the upper arm against the side.

name: dumbbell upright shoulder external rotation
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand and placing the other hand on your hip.
Raise the working arm out to the side until the upper arm is parallel to the floor, elbow bent 90 degrees and forearm pointing down.
Keeping your upper arm still, rotate your shoulder to bring the forearm up until the dumbbell is above your elbow.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly rotate the forearm back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The dumbbell upright shoulder external rotation is an exercise that targets the deltoids and rotator cuff. Holding a dumbbell with the upper arm out at shoulder height and the elbow bent, you rotate the forearm from pointing down to pointing up.

name: lying leg-hip raise
instructions: Lie on your back on a flat bench with your legs extended and grip the bench behind your head.
Engage your core and raise your legs, bending your knees as they come toward your chest.
Lift your hips off the bench, pointing your feet toward the ceiling.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower your hips and legs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lying leg-hip raise is an abdominal exercise performed lying on a flat bench and gripping it behind your head. It targets the abs and hip flexors by raising the legs and lifting the hips off the bench, then lowering them with control.

name: weighted hanging leg-hip raise
instructions: Hold a dumbbell between your feet and hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended and your palms facing away from you.
Engage your core and raise your knees toward your chest, bending them as they rise.
Continue until your thighs are above parallel and your hips curl up slightly.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted hanging leg-hip raise is an advanced core exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, with additional emphasis on the hip flexors and lower back. The movement requires hanging from a pull-up bar while lifting weighted legs up to engage the core.

name: cable curl
instructions: Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the cable attachment with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary.
Exhale and curl the cable attachment towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the cable attachment back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable curl is a strength exercise targeting the biceps, performed using a cable machine. It involves curling a cable attachment towards the shoulders while keeping the elbows close to the body, providing constant tension on the biceps throughout the movement.

name: lever shoulder press v. 2
instructions: Adjust the seat height and backrest of the leverage machine to a comfortable position.
Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles of the machine with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Push the handles upward and forward until your arms are fully extended, but not locked.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the handles back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever shoulder press v. 2 is a machine-based exercise targeting the deltoid muscles, with secondary emphasis on the triceps and chest. It is performed seated on a leverage machine, pressing handles upward and forward to work the shoulders.

name: butt-ups
instructions: Start in a forearm plank with your elbows under your shoulders and your legs extended, balancing on your toes.
Keep your forearms on the ground with your hands loosely clasped or flat.
Engaging your abs, push your hips up toward the ceiling, forming an inverted V with your body.
At the top of the movement, squeeze your abs and pause for a moment.
Slowly lower your hips back down to the straight plank position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Butt-ups are a bodyweight exercise targeting the abdominal muscles. From a forearm plank, you drive your hips up toward the ceiling and lower them back to a straight plank. This exercise also works the hip flexors and shoulders as secondary muscles.

name: tuck crunch
instructions: Lie flat on your back and lift your legs, bending your hips and knees so your feet are in the air.
Cross your arms over your chest.
Engaging your abs, lift your shoulder blades off the ground, curling your upper body towards your knees while keeping your legs still.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your shoulder blades back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The tuck crunch is a bodyweight abdominal exercise that targets the abs and also engages the hip flexors. It involves curling the upper body toward the knees while the legs are held raised and bent, making it an effective core strengthening movement.

name: reverse crunch
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your arms extended along your sides.
Bend your knees and lift your feet off the ground, bringing your thighs perpendicular to the floor.
Contract your abs and curl your hips off the floor, bringing your knees towards your chest.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The reverse crunch is a bodyweight exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, especially the lower abs, by curling the hips off the floor and bringing the knees toward the chest.

name: cable reverse crunch
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley and lie down facing up on a mat with your feet toward the machine.
Secure the cable to your feet and rest your arms on the floor by your sides.
Bend your knees and lift your legs up, bringing your thighs towards your chest.
While keeping your upper body stable, curl your pelvis up towards your chest, lifting your hips off the mat.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable reverse crunch is an abdominal exercise that utilizes a cable machine attached to the feet to add resistance to the traditional reverse crunch movement. It primarily targets the abs and also engages the hip flexors.

name: cable standing crunch (with rope attachment)
instructions: Attach a rope to a high pulley on a cable machine.
Stand facing away from the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the rope with both hands and bring it behind your head, keeping your elbows bent.
Engage your abs and slowly crunch your torso forward, bringing your elbows towards your knees.
Pause for a moment at the top of the crunch, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable standing crunch (with rope attachment) is an abdominal exercise performed using a cable machine and rope attachment. It targets the abs and also engages the obliques. The movement involves crunching the torso forward against resistance, providing a challenging core workout.

name: band alternating biceps curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the band with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and slowly curl one arm up towards your shoulder, squeezing your biceps at the top.
Lower the arm back down to the starting position and repeat with the other arm.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band alternating biceps curl is an exercise targeting the biceps using a resistance band. It involves curling one arm at a time while keeping the elbows close to the body, providing resistance throughout the movement.

name: band alternating v-up
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your legs straight, the band looped around one foot and the ends held in your hands with your arms extended.
Engage your abs and lift your upper body and your free leg off the ground simultaneously, reaching your hands towards the raised foot.
Lower your leg and upper body back down with control, keeping the other leg on the floor.
Repeat the movement with the other leg, alternating legs with each repetition.
Continue for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band alternating v-up is an abdominal exercise that targets the abs and hip flexors. It involves lying on your back holding a resistance band and lifting your upper body and one straight leg at a time, alternating legs.

name: band assisted pull-up
instructions: Attach the band to a pull-up bar or sturdy anchor point.
Place both knees in the band and grip the bar with your palms facing away from you, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms fully extended, keeping your core engaged and your shoulders down and back.
Pull your body up towards the bar by squeezing your shoulder blades together and driving your elbows down towards your hips.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar, then slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band assisted pull-up is a variation of the traditional pull-up that uses a resistance band to provide assistance, making it easier to perform the movement. This exercise targets the latissimus dorsi (lats) and also works the biceps and forearms. It is commonly used to build strength and improve pull-up technique, especially for those who are not yet able to perform unassisted pull-ups.

name: band assisted wheel rollerout
instructions: Anchor the band low behind you, attach it to the ab wheel, and kneel on the floor holding the wheel handles with both hands, palms facing down.
Place the wheel on the ground in front of your knees with your hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and slowly roll the wheel forward, extending your body as far as you can while maintaining control.
Pause for a moment at the furthest point, then slowly roll the wheel back towards your knees to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band assisted wheel rollout is an abdominal exercise that uses a resistance band to help control the movement and reduce the difficulty compared to a standard ab wheel rollout. It targets the abs and also engages the lower back for stability.

name: band bicycle crunch
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your hands behind your head and your knees bent.
Lift your feet off the ground and bring your right knee towards your chest while simultaneously twisting your torso to bring your left elbow towards your right knee.
Straighten your right leg while bringing your left knee towards your chest and twisting your torso to bring your right elbow towards your left knee.
Continue alternating the twisting motion, as if you are pedaling a bicycle, while keeping your core engaged throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band bicycle crunch is a core exercise that targets the abs, with additional emphasis on the hip flexors and obliques. The use of a resistance band increases the challenge, requiring greater core stability and strength.

name: band close-grip pulldown
instructions: Attach the band to a high anchor point, such as a pull-up bar or sturdy beam.
Sit on a bench or box facing the anchor point and grab the band with both hands close together, arms extended overhead.
Sit tall with your feet flat on the floor so the band is under tension.
Engage your core and keep your back straight as you pull the band down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly release the band back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band close-grip pulldown is a resistance exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi (lats) using a resistance band anchored overhead. It mimics the motion of a cable pulldown but uses a band for resistance, making it accessible and effective for home workouts.

name: band close-grip push-up
instructions: Wrap the band across your upper back and hold one end under each hand.
Assume a push-up position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest towards the ground, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Push through your palms against the band to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band close-grip push-up is a variation of the traditional push-up that uses a resistance band to increase tension and target the triceps more effectively. The close hand placement emphasizes the triceps, while the band adds extra resistance throughout the movement.

name: band concentration curl
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your legs spread apart and your feet flat on the ground.
Hold one end of the band in your hand and step on the other end with your foot on the same side.
Lean forward slightly and rest your elbow on the inside of your thigh, just above the knee.
With your palm facing up, slowly curl your hand towards your shoulder, keeping your upper arm stationary.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hand back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The band concentration curl is an isolation exercise targeting the biceps using a resistance band. It is performed seated, with the working arm braced against the thigh to minimize cheating and maximize biceps engagement.

name: band front lateral raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart on the band and hold one end in one hand beside your thigh, palm facing down.
Keep your arm straight and lift it diagonally forward and out to the side until it is parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the arm back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The band front lateral raise is a shoulder exercise that targets the deltoid muscles. Using a resistance band, you lift one straight arm diagonally forward and out to the side, working the shoulders and upper back.

name: band front raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the band in front of your thighs with your palms facing down.
Keep your arms straight and slowly raise them forward until they are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band front raise is an exercise targeting the deltoid muscles of the shoulders. It is performed by standing on a resistance band and raising the arms straight in front of the body to shoulder height, then lowering them back down. This movement helps build shoulder strength and stability, with secondary activation of the triceps and upper back.

name: band horizontal pallof press
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point at waist height.
Stand perpendicular to the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the band handle with both hands and step away from the anchor point to create tension in the band.
Bring your hands to your chest, keeping your elbows bent and close to your body.
Engage your core and maintain a stable stance.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you, pushing the band away from your body.
Hold the extended position for a few seconds, focusing on maintaining tension in your core.
Slowly bring your hands back to your chest, resisting the pull of the band.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band horizontal Pallof press is an anti-rotation core exercise that targets the abs and obliques, helping to build core stability and strength. It is performed using a resistance band anchored at waist height.

name: band bent-over hip extension
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point at ankle height and loop it around one ankle.
Stand facing the anchor point with your feet hip-width apart and place your hands on a wall or support in front of you.
Step back to create tension in the band, keeping your standing knee slightly bent.
Hinge at the hips and lean forward, maintaining a neutral spine.
Extend the banded leg straight back, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Slowly bring the leg back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The band bent-over hip extension is an exercise targeting the glutes, performed by extending one leg back against resistance from a band while maintaining a bent-over position. It also engages the hamstrings and lower back.

name: band jack knife sit-up
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your legs straight, the band anchored in front of you and looped around your ankles, and your arms by your sides.
Engage your abs and sit up while bending your knees and pulling them towards your chest, bringing your hands towards your shins.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly extend your legs and lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band jack knife sit-up is an abdominal exercise that uses a resistance band attached to the feet to increase difficulty. It targets the abs and also works the hip flexors. The movement involves simultaneously sitting up and tucking the knees toward the chest against the band, requiring core strength and coordination.

name: band kneeling one arm pulldown
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point above your head.
Kneel down and hold the band with one hand, palm facing down.
Extend your arm fully overhead, keeping your elbow slightly bent.
Engage your lat muscles and pull the band down towards your side, bringing your elbow towards your ribcage.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The band kneeling one arm pulldown is a resistance band exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi (lats) and also engaging the biceps and rhomboids. It involves kneeling and pulling a resistance band from overhead down to your side, focusing on controlled movement and muscle engagement.

name: band lying hip internal rotation
instructions: Lie face down with your legs straight and a resistance band anchored to your side and looped around one ankle.
Bend the knee of the banded leg to 90 degrees so your shin points up.
Keeping your hips and thigh on the floor, slowly swing your foot outward, away from your other leg, rotating your hip inward against the band.
Pause for a moment at the end of the rotation, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The band lying hip internal rotation is an exercise that targets the glutes and helps improve hip mobility and strength. It is performed lying face down with one knee bent and a resistance band around the ankle, rotating the lower leg sideways against the band.

name: band kneeling twisting crunch
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point above head height.
Kneel down facing away from the anchor point and hold the band with both hands beside your head, elbows bent.
Engage your abs and slowly crunch down, twisting your torso to bring one elbow towards the opposite knee.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band kneeling twisting crunch is an abdominal exercise that targets the abs and obliques using a resistance band. It involves kneeling and twisting the torso against the resistance of the band, engaging the core muscles.

name: band one arm high biceps curl
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point at shoulder height and stand sideways to it with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the band with the hand nearest the anchor, arm extended out to the side at shoulder height, palm facing up; place your other hand on your hip.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, curl your forearm towards your head, squeezing your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly extend your forearm back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The band one arm overhead biceps curl is an isolation exercise targeting the biceps, performed with a resistance band anchored to the side. It involves curling the hand toward the head while the upper arm stays raised at shoulder height, providing resistance throughout the movement.

name: band one arm single leg split squat
instructions: Stand in front of a bench or box and place the middle of a resistance band under your front foot.
Extend one leg back and rest the top of your foot on the bench or step behind you.
Hold the free end of the band in one hand with your arm extended by your side.
Bend your front leg and lower your body down into a squat position, keeping your knee in line with your toes.
Push through your heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The band one arm single leg split squat is a lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, with secondary emphasis on the glutes and hamstrings. It involves performing a split squat with the rear foot elevated while holding a resistance band anchored under the front foot with one hand, challenging balance and unilateral strength.

name: band one arm standing low row
instructions: Attach the band to a stable anchor point near the floor.
Stand facing the anchor point in a staggered stance, one foot in front of the other.
Hold the band with one hand, palm facing inward, and step back to create tension in the band.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Pull the band towards your hip, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release the band back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The band one arm standing low row is a resistance band exercise targeting the upper back, performed by pulling a band anchored low towards your hip with one arm while standing.

name: band one arm twisting chest press
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point at chest height when seated.
Sit on the floor with your legs extended, your side facing the anchor point, and grab the band with the hand nearest to it.
Scoot away from the anchor point to create tension in the band.
Sit tall with your back straight and your core engaged.
Bring your hand holding the band to the side of your chest, elbow bent and pointing back.
While maintaining tension in the band, push your hand forward and across your body, rotating your torso and extending your arm.
Slowly return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Switch sides and repeat the exercise with the other hand.
description: The band one arm twisting chest press is a unilateral chest exercise using a resistance band. It targets the pectorals while also engaging the shoulders and triceps. The twisting motion adds a rotational component, increasing core activation and coordination demands.

name: band one arm twisting seated row
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you and your back straight, with the band anchored in front of you.
Hold the band with one hand and extend your arm fully in front of you.
Keeping your back straight, pull the band towards your body by bending your elbow and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
At the same time, twist your torso towards the side of the pulling arm.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly release the tension in the band and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
description: The band one arm twisting seated row is a resistance exercise targeting the upper back, with secondary emphasis on the biceps and shoulders. It incorporates a twisting motion to engage the core and improve rotational strength.

name: band pull through
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at ground level.
Stand facing away from the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step forward to create tension in the band, keeping your knees slightly bent.
Hinge at the hips and push your glutes back, maintaining a slight bend in your knees.
Lower your torso until it is parallel to the ground, feeling a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band pull through is a hip hinge exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back using a resistance band. It is performed by hinging at the hips while facing away from an anchored band, then driving the hips forward to stand upright.

name: band push sit-up
instructions: Attach the band securely to a stable anchor point behind your head.
Lie flat on your back with your legs extended on the ground.
Hold the band with both hands and extend your arms straight up towards the ceiling.
Engaging your abs, slowly lift your upper body off the ground, curling forward until you are sitting upright with your arms pushed forward.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band push sit-up is an abdominal exercise that incorporates resistance from a band to increase the challenge on the core muscles. It also engages the shoulders and chest as stabilizers during the movement.

name: band reverse fly
instructions: Attach the band to a stationary object at chest height.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the band with both hands in front of you.
Keep your arms straight and lift them out to the sides until they are parallel to the ground.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band reverse fly is an exercise that targets the deltoid muscles of the shoulders, as well as the upper back and trapezius. It is performed using a resistance band attached to a stationary object, and involves pulling the band apart with straight arms to strengthen the rear delts and upper back.

name: band reverse wrist curl
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet flat on the ground.
Hold the band with an overhand grip, palms facing down, and wrap it around your fingers.
Rest your forearms on your thighs, with your wrists hanging off the edge.
Slowly curl your wrists upward, squeezing your forearms.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band reverse wrist curl is an isolation exercise targeting the forearms, specifically the wrist extensors, using a resistance band. It is performed seated, with the forearms resting on the thighs and the wrists curling upward against the resistance of the band.

name: band seated hip internal rotation
instructions: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Loop a resistance band anchored to your side around one ankle.
Keep your knees bent at a 90-degree angle and the knee of the working leg still.
Engage your glutes and slowly swing your foot outward, away from your other leg, rotating your hip inward against the band.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The band seated hip internal rotation is an exercise that targets the glutes and helps improve hip mobility and strength. It is performed while seated, with a resistance band around one ankle, rotating the lower leg outward to turn the hip inward.

name: band shoulder press
instructions: Stand in a staggered stance and place the band under your front foot.
Hold the band with your palms facing forward and raise your hands to shoulder height, elbows bent.
Press the band overhead, fully extending your arms.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the band back to shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band shoulder press is a resistance exercise targeting the deltoid muscles of the shoulders, using a resistance band for added tension. It also engages the triceps and upper back as secondary muscles. The movement involves pressing the band overhead from shoulder height, making it a fundamental strength exercise for the upper body.

name: band side triceps extension
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart beside a band anchored at shoulder height on your opposite side, and hold it with the far hand, palm facing down; place your other hand on your hip.
Raise your working upper arm out to the side, parallel to the ground, with your elbow bent and your hand near your head.
Slowly extend your elbow, pushing your hand out to the side until your arm is straight, keeping your upper arm still.
Pause for a moment, then slowly bend your elbow back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The band side triceps extension is an exercise targeting the triceps using a resistance band. It also engages the shoulders as secondary muscles. The movement involves holding one upper arm out to the side and straightening the elbow against the band, then returning the hand toward the head.

name: band single leg calf raise
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and place the band around the ball of your left foot.
Hold onto a stable object for balance if needed.
Slowly raise your left heel off the ground, lifting your body weight onto the ball of your foot.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your left heel back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the right leg.
description: The band single leg calf raise is a lower leg exercise that targets the calves using a resistance band. It also engages the ankles and feet, helping to improve strength and stability in the lower leg. The movement is performed one leg at a time, which increases the balance and coordination required.

name: band single leg reverse calf raise
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and place the band around the ball of your foot.
Hold onto a stable object for balance.
Slowly raise your heel off the ground, lifting your body weight onto the ball of your foot.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other leg.
description: The band single leg reverse calf raise is a lower leg exercise that targets the calves, with secondary emphasis on the hamstrings and glutes. It uses a resistance band and requires balance and control as you raise your heel off the ground on one leg.

name: band single leg split squat
instructions: Stand in front of a bench or box and place the middle of a resistance band under your right foot, holding the ends with both hands.
Rest the top of your left foot on the bench behind you, with your right foot well forward.
Bend your knees and lower your body until your right thigh is parallel to the ground, keeping your left knee slightly above the ground.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side.
description: The band single leg split squat is a lower body exercise targeting the quads, with secondary emphasis on the glutes and hamstrings. It uses a resistance band for added tension and requires balance and coordination.

name: band lying straight leg raise
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your legs straight and your feet together.
Loop a band anchored low beyond your feet around your feet and place your hands by your head.
Engaging your abs, lift both legs off the ground until they are perpendicular to the floor.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band lying straight leg raise is an abdominal exercise that also engages the hip flexors. It uses a resistance band to add difficulty and helps strengthen the core and lower body.

name: band squat row
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point at waist height.
Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the band handles with your palms facing each other and your arms extended in front of you.
Bend your knees and lower into a squat position with your arms extended, keeping your back straight and chest lifted.
Drive up to standing while pulling the band handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then extend your arms as you lower back into the squat.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band squat row is a compound exercise that targets the glutes while also engaging the hamstrings, quadriceps, and back. It combines a squat with a rowing motion using a resistance band, making it effective for both lower and upper body strength.

name: band squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart on the band, holding the handles at your shoulders.
Keeping your chest up and core engaged, push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat position.
Make sure your knees are tracking over your toes and your weight is in your heels.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band squat is a lower body exercise that targets the glutes using a resistance band stood on and held at the shoulders. It also engages the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. This exercise helps build strength and stability in the lower body.

name: band standing crunch
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point above head height.
Stand facing away from the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the band with both hands and bring it up to your chest, keeping your elbows bent and close to your body.
Engage your abs and slowly crunch forward, bringing your chest towards your knees.
Pause for a moment at the top of the crunch, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band standing crunch is an abdominal exercise performed with a resistance band anchored above head height. It targets the abs and also engages the obliques. The movement involves crunching forward against the resistance of the band while standing, which can help strengthen the core.

name: band standing twisting crunch
instructions: Attach the band to a high anchor behind you and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the band with both hands at the sides of your head, elbows bent.
Engage your abs and crunch forward, twisting your torso to bring one elbow towards the opposite knee.
Pause for a moment, then return to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band standing twisting crunch is an abdominal exercise that targets the abs and obliques using a resistance band. It involves twisting the torso while performing a crunch motion, engaging the core muscles.

name: band step-up
instructions: Stand facing a step or platform and place your right foot on it, with the band under that foot.
Hold the band ends at shoulder height.
Step up onto the platform, pushing through your right heel until your leg is straight.
Bring your left foot up beside your right.
Lower your left foot back down to the ground with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The band step-up is a lower body exercise that targets the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. It involves stepping onto a platform with resistance provided by a band anchored under the working foot and held at shoulder height.

name: band stiff leg deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart on the band.
Hold the band with both hands in front of your thighs, palms facing your body.
Keeping your back straight and your core engaged, hinge at the hips and slowly lower your upper body towards the ground.
As you lower, push your hips back and allow your knees to bend slightly.
Lower the band towards the ground, feeling a stretch in your hamstrings.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then engage your glutes and hamstrings to lift your upper body back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band stiff leg deadlift is a lower body exercise targeting the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the hamstrings and lower back. It uses a resistance band to provide tension throughout the movement, focusing on hip hinging and posterior chain activation.

name: band straight leg deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place the band around your feet.
Hold the band with both hands, palms facing your body, and keep your arms straight.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Slowly hinge forward at your hips, keeping your back straight and chest lifted.
Lower the band towards the ground while keeping your legs straight.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then squeeze your glutes and hamstrings to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band straight leg deadlift is a resistance exercise targeting the muscles of the lower back, hamstrings, and glutes. Using a resistance band, it mimics the movement of a traditional straight leg deadlift, focusing on hip hinging and posterior chain activation.

name: band seated twist
instructions: Attach the band to an anchor at chest height beside you and sit on the ground with your legs extended and your back straight.
Hold the band with both hands, arms extended in front of your chest.
Engage your abs and slowly twist your torso away from the anchor, keeping your arms straight and your feet on the ground.
Pause for a moment at the end of the twist, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The band seated twist is an exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, particularly the obliques, by incorporating rotational movement with resistance from a band. It is performed seated on the ground with legs extended and involves twisting the torso side to side.

name: band twisting overhead press
instructions: Attach the band to a low anchor beside you and stand with a wide stance.
Hold the band handle at the shoulder farther from the anchor, knees slightly bent.
Engage your core and push up through your legs as you rotate your torso away from the anchor.
Press the band diagonally overhead until your arm is fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, then return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The band twisting overhead press is a dynamic shoulder exercise that combines an overhead press with a torso twist, engaging the deltoids, triceps, and upper back while also challenging core stability and coordination.

name: band underhand pulldown
instructions: Attach the band to a high anchor point, such as a pull-up bar or sturdy beam.
Sit on a bench or box under the anchor with your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the band with an underhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms fully overhead, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Engage your lats and pull the band down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band underhand pulldown is a resistance band exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi (lats) and also engaging the biceps and forearms. It mimics the movement of a lat pulldown machine but uses a resistance band anchored overhead.

name: band v-up
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your legs straight and your arms extended overhead, holding the band.
Engaging your abs, lift your legs and upper body off the ground simultaneously, reaching your hands towards your toes.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs and upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band v-up is an abdominal exercise that uses a resistance band to increase the challenge. It targets the abs and also engages the hip flexors, requiring core strength and coordination to perform the simultaneous lifting of the upper and lower body.

name: band vertical pallof press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and wrap the band around a sturdy object at chest height.
Hold the band with both hands and step away from the anchor point, creating tension in the band.
Position yourself perpendicular to the anchor point, with your side facing the band.
Hold your hands together at the center of your chest.
Engage your core and press the band straight up overhead, fully extending your arms without letting your torso rotate.
Hold the position for a moment, then slowly bring the band back to your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The band vertical Pallof press is an anti-rotation core exercise that targets the abs and also engages the obliques and glutes. It is performed by pressing a resistance band from the chest up overhead while resisting rotational forces, helping to build core stability and strength.

name: band wrist curl
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet flat on the ground.
Hold the band with both hands, palms facing up, and rest your forearms on your thighs.
Slowly curl your wrists upward, squeezing your forearms.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band wrist curl is an isolation exercise targeting the forearms using a resistance band. It is performed seated, with the forearms resting on the thighs, and involves curling the wrists upward to strengthen the forearm muscles.

name: band y-raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the band in front of your thighs with your palms facing inwards.
Keep your arms straight and lift them up and out to the sides, forming a 'Y' shape with your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band Y-raise is a shoulder exercise that targets the deltoids and also engages the traps and rhomboids. It is performed using a resistance band and involves raising the arms in a 'Y' shape to strengthen the upper back and shoulders.

name: band shrug
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place the band under your feet, holding the ends with your hands.
Keep your arms straight and relaxed, and let the band hang in front of your thighs.
Engage your traps by shrugging your shoulders upward, lifting the band as high as possible.
Hold the contraction for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band shrug is an exercise targeting the trapezius muscles using a resistance band. It is performed by standing on the band, holding the ends, and shrugging the shoulders upward to engage the traps.

name: band standing rear delt row
instructions: Attach the band to an anchor at shoulder height and stand facing it in a staggered stance.
Hold the band handles with your arms extended in front of you at shoulder height.
Keep your torso upright and your core engaged.
Pull the band back, leading with your elbows held high and out to the sides, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band standing rear delt row is an exercise targeting the rear deltoids, with secondary emphasis on the trapezius, rhomboids, and biceps. It uses a resistance band anchored in front at shoulder height and involves pulling the band back with the elbows high, focusing on squeezing the shoulder blades together.

name: band straight back stiff leg deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart on the band.
Hold the band with both hands in front of your thighs, palms facing your body.
Keeping your back straight and your knees slightly bent, hinge at the hips and lower the band towards the ground.
Feel the stretch in your hamstrings as you lower the band.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings to lift your body back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band straight back stiff leg deadlift is a lower body exercise targeting the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the hamstrings and lower back. It uses a resistance band and requires maintaining a straight back while hinging at the hips, focusing on posterior chain strength.

name: burpee
instructions: Start in a standing position with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and placing your hands on the floor in front of you.
Kick your feet back into a push-up position.
Perform a push-up, keeping your body in a straight line.
