Jump your feet back into the squat position.
Jump up explosively, reaching your arms overhead.
Land softly and immediately lower back into a squat position to begin the next repetition.
description: The burpee is a full-body exercise that combines a squat, push-up, and jump to elevate heart rate and build strength and endurance.

name: dynamic chest stretch (male)
instructions: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms straight in front of you at shoulder height.
Swing your arms open out to the sides, slightly behind your body, keeping them parallel to the ground.
Feel the stretch in your chest muscles.
Bring your arms back in front of you with control.
Repeat the movement continuously for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dynamic chest stretch (male) is a bodyweight exercise designed to increase flexibility and mobility in the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It involves controlled arm movements to stretch the pectoral muscles dynamically.

name: dumbbell burpee
instructions: Start in a standing position with your feet shoulder-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Lower your body into a squat position, placing the dumbbells on the ground in front of you.
Kick your feet back into a push-up position, keeping your body in a straight line and your hands on the dumbbells.
Jump your feet back towards your hands, landing in a squat position.
Stand up explosively, lifting the dumbbells off the ground and holding them at your sides.
Repeat the entire sequence for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell burpee is a full-body exercise that combines a squat, a plank and a stand-up while holding dumbbells. It targets the cardiovascular system while also engaging multiple muscle groups, including the legs, shoulders, and core.

name: lever donkey calf raise
instructions: Adjust the leverage machine to the appropriate height for your body.
Position yourself facing the machine, with your toes on the foot platform and your heels hanging off the edge.
Place your hands on the handles or the support bars for stability.
Engage your calves and lift your heels as high as possible, using the balls of your feet.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever donkey calf raise is a machine-based exercise targeting the calf muscles. It involves standing on a platform with your heels hanging off, then raising and lowering your heels to work the calves. The leverage machine provides resistance and support, making it a controlled movement.

name: band bench press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Grasp the band handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms fully, pushing the bands away from your chest.
Slowly lower the bands back down to your chest, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band bench press is a resistance exercise targeting the pectoral muscles using a resistance band. It mimics the traditional bench press but uses bands instead of weights, making it accessible and effective for building chest strength with less equipment.

name: barbell decline pullover
instructions: Lie down on a decline bench with your head lower than your hips and your feet secured.
Hold the barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing away from you) and your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the barbell in an arc motion behind your head, feeling a stretch in your chest and shoulders.
Pause for a moment, then return the barbell to the starting position by reversing the motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The barbell decline pullover is a chest exercise performed on a decline bench, targeting the pectorals with secondary emphasis on the triceps and shoulders. It involves lowering a barbell in an arc behind the head and returning to the starting position, requiring control and stability.

name: barbell reverse grip decline bench press
instructions: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and your head lower than your hips.
Grasp the barbell with a reverse grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The barbell reverse grip decline bench press is a chest exercise performed on a decline bench using a barbell with a reverse (underhand) grip. This variation targets the lower chest and places additional emphasis on the triceps and shoulders.

name: barbell reverse grip incline bench press
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Lie down on the bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the barbell with a reverse grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The barbell reverse grip incline bench press is a chest exercise performed on an incline bench using a barbell with a reverse (underhand) grip. This variation targets the upper chest and also involves the triceps and shoulders. It requires good technique and control to perform safely, especially due to the unusual grip and incline position.

name: barbell wide reverse grip bench press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Grasp the barbell with a wide reverse grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Lower the barbell slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in and your wrists straight.
Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest, then push it back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The barbell wide reverse grip bench press is a chest exercise that targets the pectorals, with secondary emphasis on the triceps and shoulders. It involves lying on a bench and pressing a barbell with a wide, reverse (underhand) grip.

name: behind head chest stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and your back tall.
Interlace your fingers behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Have a partner stand behind you and hold your elbows.
Let your partner gently pull your elbows back while you push your chest forward.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds.
Release the stretch and repeat as desired.
description: The behind head chest stretch is an assisted flexibility exercise that targets the pectoral muscles. It is performed seated on the floor with the fingers interlaced behind the head while a partner gently draws the elbows back to stretch the chest.

name: cable decline one arm press
instructions: Place a decline bench next to a low pulley cable machine.
Lie on the decline bench with your feet secured and your head lower than your hips, and grab the handle with one hand.
Hold the handle at the side of your chest with your elbow bent.
Press the handle straight up until your arm is fully extended above your chest.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the handle back to your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The cable decline one arm press is a unilateral chest exercise performed on a cable machine, targeting the lower pectorals while also engaging the triceps and shoulders. It requires stabilization and control, especially due to the single-arm nature and the decline angle.

name: cable decline press
instructions: Place a decline bench between two low pulleys.
Lie on the decline bench with your legs secured and your head lower than your hips.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position them at chest level.
Keep your back firmly against the bench.
Exhale and press the handles up away from your body, extending your arms fully.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, squeezing your chest muscles.
Inhale and slowly return the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable decline press is a chest exercise performed on a cable machine with a decline bench. It targets the lower portion of the pectoral muscles and also engages the triceps and shoulders. The movement involves pressing the handles away from the body in a decline position, providing constant tension through the range of motion.

name: cable one arm decline chest fly
instructions: Attach a D-handle to a low pulley cable machine and set the bench to a decline angle.
Lie down on the bench with your head towards the machine and grab the handle with your right hand.
Extend your arm straight up above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
With a controlled motion, lower your arm out to the side until your hand is in line with your shoulder.
Pause for a moment, then reverse the motion and bring your arm back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to your left arm and repeat the exercise.
description: The cable one arm decline chest fly is an isolation exercise targeting the pectoral muscles using a cable machine and a decline bench. It emphasizes unilateral strength and control, helping to improve muscle symmetry and chest development.

name: cable one arm fly on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball next to a low pulley and walk your feet forward until your upper back rests on the ball, hips lifted.
Hold the cable handle in the hand closer to the pulley with your arm extended out to the side.
Keep your elbow slightly bent and your palm facing up.
Slowly bring your arm up over your chest, squeezing your chest muscles.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The cable one arm fly on exercise ball is a unilateral chest exercise performed with the upper back supported on an exercise ball, which adds a balance component to the traditional cable fly movement. It targets the pectorals while also engaging the deltoids and triceps, and requires core and glute stability to hold the bridge on the ball.

name: cable one arm incline fly on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball next to a low pulley and walk your feet forward until your back rests on the ball at an incline.
Hold a cable handle in the hand closer to the pulley with your arm extended out to the side.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbow, squeeze your chest muscles to bring your arm up over your chest.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower your arm out to the side until your hand is in line with your shoulder.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The cable one arm incline fly on exercise ball is a chest exercise performed using a cable machine and an exercise ball, targeting the pectorals while also engaging the deltoids and triceps. The exercise requires balance and coordination due to the unstable surface of the exercise ball and the unilateral movement.

name: cable one arm incline press
instructions: Adjust the cable machine to a low pulley position.
Sit on an incline bench facing away from the cable machine.
Grasp the handle with one hand and bring it up to shoulder height.
Position your feet firmly on the ground and maintain a stable position.
Press the handle forward and upward, extending your arm fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the handle back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The cable one arm incline press is a unilateral chest exercise performed on an incline bench using a cable machine. It targets the pectoral muscles while also engaging the deltoids and triceps. This movement requires stability and coordination as you press the cable handle upward with one arm at a time.

name: cable one arm incline press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball next to a low pulley and walk your feet forward until your back rests on the ball at an incline.
Hold a cable handle in one hand and position your arm at a 90-degree angle with your elbow bent.
Press the cable handle forward and upward, extending your arm fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the cable handle back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
description: The cable one arm incline press on exercise ball is a unilateral chest exercise performed on an unstable surface, targeting the pectorals while also engaging the shoulders and triceps. The use of the exercise ball increases the demand for balance and core stability.

name: cable one arm press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball next to a low pulley and walk your feet forward until your upper back rests on the ball, hips lifted.
Hold the cable handle in the hand closer to the pulley at chest height, elbow bent.
Keep your hips level and your core braced.
Press the cable handle straight up, extending your arm fully.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The cable one arm press on exercise ball is a unilateral chest exercise that also challenges core stability and balance by having the user hold a bridge with the upper back on an unstable ball while pressing a cable handle upward.

name: cable press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball between two low pulleys and walk your feet forward until your upper back rests on the ball, hips lifted and knees at a 90-degree angle.
Hold the cable handles at chest height with your palms facing forward and your elbows bent.
Engage your core and press the cable handles straight up until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment, then slowly release the tension and bring the cable handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable press on exercise ball is a chest exercise that also engages the shoulders and triceps. It is performed with the upper back supported on an exercise ball, holding cable handles, and pressing them upward while maintaining balance and core stability.

name: cable standing up straight crossovers
instructions: Stand in the middle of a cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the handles of the cables with your palms facing down and your arms extended straight out to the sides.
Keeping your arms straight, bring your hands together in front of your body, crossing them over each other.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position, keeping your arms extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Cable standing up straight crossovers are a chest exercise performed using a cable machine. The movement involves bringing the arms together in front of the body, crossing them over each other, which targets the pectoral muscles and also engages the deltoids and triceps.

name: cable upper chest crossovers
instructions: Attach the handles to the cables at the lowest position.
Stand in the center of the cable machine with one foot slightly in front of the other.
Grasp the handles with your palms facing up and your arms extended out to the sides.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and engage your core.
Sweep the cables up and together until your hands meet in front of your forehead.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the peak of the movement.
Slowly release the cables back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Cable upper chest crossovers target the pectoral muscles using a cable machine, emphasizing the upper chest. The movement involves crossing the cables in front of the body, which also engages the deltoids and triceps.

name: chest and front of shoulder stretch
instructions: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a stick or towel with a wide overhand grip in front of your hips.
Keeping your arms long, lift the stick up over your head.
Continue moving it back behind your head as far as is comfortable, feeling a stretch in your chest and front of your shoulders.
Hold briefly, then bring the stick back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: A stretch targeting the chest and front of the shoulders, performed by holding a stick or towel with a wide grip and lifting it up and back over the head to open up the pectorals and deltoids.

name: chest stretch with exercise ball
instructions: Kneel on all fours with a stability ball beside you.
Place one hand on top of the ball with your arm extended out to the side, keeping the other hand on the floor.
Slowly roll the ball outward and lower your chest towards the floor, feeling a stretch in your chest and front of your shoulder.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: A chest stretch performed kneeling with one arm resting on a stability ball to help open up the pectoral muscles, with some engagement of the shoulders. This exercise focuses on flexibility and mobility rather than strength or cardio.

name: clap push up
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your core engaged.
Push through your palms explosively to propel your body off the ground.
While in mid-air, clap your hands together before landing back in the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The clap push up is a plyometric bodyweight exercise that targets the pectorals, triceps, and shoulders. It involves an explosive push off the ground, clapping the hands in mid-air, and landing back in the push-up position. This movement requires significant upper body strength, power, and coordination.

name: deep push up
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The deep push up is a variation of the traditional push up that increases the range of motion, targeting the pectorals more intensely and also engaging the triceps and shoulders.

name: drop push up
instructions: Place two benches parallel, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and start in a high plank with your hands on the benches.
Remove your hands from the benches and drop down, landing with your hands on the floor between them.
Absorb the landing by bending your elbows and lowering your chest towards the floor.
Push explosively off the floor to bring your hands back onto the benches.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The drop push up is a plyometric bodyweight exercise that targets the pectorals and also works the triceps and shoulders. It involves dropping from a raised push-up position between two benches, catching yourself on the floor, and pushing explosively back up.

name: dumbbell decline one arm fly
instructions: Lie down on a decline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting it on your thigh.
Using your thigh to help raise the dumbbell, lift it up to shoulder width with your palm facing your torso.
Rotate your wrist so that the palm of your hand is facing forward.
As you breathe in, lower the dumbbell slowly to the side until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Exhale and use your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The dumbbell decline one arm fly is a unilateral chest exercise performed on a decline bench, targeting the pectoral muscles and also engaging the shoulders. It requires good control and stability to perform safely, especially due to the decline angle and single-arm movement.

name: dumbbell fly on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported by the ball.
Extend your arms straight up above your chest, palms facing each other.
Bend your elbows slightly and lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Pause for a moment, then reverse the movement and squeeze your chest muscles as you bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell fly on exercise ball is a chest exercise that also challenges your core and stability by performing the movement on an unstable surface. It targets the pectorals, with secondary emphasis on the shoulders and triceps.

name: dumbbell incline fly on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand.
Walk your feet forward slightly and lean back until your mid and upper back rest on the ball, keeping your hips low so your torso is inclined.
Hold the dumbbells with your palms facing each other and your arms extended above your chest.
Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Pause for a moment, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell incline fly on exercise ball is a chest exercise that targets the pectorals while also engaging the shoulders and core for stability. It is performed by lying back on an exercise ball with dumbbells and performing a fly motion.

name: dumbbell incline one arm fly
instructions: Adjust the incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Sit on the bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting it on your thigh.
Lie back on the bench, keeping your feet flat on the ground.
Hold the dumbbell with your arm extended straight up over your chest.
Lower the dumbbell out to the side in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pause when your arm is parallel to the ground, then reverse the motion to bring the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The dumbbell incline one arm fly is a unilateral chest exercise performed on an incline bench. It targets the pectoral muscles and also engages the deltoids and triceps. The movement requires control and stability, as only one arm is working at a time, increasing the demand on core and shoulder stabilizers.

name: dumbbell incline one arm fly on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand.
Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbell with your arm extended straight up over your chest, palm facing inwards.
Slowly lower the dumbbell out to the side, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pause for a moment when your arm is parallel to the ground.
Engage your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The dumbbell incline one arm fly on exercise ball is a chest exercise that also challenges stability and balance by using an exercise ball. It targets the pectorals and also engages the shoulders and core for stabilization.

name: dumbbell incline one arm press
instructions: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting on your thigh.
Lie back on the bench and position the dumbbell at shoulder level, palm facing forward.
Press the dumbbell upward and slightly inward, extending your arm fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
description: The dumbbell incline one arm press is a unilateral chest exercise performed on an incline bench, targeting the upper pectorals while also engaging the shoulders and triceps. It requires balance and coordination due to the single-arm movement.

name: dumbbell incline one arm press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand, feet flat on the ground.
Slowly walk your feet forward, rolling the ball until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbell at shoulder height with your palm facing forward.
Press the dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
description: The dumbbell incline one arm press on exercise ball is a chest exercise that also engages the shoulders and triceps. It requires balance and core stability due to the use of an exercise ball and the unilateral pressing movement.

name: dumbbell incline press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Slowly walk your feet forward, rolling your body down the ball until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbells at shoulder level, elbows bent and pointing out to the sides.
Press the dumbbells upward, extending your arms fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell incline press on exercise ball is a chest exercise that also engages the shoulders and triceps. Performing this movement on an exercise ball increases the demand for balance and core stability compared to a traditional incline press on a bench.

name: dumbbell lying pullover on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball and roll forward until your upper back is resting on the ball.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight up over your chest.
Slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head while keeping your arms straight.
Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell lying pullover on exercise ball is a chest exercise that also engages the triceps, shoulders, and back. It requires balance and stability due to the use of the exercise ball, making it more challenging than the standard pullover.

name: dumbbell one arm bench fly
instructions: Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting it on top of your thigh.
Lie back on the bench, keeping the dumbbell pressed against your thigh.
Using your free hand, help lift the dumbbell up to the starting position.
Hold the dumbbell directly above your shoulder with your arm extended and palm facing inward.
Lower the dumbbell out to the side in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pause when your arm is parallel to the ground, then reverse the movement and bring the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms and repeat.
description: The dumbbell one arm bench fly is a unilateral chest exercise that targets the pectoral muscles and also engages the shoulders. It requires balance and control to stabilize the weight with one arm while lying on a bench.

name: dumbbell one arm chest fly on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand and your feet flat on the ground.
Walk your feet forward, rolling the ball until your upper back is supported on the ball and your head, neck, and shoulders are off the ball.
Extend your arm with the dumbbell straight up above your chest, palm facing inward.
Slowly lower the dumbbell out to the side, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pause for a moment when your arm is parallel to the ground.
Engage your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The dumbbell one arm chest fly on exercise ball is a unilateral chest exercise that also challenges core stability and balance by using an exercise ball as the base of support. It targets the pectoral muscles and also works the shoulders and triceps.

name: dumbbell one arm decline chest press
instructions: Lie on a decline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting on your chest.
Place your feet flat on the ground and keep your back pressed against the bench.
Extend your arm and push the dumbbell up towards the ceiling, fully extending your elbow.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
description: The dumbbell one arm decline chest press is a unilateral chest exercise performed on a decline bench, targeting the pectorals while also engaging the triceps and shoulders. It requires good stability and control due to the single-arm movement and the decline angle.

name: dumbbell one arm fly on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand and your feet flat on the ground.
Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your upper back is resting on the exercise ball.
Extend your arm with the dumbbell straight up above your chest, palm facing inwards.
Slowly lower the dumbbell out to the side, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pause for a moment, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The dumbbell one arm fly on exercise ball is a chest exercise that also challenges balance and core stability. It involves performing a single-arm fly movement while lying with your upper back on an exercise ball, which increases the demand on stabilizing muscles.

name: dumbbell one arm incline chest press
instructions: Adjust the incline bench to a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench with your back against the pad and feet flat on the ground.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an overhand grip, resting it on your shoulder.
Push the dumbbell up and away from your body, extending your arm fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
description: The dumbbell one arm incline chest press is a unilateral upper body exercise that targets the pectoral muscles, with secondary emphasis on the shoulders and triceps. It is performed on an incline bench using a single dumbbell, which increases the demand for core stability and coordination.

name: dumbbell one arm press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand and walk your feet forward until your upper back rests on the ball, hips lifted and knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Position the dumbbell at shoulder height, with your elbow bent and palm facing forward.
Slowly press the dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended, while keeping your core engaged and maintaining balance on the exercise ball.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
description: The dumbbell one arm press on exercise ball is a unilateral chest exercise that also challenges your core and balance by performing the movement on an unstable surface. It targets the pectorals while also engaging the shoulders, triceps, and core muscles.

name: dumbbell one arm pullover on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball and walk your feet forward until your upper back rests on the ball, hips lifted and knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Hold a dumbbell with one hand and extend your arm straight up above your chest.
Slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head while keeping your arm straight.
Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The dumbbell one arm pullover on exercise ball is a chest exercise that also engages the triceps, latissimus dorsi, and rhomboids. It requires balance and core stability due to the use of the exercise ball, as well as unilateral strength and coordination.

name: dumbbell one leg fly on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand and walk your feet forward until your upper back rests on the ball, hips lifted.
Keep one foot on the ground and extend the other leg straight out in front of you.
Extend your arms above your chest with your palms facing each other and a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower the dumbbells down and out to the sides, feeling a stretch in your chest.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.
description: The dumbbell one leg fly on exercise ball is a chest exercise that also challenges balance and core stability. It involves performing a dumbbell fly with your upper back on an exercise ball while one leg is extended, targeting the pectorals with secondary emphasis on shoulders and triceps.

name: dumbbell press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and dumbbells in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Slowly walk your feet forward, rolling the exercise ball until your upper back is supported on the ball and your knees are at a 90-degree angle.
Raise the dumbbells to shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell press on exercise ball is a chest exercise that also engages the shoulders and triceps, performed while balancing on an exercise ball to increase core activation and stability demands.

name: dumbbell pullover hip extension on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and the dumbbell resting on your thighs.
Slowly walk your feet forward, rolling the exercise ball down your back until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight up over your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head, keeping your arms straight and maintaining control.
Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
While keeping your arms extended, lift your hips off the ground, squeezing your glutes and engaging your core.
Lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell pullover hip extension on exercise ball is a compound exercise that targets the pectorals while also engaging the triceps, shoulders, and core. It combines a pullover movement with a hip extension, performed on an unstable surface (exercise ball), which increases the demand for balance and coordination.

name: dumbbell pullover on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball and walk your feet forward until your upper back rests on the ball, hips lifted, then hold a dumbbell with both hands above your chest, arms extended.
Slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head while keeping your arms straight.
Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell pullover on exercise ball is a chest exercise that also engages the triceps and latissimus dorsi. It is performed by lying on an exercise ball, holding a dumbbell above the chest, and lowering it behind the head before returning to the starting position.

name: exercise ball pike push up
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands on the floor and your shins resting on the stability ball.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest towards the floor, keeping your body in a straight line.
Push through your hands to extend your arms.
Engage your core and lift your hips up towards the ceiling, rolling the ball towards your hands with your legs straight to form an inverted V shape.
Lower your hips to return to the push-up position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The exercise ball pike push up is a challenging upper body and core exercise that combines a push-up with a pike, performed with the shins on a stability ball. This exercise targets the pectorals while also engaging the shoulders, triceps, and core for stabilization and strength.

name: isometric chest squeeze
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you, parallel to the ground, with your palms facing each other.
Squeeze your chest muscles together as hard as you can, while keeping your arms straight.
Hold this position for a few seconds, focusing on contracting your chest muscles.
Release the squeeze and relax your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The isometric chest squeeze is a bodyweight exercise that targets the pectoral muscles by requiring you to contract and hold tension in your chest while your arms are extended in front of you.

name: kettlebell one arm floor press
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your legs extended.
Hold the kettlebell in one hand with your palm facing towards your feet and your arm extended straight up towards the ceiling.
Slowly lower the kettlebell towards your chest by bending your elbow, keeping your upper arm close to your body.
Pause for a moment when your upper arm touches the floor, then push it back up to the starting position by extending your elbow.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
description: The kettlebell one arm floor press is a unilateral chest exercise performed lying on the floor, pressing a kettlebell with one arm at a time. It targets the pectorals while also engaging the triceps and shoulders, and requires stability and control.

name: lever incline chest press
instructions: Adjust the seat and backrest of the leverage machine to a comfortable position.
Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Push the handles forward and away from your body until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment, then slowly bend your elbows and lower the handles back towards your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever incline chest press is a machine-based exercise targeting the upper chest (pectorals), with secondary emphasis on the shoulders and triceps. It is performed on a leverage machine, providing guided movement for safety and stability.

name: lever decline chest press
instructions: Adjust the seat height and backrest of the leverage machine to a comfortable position.
Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Push the handles forward and away from your body until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly lower the handles back towards your chest, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever decline chest press is a machine-based exercise targeting the pectoral muscles, with secondary emphasis on the triceps and shoulders. It is performed on a leverage machine, providing guided movement for safety and stability.

name: machine inner chest press
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back flat against the pad.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended, exhaling during the movement.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position, inhaling as you do so.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The machine inner chest press is a chest-focused exercise performed on a leverage machine. It targets the pectoral muscles and also works the triceps and shoulders. The machine provides stability and guided movement, making it accessible for most users.

name: medicine ball chest pass
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the medicine ball at chest level.
Extend your arms forward, pushing the medicine ball away from your chest with force.
As you release the ball, follow through with your arms and torso, transferring your weight from your back foot to your front foot.
Catch the ball as it rebounds off the wall or partner, and immediately repeat the movement.
Continue for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The medicine ball chest pass is an explosive upper body exercise that targets the pectorals, shoulders, and triceps. It involves forcefully passing a medicine ball from the chest, often against a wall or to a partner, and catching it on the rebound.

name: medicine ball chest push from 3 point stance
instructions: Stand with your feet staggered and hinge at the hips, reaching down with your hands to the medicine ball on the ground in front of you.
Pick up the ball and drive up through your legs and hips, bringing the ball to your chest as you stand tall.
Explosively push the medicine ball straight out in front of you, extending your arms fully.
Return to the bent-over starting position with the ball on the ground and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The medicine ball chest push from a 3 point stance is a dynamic exercise targeting the pectoral muscles, with additional engagement of the shoulders, triceps and legs. It involves starting bent over at the hips with the medicine ball on the ground, rising explosively, and pushing the ball away from the chest.

name: medicine ball chest push multiple response
instructions: Kneel upright with your knees hip-width apart, holding a medicine ball at chest level.
Explosively push the medicine ball forward and release it, letting your body fall forward.
Catch yourself on your hands with your elbows slightly bent to absorb the landing.
Push back up to the kneeling position, retrieve the ball and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: An explosive chest exercise performed kneeling with a medicine ball. The ball is thrown forward from the chest and the body falls forward to land on the hands, then returns to kneeling for repeated responses, engaging the pectorals, triceps, and shoulders.

name: medicine ball chest push single response
instructions: Kneel upright with your knees hip-width apart, holding the medicine ball at chest level.
Explosively push the medicine ball forward and release it, letting your body fall forward.
Land on your hands in a push-up position, bending your elbows to absorb the impact.
Push back up to the kneeling position, retrieve the ball and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The medicine ball chest push single response is an explosive exercise that targets the pectoral muscles by throwing a medicine ball from the chest while kneeling, engaging the triceps and shoulders as secondary muscles. After the throw, the body falls forward and lands in a push-up position.

name: plyo push up
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your body in a straight line.
Push explosively off the ground, using your chest muscles to propel your upper body off the ground.
Land softly with your hands back in the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The plyo push up is an explosive bodyweight exercise that targets the pectoral muscles and also works the triceps, shoulders, and core. It involves pushing off the ground with enough force for your hands to leave the floor, requiring power, coordination, and upper body strength.

name: push up on bosu ball
instructions: Place the bosu ball on the ground with the dome side facing up.
Position yourself in a push-up position with your hands on top of the dome, about shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and lower your body down towards the bosu ball by bending your elbows.
Push yourself back up to the starting position by extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: A push-up variation performed with hands on a BOSU ball (dome side up), increasing instability and core engagement.

name: smith wide grip bench press
instructions: Adjust the bench to a comfortable position on the smith machine.
Lie down on the bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the barbell with a wide grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows out to the sides.
Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith wide grip bench press is a chest exercise performed on a smith machine with a wide grip to target the pectoral muscles. It also engages the triceps and shoulders as secondary muscles. The smith machine provides stability, making it accessible to those with less experience, but proper form and control are still required.

name: smith wide grip decline bench press
instructions: Adjust the decline bench to the desired angle.
Lie down on the bench with your feet secured under the foot pads.
Grasp the barbell with a wide grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows pointed outwards.
Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith wide grip decline bench press is a chest exercise performed on a smith machine with a wide grip, targeting the lower pectorals and also engaging the triceps and shoulders. The decline angle and wide grip emphasize the lower chest and require good control and technique.

name: weighted drop push up
instructions: Place two benches parallel, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and start in a high plank with your hands on the benches and a weight plate on your upper back.
Remove your hands from the benches and drop down, landing with your hands on the floor between them.
Absorb the landing by bending your elbows and lowering your chest towards the floor.
Push explosively off the floor to bring your hands back onto the benches.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted drop push up is an advanced plyometric chest exercise in which you drop from two benches to the floor and push back up, performed with a weight plate on your back for increased resistance. This movement challenges strength, power, coordination, and control, making it suitable for experienced individuals.

name: wide hand push up
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to toe.
Lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, letting them move out to the sides.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The wide hand push up is a bodyweight exercise that targets the pectoral muscles by increasing the distance between the hands, placing more emphasis on the chest compared to a standard push up. It also engages the triceps and shoulders as secondary muscles.

name: medicine ball chest push with run release
instructions: Stand with your feet staggered and hinge at the hips, reaching down with your hands to the medicine ball on the ground in front of you.
Pick up the ball and drive up through your legs and hips, bringing the ball to your chest as you stand tall.
Explosively push the medicine ball straight out in front of you, extending your arms fully and releasing it.
Retrieve the ball, return to the bent-over starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: A dynamic exercise that combines a hip hinge with an explosive chest push, targeting the pectorals while also engaging the triceps, shoulders, legs, and core. This movement requires coordination and explosive power.

name: lever unilateral row
instructions: Place one knee on the machine pad and stand on the other foot, bending forward at the hips and supporting yourself with one hand on the front support.
Grasp the handle with your free hand and keep your back straight.
Pull the handle towards your hip, squeezing your shoulder blade towards your spine.
Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement, then slowly release and extend your arm back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The lever unilateral row is a machine-based exercise targeting the upper back. It involves pulling a lever arm with one side of the body at a time, focusing on the upper back muscles while also engaging the biceps and forearms. This exercise is performed on a leverage machine, providing stability and controlled resistance.

name: back extension on exercise ball
instructions: Place the stability ball on the ground and lie face down on top of it, with your hips resting on the ball and your feet against a wall or other stable surface.
Position your hands behind your head or crossed over your chest.
Engage your core and slowly lift your upper body off the ball, extending your back until your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The back extension on an exercise ball is a bodyweight exercise that targets the spinal erectors and helps strengthen the lower back. It also engages the glutes and hamstrings as secondary muscles. The use of a stability ball requires core engagement and balance, making it more challenging than a standard floor back extension.

name: barbell bent arm pullover
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your head at one end and your feet on the floor.
Hold a barbell with a shoulder-width grip and extend your arms straight above your chest.
Lower the barbell behind your head while keeping your arms slightly bent.
Pause for a moment, then raise the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The barbell bent arm pullover is a compound exercise that targets the lats, with secondary emphasis on the triceps and chest. It involves lying on a bench and moving a barbell in an arc over and behind the head, requiring control and strength.

name: barbell reverse grip incline bench row
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench facing the backrest with your chest against it.
Grab the barbell with a reverse grip (palms facing down) and hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Pull the barbell towards your upper abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The barbell reverse grip incline bench row targets the upper back and also engages the biceps and forearms. It is performed on an incline bench with a reverse grip on the barbell, focusing on pulling the weight towards the upper abdomen while maintaining a strong, stable posture.

name: cable incline bench row
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle and attach a cable handle to the low pulley.
Sit on the bench facing the cable machine with your feet flat on the floor and your knees slightly bent.
Grasp the cable handle with an overhand grip and extend your arms fully in front of you.
Lean forward from your hips while keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the cable handle towards your chest by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
Squeeze your back muscles at the top of the movement, then slowly extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable incline bench row is a strength exercise targeting the upper back, performed using a cable machine and an incline bench. It also engages the biceps and rear deltoids as secondary muscles.

name: cable palm rotational row
instructions: Attach a handle to a cable machine at waist height.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handle with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Step back to create tension on the cable, keeping your back straight and knees slightly bent.
Pull the handle towards your body, rotating your palms to face upwards as you do so.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
Slowly release the handle back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable palm rotational row is a cable-based exercise targeting the upper back, with secondary emphasis on the biceps and forearms. It involves pulling a cable handle towards the body while rotating the palms, engaging the upper back muscles and improving grip strength.

name: cable rope crossover seated row
instructions: Sit on the rowing machine with your feet flat on the footrests and your knees slightly bent.
Grasp the cable ropes with an overhand grip, palms facing each other.
Lean back slightly, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the cable ropes towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable rope crossover seated row is a strength exercise targeting the upper back, performed on a cable machine using rope attachments. It also engages the biceps and forearms as secondary muscles.

name: cable rope elevated seated row
instructions: Sit on the elevated seat facing the cable machine.
Grab the cable rope handles with an overhand grip, palms facing each other.
Keep your back straight and lean slightly back, maintaining a slight bend in your knees.
Pull the cable towards your body by retracting your shoulder blades and squeezing your back muscles.
Pause for a moment at the fully contracted position.
Slowly release the tension and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable rope elevated seated row is a strength exercise targeting the upper back, performed on an elevated seat using a cable machine with rope handles. It emphasizes scapular retraction and upper back engagement while also working the biceps and forearms.

name: cable rope extension incline bench row
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle and attach a cable machine to the low pulley.
Attach a rope handle to the cable machine and sit on the incline bench facing the machine.
Grab the rope handle with an overhand grip and lean forward, keeping your back straight.
Extend your arms fully, pulling the rope towards your upper chest while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
Slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable rope extension incline bench row targets the upper back using a cable machine and an incline bench. It requires pulling a rope attachment towards the upper chest while seated on an incline bench, emphasizing scapular retraction and upper back engagement.

name: cable rope seated row
instructions: Sit on the rowing machine with your feet flat on the footrests and knees slightly bent.
Grasp the cable ropes with an overhand grip, palms facing each other.
Keep your back straight and lean slightly forward, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Pull the cable ropes towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable rope seated row is a strength exercise targeting the upper back, performed using a cable machine with rope attachment. It also engages the biceps and forearms as secondary muscles.

name: cable upper row
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a cable machine at chest height and sit on a bench facing the machine.
Plant your feet on the floor in front of you.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the bar towards your upper chest, raising your elbows out to the sides and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement.
Slowly release the bar back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable upper row is a compound exercise targeting the upper back, performed using a cable machine and a straight bar. It involves pulling the bar towards the upper chest, engaging the upper back, biceps, and shoulders.

name: cable wide grip rear pulldown behind neck
instructions: Adjust the cable machine so that the pulldown bar is at a height above your head.
Sit down on the seat and grab the pulldown bar with a wide overhand grip.
Keep your back straight and your head slightly forward.
Pull the bar down behind your head towards the base of your neck, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly release the bar back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable wide grip rear pulldown behind neck is a strength exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi (lats) and also engaging the biceps, rhomboids, and rear deltoids. It involves pulling a cable bar behind the neck while seated, requiring good shoulder mobility and control.

name: chin-up
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with your palms facing towards you and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The chin-up is a bodyweight exercise that targets the latissimus dorsi (lats) and also works the biceps and forearms. It involves pulling your body up towards a bar with an underhand grip until your chin clears the bar.

name: close grip chin-up
instructions: Grab the pull-up bar with your palms facing towards you and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your feet off the ground.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The close grip chin-up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the lats, with significant involvement of the biceps and forearms. It requires pulling your body up to a bar with a close, underhand grip, emphasizing upper body strength.

name: dumbbell lying rear delt row
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with your feet on the floor and a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.
Extend your arms straight down towards the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Engaging your back muscles, lift the dumbbells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell lying rear delt row targets the upper back and rear deltoids, performed while lying face down on an incline bench and rowing dumbbells upward.

name: dumbbell palm rotational bent over row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your knees slightly bent.
Let your arms hang straight down, palms facing your body.
Engage your core and pull the dumbbells up towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
As you pull the dumbbells up, rotate your palms so they face away from your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position, rotating your palms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell palm rotational bent over row is a compound exercise targeting the upper back, with additional engagement of the biceps and forearms. The rotational component adds a coordination challenge and increases muscle activation.

name: dumbbell reverse grip incline bench one arm row
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Lie face down on the bench with your chest against the pad and your feet on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with a reverse grip (palm facing forward), arm hanging straight down.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the dumbbell up towards your chest, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Squeeze your back muscles at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Switch sides and repeat the exercise with your left arm.
description: The dumbbell reverse grip incline bench one arm row is a strength exercise targeting the upper back, performed on an incline bench using a single dumbbell and a reverse grip.

name: dumbbell reverse grip incline bench two arm row
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Lie face down on the bench with your chest against the backrest and your toes or feet on the ground.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip.
Let your arms hang straight down, fully extended.
Pull the dumbbells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell reverse grip incline bench two arm row is a strength exercise targeting the upper back, performed on an incline bench with dumbbells using an underhand grip. It also engages the biceps and forearms.

name: exercise ball alternating arm ups
instructions: Lie face down over the stability ball with your torso on the ball and your feet on the ground behind you.
Place both hands on the floor in front of the ball, arms straight.
Engage your core and slowly raise one arm straight forward until it is in line with your body, keeping the other hand on the floor.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arm back down to the floor.
Repeat the movement with the other arm.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
description: This exercise targets the latissimus dorsi (lats) and involves alternating straight-arm raises while lying face down over a stability ball, engaging the core and shoulders for balance and control.

name: exercise ball back extension with arms extended
instructions: Place the stability ball on the ground and kneel behind it, resting your hips and torso face down on the ball with your knees on the floor.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you, with your palms facing down.
Engage your core and slowly lift your upper body off the ball, keeping your back straight and your neck in line with your spine.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The exercise ball back extension with arms extended targets the spinal erectors and helps strengthen the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings. It requires balance and core engagement due to the instability of the ball and the extended arm position.

name: exercise ball back extension with hands behind head
instructions: Place the stability ball on the ground and lie face down on top of it with your hips resting on the ball.
Position your feet against a wall or other stable surface for support.
Cross your arms behind your head, with your hands touching the back of your head.
Engage your core and slowly lift your upper body off the ball, extending your back until your body forms a straight line from your head to your hips.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: This exercise targets the spinal erectors and involves performing back extensions while lying face down on a stability ball, with hands placed behind the head for increased difficulty. It also engages the glutes and hamstrings as secondary muscles.

name: exercise ball back extension with knees off ground
instructions: Place the stability ball on the ground and lie face down on top of it, with your hips resting on the ball and your feet against a wall for stability.
Position your hands behind your head or crossed over your chest.
Engage your core and slowly lift your upper body off the ball, extending your back until your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: This exercise targets the spinal erectors and requires you to perform a back extension while balancing your hips on a stability ball with your knees off the ground. It challenges your core, glutes, and hamstrings, and requires balance and coordination.

name: exercise ball back extension with rotation
instructions: Start by lying face down on the stability ball with your hips resting on the ball and your feet firmly planted on the ground.
Place your hands behind your head or cross them over your chest.
Engage your core and slowly lift your upper body off the ball, extending your back until your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly rotate your torso to one side, keeping your hips and legs stable.
Return to the center and repeat the rotation to the other side.
Lower your upper body back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The exercise ball back extension with rotation is a movement that targets the spinal erectors and involves extending the back while lying face down on a stability ball, then adding a rotational component to engage the obliques and improve core stability.

name: exercise ball hug
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and the stability ball in front of you, against your shins.
Wrap your arms around the ball, hugging it close to your chest.
Slowly round your back and lower your chest and head over the ball.
Continue rounding until you feel a stretch along your back muscles.
Hold the position for a few seconds, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The exercise ball hug is a gentle stretch performed hugging a stability ball, focusing on stretching and mobilizing the spine by rounding the back over the ball. It is suitable for improving flexibility and mobility in the back, with secondary engagement of the shoulders and chest.

name: exercise ball lat stretch
instructions: Kneel on the floor with the stability ball in front of you.
Place your forearms or hands on top of the ball, arms extended.
Slowly roll the ball forward and sit your hips back, sinking your chest toward the floor until you feel a stretch in your lats.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The exercise ball lat stretch is a flexibility movement that targets the latissimus dorsi muscles. It involves kneeling with your arms on a stability ball and rolling it forward to sink the chest toward the floor, providing a deep stretch to the lats and shoulders.

name: exercise ball lower back stretch (pyramid)
instructions: Kneel behind the stability ball and lie face down over it with your stomach and hips on top of the ball.
Straighten your legs with your toes on the floor behind you.
Place your hands on the floor in front of the ball.
Relax and let your back round over the ball, feeling a stretch in your lower back and lats.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: A stretch performed on a stability ball to target the lower back and lats, also engaging the glutes and hamstrings. It involves draping your torso face down over the ball with hands and feet on the floor, letting the back round into a pyramid shape.

name: exercise ball lying side lat stretch
instructions: Lie on your side over the stability ball so that your hip and the side of your torso rest on it, with your legs extended and staggered on the floor.
Place your bottom hand on the floor or the ball for stability.
Reach your top arm overhead and allow your torso to rotate slightly.
Feel the stretch in your lat muscles on the side of your body.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides and repeat.
description: A stretch performed lying on your side over a stability ball to target the lat muscles, with additional stretching for the shoulders and triceps.

name: exercise ball prone leg raise
instructions: Lie face down over the stability ball with your hips on the ball and your legs extended behind you, toes on the floor.
Place your hands on the ground, shoulder-width apart, and engage your core muscles.
Keeping your leg straight, slowly lift one leg off the ground, using your lower back and glutes to raise it as high as possible.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your leg back down and repeat with the other leg.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The exercise ball prone leg raise is performed by lying face down with your hips on a stability ball and your hands on the floor. You lift one straight leg at a time using your lower back and glutes, targeting the spine and core stabilizers.

name: ez bar reverse grip bent over row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Hold the ez barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and hands shoulder-width apart.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up, until your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
Pull the ez barbell towards your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the ez barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The EZ bar reverse grip bent over row is a compound exercise targeting the upper back, with secondary emphasis on the biceps and forearms. It involves pulling an EZ barbell towards the lower chest while bent over, using an underhand grip.

name: kettlebell two arm row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a kettlebell in each hand with your palms facing your body.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the kettlebells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the kettlebells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kettlebell two arm row is a compound exercise targeting the upper back, performed by pulling two kettlebells towards the chest while maintaining a bent-over position.

name: kneeling lat stretch
instructions: Start on all fours with your knees hip-width apart and your hands on the floor in front of your shoulders.
Walk your hands slightly forward and keep your arms extended.
Keeping your hands in place, slowly sit your hips back toward your heels and lower your chest toward the floor, feeling a stretch in your lats.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kneeling lat stretch is a bodyweight exercise that targets the latissimus dorsi (lats) and helps improve flexibility and mobility in the upper back and shoulders. It is performed on all fours by sitting the hips back toward the heels while keeping the arms extended forward on the floor.

name: lever one arm lateral wide pulldown
instructions: Adjust the seat height and sit on the machine with your thighs secured under the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handle overhead with an overhand grip and fully extend your arm, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pull the handle straight down towards the side of your shoulder, squeezing your lat muscle at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly return the handle to the starting position, fully extending your arm.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The lever one arm lateral wide pulldown is a machine-based exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi, performed one arm at a time for unilateral strength and muscle development.

name: lever reverse grip vertical row
instructions: Adjust the seat height and footplate position to ensure proper alignment.
Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the footplate.
Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever reverse grip vertical row is a machine-based exercise targeting the upper back, with secondary emphasis on the biceps and forearms. It involves pulling handles with an underhand grip while seated, focusing on squeezing the shoulder blades together.

name: lever reverse t-bar row
instructions: Adjust the chest pad and footplate position on the leverage machine.
Stand on the footplates and lean forward with your chest against the inclined pad.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever reverse t-bar row is a machine-based exercise targeting the upper back. It involves pulling handles towards the chest while leaning on an inclined chest pad, emphasizing scapular retraction and upper back engagement.

name: lever seated row
instructions: Adjust the seat height and footrests to a comfortable position.
Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet on the footrests.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement.
Slowly release the handles and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever seated row is a machine-based exercise targeting the upper back. It involves pulling handles towards the torso while seated, focusing on squeezing the shoulder blades together.

name: lever t-bar reverse grip row
instructions: Stand on the machine platform with your feet shoulder-width apart and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back flat.
Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, about shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever t-bar reverse grip row is a machine-based exercise targeting the upper back, with secondary emphasis on the biceps and forearms. It involves pulling a lever towards the chest from a bent-over standing position, promoting upper back strength and muscle development.

name: lower back curl
instructions: Lie flat on your stomach with your legs extended and your arms by your sides.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings, and slowly lift your upper body off the ground, curling your back upwards.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lower back curl is a bodyweight exercise that targets the muscles of the lower back (spine) and also engages the glutes and hamstrings. It involves lying face down and curling the upper body off the ground by contracting the lower back muscles.

name: medicine ball catch and overhead throw
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing a wall or partner, with your arms ready to catch the ball.
Catch the medicine ball with both hands, bending at the hips and knees to absorb it.
Bring the ball up and back behind your head with your arms extended, keeping your core engaged.
Explosively pull your arms forward and down, throwing the ball in front of you.
Catch the ball on the rebound or from your partner, absorbing it with your hips and knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The medicine ball catch and overhead throw is a dynamic exercise targeting the lats, shoulders, and core. It involves catching a medicine ball low, bringing it behind your head, and explosively throwing it forward and down, combining elements of strength and power.

name: medicine ball overhead slam
