instructions: Kneel on the seat of the lat pulldown machine facing away from it, with your ankles hooked under the thigh roller.
Keep your body straight from knees to head, hips extended, hands in front of your chest.
Slowly lower your torso forward toward a step or the floor in front of you, resisting with your hamstrings.
Catch yourself with your hands at the bottom.
Push lightly with your hands and pull with your hamstrings to return to the upright kneeling position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The inverse leg curl (on pull-up cable machine) is a kneeling Nordic hamstring curl that uses the lat pulldown seat and thigh roller to anchor the ankles. It targets the hamstrings, with secondary emphasis on the glutes and calves.

name: dumbbell biceps curl (with arm blaster)
instructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your upper arms stationary.
Exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell biceps curl (with arm blaster) is an isolation exercise targeting the biceps, using a specialized arm blaster to maintain strict form and minimize shoulder involvement. This exercise is performed with dumbbells and emphasizes biceps strength and hypertrophy.

name: dumbbell hammer curls (with arm blaster)
instructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your torso.
Keep your elbows against the arm blaster and your palms facing your torso throughout the movement.
This will be your starting position.
Now, while holding your upper arm stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell hammer curl with arm blaster is an isolation exercise targeting the biceps and forearms. The arm blaster helps maintain proper form by preventing the elbows from moving forward, increasing biceps activation.

name: dumbbell alternate biceps curl (with arm blaster)
instructions: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Place the arm blaster on your upper arms, ensuring a secure fit.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl one dumbbell up towards your shoulder while contracting your biceps.
Continue to raise the dumbbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with the opposite arm.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell alternate biceps curl (with arm blaster) is an isolation exercise targeting the biceps, using an arm blaster to maintain strict form and minimize shoulder involvement. This exercise is performed by alternately curling dumbbells while keeping the upper arms stationary against the arm blaster.

name: ez-bar biceps curl (with arm blaster)
instructions: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the ez barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Place your upper arms against the arm blaster, keeping them stationary throughout the exercise.
Keeping your elbows close to your body, exhale and curl the barbell up towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The EZ-bar biceps curl (with arm blaster) is a strength exercise targeting the biceps, using an EZ barbell and an arm blaster to isolate the upper arms and minimize cheating. It is performed standing, with the upper arms stabilized against the arm blaster, curling the barbell upward and then lowering it under control.

name: cable triceps pushdown (v-bar) (with arm blaster)
instructions: Attach a v-bar attachment to the cable machine at the highest setting.
Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the v-bar with an overhand grip, palms facing down, and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary throughout the exercise.
Engage your triceps and exhale as you push the v-bar down until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, squeezing your triceps.
Inhale as you slowly return the v-bar to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable triceps pushdown (v-bar) with arm blaster is an isolation exercise targeting the triceps, performed using a cable machine and a v-bar attachment. The arm blaster helps keep the upper arms stationary, increasing triceps engagement.

name: cable reverse grip triceps pushdown (sz-bar) (with arm blaster)
instructions: Attach a straight bar to the cable machine at the highest setting.
Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary throughout the exercise.
Engage your triceps and slowly push the bar down until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly return the bar to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable reverse grip triceps pushdown (sz-bar) with arm blaster is an isolation exercise targeting the triceps, using a cable machine and an underhand grip for increased emphasis on the triceps' long head. The arm blaster helps keep the upper arms stationary, improving form and muscle engagement.

name: barbell biceps curl (with arm blaster)
instructions: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Place your upper arms against the arm blaster, keeping your elbows close to your torso.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to raise the barbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Inhale and slowly begin to lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The barbell biceps curl with arm blaster is a strength exercise that isolates the biceps by preventing elbow movement and reducing cheating. The arm blaster helps maintain proper form, making the exercise more effective for targeting the biceps.

name: barbell standing concentration curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is close to parallel with the floor and let your arms hang straight down.
Keeping your upper arms still, curl the barbell toward your chest.
Squeeze your biceps at the top for a moment.
Slowly lower the barbell until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The barbell standing concentration curl is an isolation exercise targeting the biceps: bent over at the hips with your arms hanging, you curl a barbell with both hands toward your chest, which removes momentum and emphasizes strict contraction.

name: frog crunch
instructions: Lie flat on your back and lift your legs, bringing the soles of your feet together with your knees out to the sides.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Engaging your abs, curl your upper body up while drawing your knees toward your chest.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The frog crunch is a bodyweight abdominal exercise that targets the abs and also engages the hip flexors. It is performed lying on your back, curling your torso up while keeping your feet together and knees bent.

name: ez-bar close-grip bench press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Grasp the ez barbell with a close grip, hands shoulder-width apart, palms facing forward.
Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Slowly lower the barbell towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The EZ-bar close-grip bench press is a compound upper body exercise that primarily targets the triceps, with secondary emphasis on the chest and shoulders. It is performed lying on a bench, using a close grip on an EZ barbell to emphasize triceps activation.

name: tire flip
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing the tire.
Bend your knees and hinge at the hips, lowering into a squat position.
Reach down and grab the bottom edge of the tire with both hands, fingers facing towards you.
Engage your glutes and leg muscles, and explosively drive through your legs to lift the tire off the ground.
As the tire flips over, use your upper body strength to guide it and maintain control.
Once the tire is fully flipped, quickly step back and reset your stance.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The tire flip is a full-body, explosive strength exercise that primarily targets the glutes, with significant involvement from the hamstrings, quadriceps, and core. It requires lifting and flipping a heavy tire, demanding power, coordination, and proper technique to perform safely.

name: chest dip on straight bar
instructions: Grab the parallel bars with your palms facing down and your arms fully extended.
Bend your knees and cross your ankles.
Lower your body by bending your arms until your shoulders are below your elbows.
Push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The chest dip on a straight bar is a bodyweight exercise that targets the pectoral muscles, with secondary emphasis on the triceps and shoulders. It requires significant upper body strength, stability, and control.

name: cable thibaudeau kayak row
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley and grab it with an overhand grip, hands wider than shoulder-width.
Stand facing the machine, take a step back and extend your arms up toward the pulley.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Pull the bar down and diagonally toward your right hip, tilting it like a paddle.
Return under control to the starting position.
Repeat toward your left hip, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable Thibaudeau kayak row is a standing high-pulley exercise that targets the lats: holding a bar with both hands, you pull it diagonally down to one hip and then the other, mimicking a kayak paddle stroke.

name: bridge - mountain climber (cross body)
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Engage your core and lift your right foot off the ground, bringing your right knee towards your left elbow.
Return your right foot to the starting position and repeat the movement with your left foot towards your right elbow.
Continue alternating sides, moving at a controlled pace.
Keep your hips level and avoid lifting your hips too high or sagging them too low.
Maintain a steady breathing pattern throughout the exercise.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The bridge - mountain climber (cross body) is a dynamic bodyweight exercise that targets the abs while also engaging the glutes, quadriceps, hamstrings, shoulders, and triceps. It combines core stabilization with a cross-body knee drive, challenging both strength and coordination.

name: dumbbell lying on floor rear delt raise
instructions: Lie on your side on the floor with your head resting on your lower arm and your knees slightly bent.
Hold a dumbbell in your top hand in front of your chest, arm nearly straight.
Raise the dumbbell up and back until your arm points toward the ceiling, keeping a slight bend in the elbow.
Pause, then slowly lower it back in front of your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The dumbbell lying on floor rear delt raise is an isolation exercise for the rear deltoid: lying on your side, you raise one dumbbell from in front of your chest up toward the ceiling.

name: seated piriformis stretch
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet flat on the floor.
Cross your right ankle over your left knee.
Keeping your back straight, lean your torso forward from the hips until you feel a stretch in your right glute.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
description: The seated piriformis stretch targets the glutes and helps relieve tension in the piriformis. It is performed seated on a bench with one ankle crossed over the opposite knee, leaning forward to stretch the gluteal region.

name: rocking frog stretch
instructions: Get on your hands and knees on a mat.
Slide your knees out wide and turn your feet out, keeping your ankles in line with your knees.
Lower onto your forearms.
Slowly rock your hips back toward your heels until you feel a stretch in your inner thighs.
Rock forward again to the starting position.
Keep your back neutral throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The rocking frog stretch is a dynamic hip mobility exercise: on your forearms with your knees wide apart, you rock your hips back toward your heels and forward again to open the adductors and hips.

name: lever horizontal one leg press
instructions: Adjust the seat of the machine so that your knees are at a 90-degree angle when your feet are on the footplate.
Sit with your back against the backrest, place one foot in the middle of the footplate and rest the other foot on the lower footrest.
Place your hands on the handles or sides of the machine for stability.
Push the footplate away from your body by extending your leg, keeping your back against the backrest.
Pause for a moment at the fully extended position, then slowly bend your leg to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The lever horizontal one leg press is a lower body strength exercise performed on a leverage machine. It primarily targets the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. The exercise involves pressing a footplate away from the body using one leg at a time, which increases the demand for unilateral strength and stability.

name: jump rope
instructions: Hold the handles of the jump rope with your hands, palms facing inward.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Swing the rope over your head and jump over it as it comes towards your feet.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and repeat the jump as the rope comes around again.
Continue jumping for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
description: Jump rope is a cardiovascular exercise that involves continuously jumping over a swinging rope. It primarily targets the cardiovascular system while also engaging the calves, quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes.

name: cable lateral pulldown with v-bar
instructions: Sit down on the cable pulldown machine and grab the v-bar attachment with an overhand grip.
Adjust the knee pad so that your thighs are secured under it.
Keep your back straight and lean back slightly.
Pull the v-bar down towards your upper chest while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your back muscles at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly return the v-bar to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable lateral pulldown with v-bar is a strength exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi (lats) using a cable machine and v-bar attachment. It also engages the biceps and forearms as secondary muscles.

name: dumbbell lying pronation on floor
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your elbow on the floor and your forearm pointing up.
Start with your palm facing your head.
Rotate your forearm so your palm turns to face away from you, keeping your elbow still.
Slowly rotate back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
description: The dumbbell lying pronation on floor targets the forearm pronators: lying on your back with your elbow on the floor and your forearm vertical, you rotate the dumbbell so your palm turns away from you.

name: dumbbell lying supination on floor
instructions: Lie on your side on the floor with your head supported.
Hold a dumbbell in your top hand with your upper arm along your body and your elbow bent at 90 degrees, palm facing down.
Keeping your elbow still, rotate your forearm until your palm faces up.
Slowly rotate back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The dumbbell lying supination on floor is an isolation exercise for the forearm supinators: lying on your side with your elbow bent, you rotate the dumbbell from palm down to palm up.

name: lever reverse grip lateral pulldown
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your knees under the pads and your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Sit upright with your chest out and shoulders back, maintaining a slight arch in your lower back.
Pull the handles down towards your chest, leading with your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly release the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever reverse grip lateral pulldown is a machine-based exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi (lats) with a reverse (underhand) grip, also engaging the biceps, rhomboids, and rear deltoids. It is performed on a leverage machine, making it accessible and safe for most users.

name: ez-barbell standing wide grip biceps curl
instructions: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the ez barbell with an underhand grip, hands wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your upper arms stationary throughout the movement.
Curl the barbell up towards your shoulders by contracting your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The EZ-barbell standing wide grip biceps curl is a strength exercise targeting the biceps, with secondary emphasis on the forearms. It involves curling an EZ barbell with a wide grip while standing.

name: dumbbell step-up lunge
instructions: Place two benches about a long stride apart and stand between them with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your sides.
Rest the top of your left foot on the bench behind you.
Step your right foot up onto the bench in front of you.
Lower your body into a deep split squat until your right thigh is about parallel to the bench.
Push through your right heel to rise, then step your right foot back down to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The dumbbell step-up lunge is a compound lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps while also engaging the glutes, hamstrings and calves. With your rear foot on a bench behind you, you step your front foot up onto a second bench and lower into a deep split squat, holding dumbbells.

name: barbell squat jump step rear lunge
instructions: Stand in front of a low step with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back.
Lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
Explode upward and jump onto the step.
Land softly and immediately step back off the step with one leg into a reverse lunge.
Lower your body down until your front thigh is parallel to the ground, keeping your back straight.
Push through your front heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat the jump and lunge sequence on the other leg.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The barbell squat jump step rear lunge is a dynamic lower body exercise that combines a squat jump with a reverse lunge, performed while holding a barbell across the upper back. This movement targets the quadriceps, glutes, hamstrings, and calves, and requires strength, coordination, and balance.

name: barbell sitted alternate leg raise
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and lean your torso back slightly.
Hold a barbell overhead with your arms straight, hands shoulder-width apart.
Keeping your arms and core tight, raise one straight leg as high as you can.
Lower it under control and repeat with the other leg, alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The barbell sitted alternate leg raise is an abdominal and hip flexor exercise performed seated on the floor, leaning back slightly while holding a barbell overhead with straight arms and alternately raising each straight leg.

name: barbell sitted alternate leg raise (female)
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and lean your torso back slightly.
Hold a barbell overhead with your arms straight, hands shoulder-width apart.
Keeping your arms and core tight, raise one straight leg as high as you can.
Lower it under control.
Repeat with the other leg, alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The barbell sitted alternate leg raise (female) is an abdominal and hip flexor exercise performed seated on the floor, leaning back slightly while holding a barbell overhead with straight arms and alternately raising each straight leg.

name: twisted leg raise (female)
instructions: Stand in a captain's chair (vertical knee raise station) with your forearms on the pads, gripping the handles, and your back against the backrest.
Let your legs hang straight down and brace your core.
Raise one straight leg forward and slightly across your body to hip height.
Lower it under control.
Repeat with the other leg, raising it slightly across toward the opposite side.
Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The twisted leg raise (female) is an abdominal exercise performed in a captain's chair that targets the abs, obliques and hip flexors: you raise one straight leg forward and slightly across your body, alternating sides.

name: twisted leg raise
instructions: Stand in a captain's chair (vertical knee raise station) with your forearms on the pads, gripping the handles, and your back against the backrest.
Let your legs hang straight down and brace your core.
Raise one straight leg forward and slightly across your body to hip height.
Lower it under control.
Repeat with the other leg, raising it slightly across toward the opposite side.
Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
Keep your back against the pad and avoid swinging.
description: The twisted leg raise is a bodyweight exercise performed in a captain's chair, targeting the abs with emphasis on the obliques and hip flexors: you raise one straight leg forward and slightly across your body, alternating sides.

name: dumbbell supported squat
instructions: Stand in front of a box with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding one dumbbell vertically at your chest.
Keeping your chest up and core engaged, slowly lower your body down by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
Continue lowering until you sit lightly on the box.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell supported squat is a lower body exercise targeting the quadriceps, with additional activation of the glutes, hamstrings, and calves. Holding one dumbbell at your chest, you squat down to a box behind you, which guides depth and adds stability.

name: dumbbell single leg deadlift with stepbox support
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand.
Place your left foot on a stepbox or elevated surface behind you.
Keeping your back straight and core engaged, hinge forward at the hips, lowering the dumbbell towards the ground.
As you lower the dumbbell, keep your left foot resting on the box for support.
Lower the dumbbell until you feel a stretch in your right hamstring, then return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
description: The dumbbell single leg deadlift with stepbox support is a unilateral lower body exercise that targets the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the hamstrings and lower back. It challenges balance, stability, and strength, making it suitable for those with some experience in weight training.

name: dumbbell sumo pull through
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointed outwards.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands in front of your body, arms extended.
Bend your knees and lower your hips down into a squat position, keeping your back straight.
Lower the dumbbell down between your legs, keeping your arms straight.
Drive through your heels and extend your hips forward, pulling the dumbbell up and in front of your body.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement, then lower the dumbbell back down between your legs.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The dumbbell sumo pull through is a lower body exercise that targets the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the hamstrings, quadriceps, and core. It involves a wide-stance squat and a hip hinge movement, using a dumbbell for resistance.

name: barbell split squat v. 2
instructions: Stand holding a barbell with an overhand grip in front of your hips, arms straight.
Take a large step forward with your right foot into a split stance, keeping your torso upright.
Lower your body by bending your knees and hips until your right thigh is parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment, then push through your right heel to rise, keeping your feet in place.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The barbell split squat v. 2 is a lower body strength exercise that targets the quadriceps, while also engaging the glutes, hamstrings, and calves. It is performed in a static split stance, holding a barbell in your hands in front of your hips.

name: dumbbell step-up split squat
instructions: Place two benches about a long stride apart and stand between them with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
Rest the top of your left foot on the bench behind you, right foot on the floor.
Lower into a split squat until your right thigh is about parallel to the floor, then push back up.
Step your right foot up onto the bench in front of you.
Lower into a split squat with both feet elevated, then push back up.
Step your right foot back down to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The dumbbell step-up split squat is a lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, with additional emphasis on the glutes, hamstrings and calves. With your rear foot on a bench, you alternate a Bulgarian split squat with the front foot on the floor and one with the front foot stepped up onto a second bench.

name: captains chair straight leg raise
instructions: Sit on the captain's chair with your back against the backrest and your forearms resting on the arm pads.
Keep your upper body stable and your back straight.
Engage your abs and lift your legs up in front of you, keeping them straight.
Continue lifting until your legs are parallel to the ground or as high as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The captain's chair straight leg raise is an abdominal exercise performed on a captain's chair apparatus. It primarily targets the abdominal muscles and also engages the hip flexors. The movement requires core strength and stability to lift and control the legs while keeping the upper body stable.

name: weighted close grip chin-up on dip cage
instructions: Stand in the dip cage and grab the overhead pull-up bar with an underhand grip, hands close together.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and the weight hanging between your legs, knees slightly bent.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up toward the bar, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar, then pause for a moment.
Slowly lower your body back down to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted close grip chin-up on dip cage is a challenging upper body exercise that targets the lats, with significant involvement from the biceps and forearms. It requires the use of additional weight, increasing the demand on strength and control.

name: resistance band seated hip abduction
instructions: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Wrap the resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
Place your hands on the sides of the chair or bench for support.
Engage your abductors (outer thigh muscles) and slowly push your knees apart, against the resistance of the band.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly bring your knees back together.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: A seated exercise using a resistance band to target the hip abductors by pushing the knees apart against resistance. This movement also engages the glutes and hamstrings.

name: resistance band leg extension
instructions: Sit on a bench with your knees bent and your feet under you.
Loop a resistance band around both ankles.
Keeping one foot in place, extend the other leg forward until the knee is straight.
Pause, squeezing your quadriceps, then slowly bend the knee back to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
description: The resistance band leg extension targets the quadriceps by extending the leg against the resistance of a band, helping to build strength and endurance in the upper legs.

name: ez bar lying bent arms pullover
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your head at one end and your feet on the floor.
Hold the EZ barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing away from you) and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Hold the barbell above your chest with your elbows bent at about 90 degrees.
Lower the barbell in an arc behind your head, keeping your elbows bent at the same angle.
Pause for a moment, then return the barbell to the starting position by reversing the arc motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The EZ bar lying bent arms pullover is a strength exercise targeting the lats, with secondary emphasis on the triceps and chest. It involves lying on a bench and moving the EZ barbell in an arc over and behind the head, requiring control and stability.

name: incline scapula push up
instructions: Place your hands on a flat bench, shoulder-width apart.
Walk your feet back into an incline plank with your body in a straight line.
Keep your elbows straight throughout the movement.
Let your chest sink by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Push the bench away to spread your shoulder blades and round your upper back slightly.
Pause briefly at each end of the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The incline scapula push up is a bodyweight exercise performed with your hands on a bench that primarily targets the serratus anterior. With your arms straight, you only move your shoulder blades, letting the chest sink between them and then pushing it away, to improve shoulder stability.

name: scapula dips
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench and place your hands on it beside your hips, fingers forward.
Slide your hips just off the bench, arms straight and feet on the floor.
Keeping your elbows locked, let your shoulders rise toward your ears so your body drops slightly.
Press your shoulders down away from your ears to lift your body.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Scapula dips are a bodyweight exercise targeting the traps and shoulder depressors: with your hands on a bench and your arms straight, you lift and lower your body using only your shoulder blades.

name: low glute bridge on floor
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place your arms by your sides, palms facing down.
Engage your glutes and core, then lift your hips off the ground until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your glutes.
Slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The low glute bridge on floor is a bodyweight exercise that targets the glutes while also engaging the hamstrings and core. It is performed by lying on your back, lifting your hips off the ground, and squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.

name: curl-up
instructions: Lie flat on your back with one knee bent and the other leg straight.
Place your hands under your lower back to support its natural curve.
Brace your abs and lift your head and shoulders slightly off the ground, keeping your neck neutral.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The curl-up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the abdominal muscles. It involves lying on your back with one knee bent and your hands under your lower back, and lifting only your head and shoulders slightly off the floor.

name: barbell pendlay row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your chest up.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Pull the barbell towards your upper abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The barbell Pendlay row is a strength exercise targeting the upper back, performed by pulling a barbell from the floor to the upper abdomen with strict form.

name: bench pull-ups
instructions: Place a flat bench behind a pull-up bar.
Grab the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Rest one foot on the bench behind you and let the other leg hang.
Pull yourself up until your chin is over the bar, using the foot on the bench only as needed.
Pause briefly at the top.
Slowly lower yourself until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Bench pull-ups are an assisted pull-up targeting the lats: you hang from an overhead bar and use one foot on a bench behind you to take some of your weight while you pull your chin over the bar. They also engage the biceps and forearms.

name: scapula push-up
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Keep your elbows straight throughout the movement.
Let your chest sink by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Push the floor away to spread your shoulder blades and round your upper back slightly.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The scapula push-up is a bodyweight exercise that targets the serratus anterior and helps improve scapular mobility and stability. It is performed in a high plank position, focusing on the movement of the shoulder blades rather than the elbows.

name: band fixed back underhand pulldown
instructions: Anchor a resistance band securely above head height.
Place a box or bench under the anchor and sit on it facing it.
Grab the band with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, arms extended overhead.
Keep your chest up and your core engaged.
Pull the band down toward your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your lats and shoulder blades at the bottom.
Pause for a moment.
Slowly let your arms return overhead with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band fixed back underhand pulldown is a resistance band exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi (lats) and also working the biceps, rhomboids, and rear deltoids. It mimics the motion of a traditional lat pulldown but uses a resistance band anchored above the head.

name: band fixed back close grip pulldown
instructions: Attach the band to a fixed point above you, such as a pull-up bar or sturdy beam.
Sit down on a bench or chair facing the band, with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent.
Grasp the band with a close grip, palms facing towards you.
Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Pull the band down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, feeling the contraction in your lats.
Slowly release the band back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The band fixed back close grip pulldown is an exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi (lats) using a resistance band anchored above the user. It mimics the traditional cable pulldown but uses a band for resistance, making it accessible and effective for building back strength.

name: potty squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Lower your body down by bending your knees and pushing your hips back as if you were sitting on a chair.
Keep your chest up and your back straight throughout the movement.
Lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the ground or as low as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The bodyweight squat (air squat) targets the quadriceps while also engaging the glutes and hamstrings. Standing with the arms reaching forward, squat down as if sitting on a chair, keeping the back straight and the chest up, then return to standing.

name: resistance band seated shoulder press
instructions: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Hold the resistance band with both hands, palms facing forward, and bring it up to shoulder level.
Press the band overhead, extending your arms fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the band back down to shoulder level.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The resistance band seated shoulder press is an overhead pressing exercise performed while seated, using a resistance band to target the deltoid muscles. It also engages the triceps and upper back as secondary muscles. This exercise is suitable for building shoulder strength and stability, and is accessible for most fitness levels due to the controlled movement and support provided by the seated position.

name: resistance band seated biceps curl
instructions: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Hold the resistance band with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and arms extended down by your sides.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the resistance band up towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the resistance band back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The resistance band seated biceps curl is an upper arm exercise that targets the biceps using a resistance band while seated, making it accessible and safe for most fitness levels.

name: resistance band seated chest press
instructions: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Hold the resistance band handles in each hand, with your palms facing down and elbows bent at a 90-degree angle.
Extend one arm forward, pushing the band away from your chest while the other hand stays at your chest.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Alternate arms for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The resistance band seated chest press is a chest-focused exercise performed while sitting, using a resistance band to provide tension. It targets the pectoral muscles and also works the shoulders and triceps. This movement is performed by pressing the band forward from the chest while seated, making it accessible and safe for most fitness levels.

name: potty squat with support
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Hold onto a stable support, such as a chair or wall, for balance.
Lower your body down into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
Keep your chest up and your back straight throughout the movement.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The potty squat with support is a bodyweight exercise targeting the glutes, performed with the assistance of a stable support for balance. It is suitable for those developing lower body strength and proper squat mechanics.

name: smith sumo squat
instructions: Set up the smith machine with the barbell at hip height.
Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing outwards.
Position yourself under the barbell, resting it on your upper back and shoulders.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you lower your body down into a squat position, pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith sumo squat is a lower body exercise performed on a smith machine, targeting the glutes with secondary emphasis on the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. The wide stance and guided bar path make it accessible for those developing squat technique and lower body strength.

name: resistance band seated straight back row
instructions: Sit on a bench with your back upright, legs extended, and loop the resistance band around your feet.
Hold the ends of the resistance band with your hands, palms facing each other.
Keep your back straight and lean slightly back, engaging your core.
Pull the resistance band towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The resistance band seated straight back row targets the upper back muscles and is performed seated with your legs extended and a resistance band looped around the feet. It emphasizes scapular retraction and upper back strength.

name: push-up plus
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Once your chest is just above the ground, push through your hands to extend your arms and lift your upper body up.
At the top of the movement, protract your shoulder blades by pushing your upper back towards the ceiling.
Pause for a moment, then reverse the movement by retracting your shoulder blades and lowering your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The push-up plus is a variation of the standard push-up that adds an extra movement at the top of the push-up by protracting the shoulder blades, which further engages the serratus anterior and improves shoulder stability.

name: pelvic tilt
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place your hands by your sides.
Engage your abs and tilt your pelvis upward, pressing your lower back into the ground.
Hold this position for a few seconds, focusing on contracting your abs.
Release the tilt and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The pelvic tilt is a bodyweight exercise that targets the abdominal muscles and helps improve core stability and lower back health. It is often used in rehabilitation and as a foundational movement for beginners.

name: bodyweight standing close-grip one arm row
instructions: Stand facing wall bars with your feet close to the base.
Grab a rung at chest height with one hand.
Lean back until your arm is straight, keeping your body in a straight line.
Pull your chest toward the bars by driving your elbow back and squeezing your shoulder blade.
Slowly lower back until your arm is fully extended, then repeat and switch arms.
description: The bodyweight standing close-grip one arm row is a unilateral exercise targeting the upper back: holding a wall-bar rung with one hand, you lean back and row your body toward the bars.

name: bodyweight standing close-grip row
instructions: Stand facing wall bars with your feet close to the base.
Grab a rung at chest height with both hands close together.
Lean back until your arms are straight, keeping your body in a straight line.
Pull your chest toward the bars by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Pause for a moment.
Slowly lower back until your arms are fully extended.
description: The bodyweight standing close-grip row targets the upper back using only body weight: holding a wall-bar rung with your hands close together, you lean back and row your body toward the bars, squeezing your shoulder blades together.

name: bodyweight standing one arm row (with towel)
instructions: Stand facing wall bars with your feet close to the base.
Grab both ends of a towel looped around a rung at chest height with one hand.
Lean back until your arm is straight, keeping your body in a straight line.
Pull your chest toward the bars by driving your elbow back and squeezing your shoulder blade.
Slowly lower back until your arm is fully extended, then repeat and switch arms.
description: A bodyweight exercise targeting the upper back: holding a towel looped around a wall-bar rung with one hand, you lean back and row your body toward the bars, engaging the biceps and forearms as secondary muscles.

name: bodyweight standing one arm row
instructions: Stand facing wall bars with your feet close to the base.
Grab a rung at chest height with one hand.
Lean back until your arm is straight, keeping your body in a straight line.
Brace your core and keep your hips from rotating.
Pull your chest toward the bars by driving your elbow back and squeezing your shoulder blade.
Pause for a moment.
Slowly lower back until your arm is fully extended, then repeat and switch arms.
description: The bodyweight standing one arm row is a unilateral exercise targeting the upper back: holding a wall-bar rung with one hand, you lean back and row your body toward the bars.

name: bodyweight standing row (with towel)
instructions: Loop a towel around a sturdy bar (such as a wall bar rung) at about waist height and hold one end in each hand.
Walk your feet close to the bar and lean back until your arms are fully extended, keeping your body straight.
Pull your chest towards the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lean back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The bodyweight standing row (with towel) is a back exercise that targets the upper back using a towel looped around a fixed bar. It also engages the biceps and shoulders. The movement is performed by leaning back and pulling your chest towards the anchor while keeping your body straight.

name: bodyweight standing row
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy bar (such as a wall bar rung) at about waist height, with your feet close to it.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip and lean back until your arms are fully extended, keeping your body straight.
Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Pull your chest towards the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement.
Slowly release and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The bodyweight standing row is a back exercise that targets the upper back using only body weight for resistance. It also engages the biceps and shoulders as secondary muscles. The movement involves pulling a bar or handles towards the body while standing, focusing on squeezing the shoulder blades together.

name: bodyweight squatting row (with towel)
instructions: Loop a towel around a sturdy bar (such as a wall bar rung) and hold one end in each hand, with your feet close to the bar.
Sit down into a deep squat and lean back until your arms are fully extended, keeping your back straight and your chest up.
Staying in the squat, pull your chest towards the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment, then slowly extend your arms and lean back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The bodyweight squatting row (with towel) is a compound exercise that targets the upper back while also engaging the biceps and shoulders. From a held squat, you row your body towards a towel looped around a fixed bar, making it a functional movement that develops strength and coordination.

name: bodyweight squatting row
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy bar (such as a wall bar rung) with your feet close to it and grab it with both hands.
Sit down into a deep squat and lean back until your arms are fully extended, keeping your back straight.
Staying in the squat, pull your chest towards the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment, then slowly extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The bodyweight squatting row is a compound exercise that targets the upper back while also engaging the biceps and shoulders. It combines a squatting motion with a rowing movement, requiring coordination and strength.

name: glute-ham raise
instructions: Adjust the glute-ham raise machine so your knees rest just behind the pad and your ankles are locked under the rollers.
Kneel upright on the pad with your body in a straight line from knees to head.
Cross your arms over your chest.
Keeping your hips extended, slowly lower your upper body forward by straightening your knees until your body is nearly parallel to the ground.
Engage your hamstrings and glutes to curl your body back up.
Continue until you return to the upright kneeling position, keeping a straight line from your knees to your head.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The glute-ham raise is a bodyweight exercise that primarily targets the hamstrings, with secondary emphasis on the glutes and lower back. It is performed on a glute-ham raise machine and requires significant strength and control to execute properly.

name: frankenstein squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, rest the barbell on the front of your shoulders and extend your arms straight forward without gripping the bar.
Keeping your back straight, lower your body by bending at the knees and hips, as if sitting back into a chair.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The Frankenstein squat is a variation of the squat where the barbell rests on the front of the shoulders while the arms stay extended straight forward without gripping it, challenging the glutes, quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. This exercise emphasizes posture, core stability, and lower body strength.

name: lever lying two-one leg curl
instructions: Adjust the machine and lie face down with your knees just off the edge of the pad.
Place the backs of your ankles under the lever pad.
Grasp the handles on the sides of the machine for support.
Keeping your hips pressed into the pad, exhale and curl both legs up towards your glutes.
Pause at the top, take one leg off the pad and slowly lower the weight with the other leg back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating the lowering leg.
description: The lever lying two-one leg curl is an isolation exercise targeting the hamstrings using a leverage machine. You curl the pad up with both legs while lying face down and lower it with one leg, overloading the lowering phase of each leg.

name: lever bent-over row with v-bar
instructions: Stand straddling the bar and hinge forward at the hips.
Grasp the v-bar with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), keeping your back straight and your knees slightly bent.
Pull the v-bar towards your abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release the weight back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The lever bent-over row with v-bar is a machine-based exercise targeting the upper back, with secondary emphasis on the biceps and forearms. It involves pulling a v-bar attachment towards the abdomen while maintaining a bent-over position, focusing on squeezing the shoulder blades together.

name: quarter sit-up
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your legs straight on the ground.
Place your arms along your sides, palms down.
Engaging your abs, slowly lift your head and shoulders off the ground, curling only the upper part of your torso.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The quarter sit-up is an abdominal exercise that involves lifting your head and shoulders slightly off the ground, focusing on engaging the abs with minimal hip flexor involvement.

name: half sit-up (male)
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your legs straight on the ground.
Place your arms along your sides.
Engaging your abs, slowly lift your upper body off the ground, curling forward until your torso is upright.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The half sit-up (male) is an abdominal exercise performed with body weight. It involves lying with your legs straight and curling the upper body up until you are sitting upright, primarily targeting the abs and secondarily engaging the hip flexors.

name: prisoner half sit-up (male)
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your legs straight on the ground.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Engaging your abs, slowly lift your upper body off the ground, curling forward until your torso is upright.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The prisoner half sit-up is an abdominal exercise performed with body weight, focusing on the abs and hip flexors. It involves lying on your back with your legs straight, hands behind your head, and curling your torso up until you are sitting upright before lowering back down.

name: arms overhead full sit-up (male)
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your legs straight on the ground.
Extend your arms overhead, keeping them straight.
Engaging your abs, slowly lift your upper body off the ground, sitting up and reaching your hands forward towards your feet.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The arms overhead full sit-up is a bodyweight abdominal exercise where you lie on your back with arms extended overhead and perform a full sit-up, engaging the abs, hip flexors, and lower back.

name: kneeling push-up (male)
instructions: Start by kneeling on the ground with your hands shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing forward.
Walk your hands forward until your body forms a straight line from your head to your knees, keeping your knees on the ground.
Engage your core and lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Continue lowering until your chest is just above the ground, then push back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kneeling push-up (male) is a bodyweight exercise targeting the pectorals, with secondary emphasis on the triceps and shoulders. It is performed from a kneeling position, making it a less challenging variation of the standard push-up, suitable for building foundational upper body strength.

name: basic toe touch (male)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms raised overhead.
Bend forward at the waist, letting your back round naturally and keeping your knees slightly bent.
Reach down towards your toes with your hands, keeping your legs as straight as possible.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The basic toe touch is a bodyweight exercise that primarily targets the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the hamstrings and calves. It involves bending forward at the waist to reach towards the toes, providing a stretch to the posterior chain.

name: side-to-side toe touch (male)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms raised overhead.
Fold forward at the waist and rotate slightly to the right, reaching both hands towards your right foot.
Return to the starting position and then fold forward and rotate slightly to the left, reaching both hands towards your left foot.
Repeat the alternating side-to-side motion for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The side-to-side toe touch is a bodyweight exercise targeting the abs, obliques, and hip flexors. It involves folding forward at the waist to reach towards each foot alternately, promoting core engagement and flexibility.

name: arms apart circular toe touch (male)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms raised overhead, slightly apart.
Keeping your legs straight, bend forward at the waist and reach down towards your toes with both hands.
From the bottom, sweep your arms and torso up to one side in a wide circular motion.
Continue the circle back over the top to the starting position, then repeat circling to the other side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The arms apart circular toe touch is a bodyweight mobility exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and spine. With your arms overhead and apart, you fold forward to touch your toes and then circle back up through the side, alternating directions.

name: hands reversed clasped circular toe touch (male)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, interlace your fingers and press your palms up overhead.
Keeping your hands clasped, bend forward at the waist with your knees slightly bent.
Reach your clasped hands down towards your toes.
Slowly sweep your hands and torso up to one side in a circular motion, keeping your legs straight.
Continue the circular motion over the top until your hands are back overhead.
Repeat the circle in the opposite direction.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: This exercise involves standing with feet shoulder-width apart, hands clasped with palms reversed overhead, folding forward to the toes and circling back up through the side, targeting the glutes and stretching the lower body and spine.

name: chest tap push-up (male)
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
As you lower yourself, tap your chest with your right hand.
Push yourself back up to the starting position.
Repeat the movement, this time tapping your chest with your left hand.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The chest tap push-up is a challenging bodyweight exercise that targets the pectorals while also engaging the triceps and shoulders. It requires strength, coordination, and balance as you momentarily support your body with one hand while tapping your chest with the other.

name: modified hindu push-up (male)
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet hip-width apart.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest towards the ground, keeping your core engaged.
Push through your hands and lift your hips up towards the ceiling, creating an inverted V shape with your body.
Shift your weight forward and lower your hips to return to the push-up position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The modified Hindu push-up is a bodyweight exercise that targets the pectorals while also engaging the triceps, shoulders, and core. It involves a dynamic movement pattern that combines elements of a push-up with a downward dog-like position, challenging both strength and mobility.

name: hands clasped circular toe touch (male)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands clasped together overhead.
Bend your knees slightly and fold forward at the waist.
Lower your hands towards your toes, then sweep them up to one side in a circular motion back overhead.
Repeat the circle in the opposite direction.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The hands clasped circular toe touch is a bodyweight exercise that targets the glutes and also engages the hamstrings, quadriceps, and calves. It involves hinging at the hips and making a circular motion with your hands towards your toes, promoting flexibility and mobility in the lower body.

name: scissor jumps (male)
instructions: Stand in a split stance with your right foot forward and your left foot back.
Jump off the ground and switch your legs in the air, bringing your left foot forward and your right foot back.
As you land, immediately jump again and switch back to your right foot forward.
Continue alternating legs and jumping as quickly as possible.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Scissor jumps are a plyometric cardio exercise that involves jumping and switching your legs forward and back in mid-air. This movement elevates the heart rate and challenges coordination and lower body strength.

name: astride jumps (male)
instructions: Stand with your feet together and your arms by your sides.
Keep your knees soft and your chest up.
Jump and spread your legs wide apart.
At the same time, raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Land softly with your feet wide, then jump back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Astride jumps (male) are a cardio exercise that involves jumping your feet out wide while raising your arms out to the sides, then jumping back together. This movement targets the cardiovascular system while also engaging the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves.

name: high knees (male)
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms bent at your sides.
Drive your right knee up towards your chest while swinging the opposite arm forward.
Lower your right foot and immediately drive your left knee up, landing lightly on the balls of your feet.
Keep alternating knees at a quick, steady pace with your chest up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Half knee bends (male) are a bodyweight cardio exercise in which you drive your knees up alternately while staying in place. This movement elevates the heart rate while also engaging the hip flexors, quadriceps, and calves. This exercise is often used for light cardio and warm-ups.

name: semi squat jump (male)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees and lower your body into a squat position.
Jump explosively, extending your hips and knees while swinging your arms for momentum.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and immediately go into the next repetition.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The semi squat jump is a plyometric exercise that targets the cardiovascular system while also engaging the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. It involves performing a partial squat followed by an explosive jump, making it effective for improving cardiovascular fitness, lower body power, and coordination.

name: star jump (male)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms by your sides.
Bend your knees slightly and jump up explosively.
As you jump, spread your legs and extend your arms out to the sides, forming a star shape with your body.
Land softly on the balls of your feet with your knees slightly bent.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The star jump (male) is a plyometric cardio exercise that involves jumping explosively while spreading the arms and legs out to form a star shape in the air. It targets the cardiovascular system and also engages the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves.

name: pike jump (male)
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and lower into a squat with your arms back.
Jump explosively, lifting both straight legs forward and reaching your hands towards your feet.
Land softly back in the squat, bending your knees to absorb the impact.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: A dynamic bodyweight exercise that involves jumping from a squat and lifting your straight legs forward into a pike in the air, then landing softly. This movement elevates the heart rate and targets the cardiovascular system, with secondary emphasis on the quadriceps, hip flexors, and abs.

name: two toe touch (male)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms raised overhead.
Bend forward at the waist, letting your back round naturally and keeping your knees slightly bent.
Reach down towards your toes with both hands, keeping your legs straight.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The two toe touch (male) is a bodyweight exercise that primarily targets the spine, with secondary emphasis on the hamstrings and glutes. It involves bending forward at the waist to touch your toes, promoting flexibility and mobility in the posterior chain.

name: hyght dumbbell fly
instructions: Lie back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Extend your arms straight up over your chest, with a slight bend in your elbows.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Pause for a moment, then reverse the movement and bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The hyght dumbbell fly is a chest exercise performed on an incline bench using dumbbells. It targets the pectoral muscles and also engages the shoulders. The movement involves lowering the dumbbells in a wide arc to stretch the chest and then bringing them back together above the chest.

name: cable assisted inverse leg curl
instructions: Attach a bar to a cable set at about shoulder height behind you.
Kneel on a pad facing away from the machine with your ankles secured.
Rest the bar across your upper back and hold it with both hands.
Keeping a straight line from your knees to your head, slowly lower your body forward by extending your knees.
Lower as far as you can control, letting the cable support part of your weight.
Exhale and curl your body back up to the upright kneeling position using your hamstrings.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The cable assisted inverse leg curl is an exercise targeting the hamstrings, performed kneeling with your ankles anchored while a cable attached to a bar on your upper back helps you control the lowering of your body towards the floor.

name: resistance band hip thrusts on knees (female)
instructions: Anchor a resistance band low behind you and kneel on the ground with your knees hip-width apart.
Place the band around the front of your hips.
Place your hands on your hips or extend them out in front of you for balance.
Engage your glutes and core muscles.
Sit your hips back towards your heels, then drive them forward against the band and squeeze your glutes until your hips are fully extended.
Hold the position for a moment, then slowly sit back towards your heels.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Resistance band hip thrusts on knees (female) target the glutes primarily, with secondary activation of the hamstrings. The exercise is performed kneeling with a resistance band around your hips anchored behind you, sitting back towards your heels and thrusting the hips forward to engage the glutes.

name: landmine lateral raise
instructions: Stand side-on to the landmine with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Hold the end of the barbell in your outside hand in front of your hips, arm nearly straight.
Keeping your core engaged and back straight, raise the barbell out to the side until your arm reaches shoulder height.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The landmine lateral raise is a shoulder exercise performed using a barbell anchored at one end (landmine setup). It targets the deltoids and also engages the traps and upper back. The movement involves lifting the barbell laterally to shoulder height, emphasizing shoulder strength and stability.

name: kneeling plank tap shoulder (male)
instructions: Start in a kneeling position with your hands on the ground, shoulder-width apart.
Walk your hands forward until your body forms a straight line from your head to your knees, keeping your knees on the ground.
Keeping your core engaged and your hips stable, lift one hand off the ground and tap the opposite shoulder.
Return the hand to the ground and repeat with the other hand.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The kneeling plank tap shoulder is a core stability exercise that targets the abs while also engaging the shoulders and triceps. It requires maintaining a stable plank position while alternately tapping each shoulder with the opposite hand, challenging balance and coordination.

name: exercise ball on the wall calf raise (tennis ball between knees)
instructions: Stand facing a wall and pin an exercise ball between your chest and the wall.
Keep your feet close together under your hips.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, with your arms extended by your sides.
Place a tennis ball between your knees.
Raise your heels off the ground, lifting your body up onto your toes.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: This exercise targets the calves by performing a calf raise while facing a wall with an exercise ball pinned between your chest and the wall and a tennis ball held between the knees. Dumbbells are held for added resistance, and the movement requires balance and coordination.

name: exercise ball on the wall calf raise (tennis ball between ankles)
instructions: Stand facing a wall with your feet close together.
Pin an exercise ball between the wall and your chest.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, with your arms extended by your sides.
Place a tennis ball between your ankles.
Raise your heels off the ground, lifting your body up onto your toes.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: This exercise targets the calves by performing a calf raise while holding a dumbbell in each hand, leaning into an exercise ball pinned between your chest and the wall, and squeezing a tennis ball between the ankles to increase activation and control.

name: smith full squat
instructions: Set up the smith machine with the barbell at shoulder height.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
Step under the bar and position it across your upper back, resting on your traps.
Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar by rotating it off the hooks, keeping your feet under the bar.
Keeping your chest up and core engaged, initiate the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Lower your body until your hips are below your knees, as deep as your mobility allows.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then drive through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The smith full squat is a compound lower body exercise performed using a smith machine. It primarily targets the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. The smith machine provides stability, making it accessible to those who may not be comfortable with free-weight squats, but still requires proper form and core engagement.

name: weighted muscle up
instructions: Attach a weight to a dip belt and hang from gymnastic rings with a false grip, arms fully extended.
Engage your core and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
As the rings reach your chest, lean forward and turn your wrists to transition over the rings.
Press down until your arms are straight and you are supported above the rings, then pause for a moment.
Slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted muscle up is an advanced compound exercise that targets the lats and involves pulling your body above a pair of gymnastic rings with added resistance. It requires significant upper body strength, coordination, and technique, making it suitable for experienced athletes.

name: elbow dips
instructions: Grip the parallel bars and support your body with your arms fully extended, legs hanging.
Keep your body upright and your core engaged.
Bend your elbows and lower your body until your forearms rest on the bars.
Pause for a moment, then push through your hands to lift your forearms off the bars and straighten your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Elbow dips are a bodyweight exercise targeting the triceps, performed on parallel bars. The movement involves lowering from straight-arm support until your forearms rest on the bars, then pressing back up to straight arms.

name: korean dips
instructions: Position yourself between two parallel bars with your arms extended and supporting your body weight.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Korean dips are a challenging bodyweight exercise performed on parallel bars, targeting the pectorals, triceps, and shoulders. The movement requires significant upper body strength, shoulder mobility, and stability, as the body is lowered deeply between the bars before pressing back up.

name: impossible dips
instructions: Position yourself between two parallel bars with your arms fully extended and your body suspended in the air.
Keep your legs straight and together.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: Impossible dips are a challenging bodyweight exercise performed between two parallel bars, focusing on the triceps while also engaging the chest and shoulders. The movement requires significant upper body strength and control, as well as experience with dip variations.

name: weighted one hand pull up
instructions: Grab the pull-up bar with one hand in an overhand grip and hold a dumbbell in your other hand at your side.
Hang from the bar with your arm fully extended and your body straight.
Engage your core and pull your body up towards the bar by bending your elbow and squeezing your back muscles.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Lower your body back down to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The weighted one hand pull up is an advanced bodyweight exercise that targets the latissimus dorsi (lats) and also engages the biceps and forearms. By adding weight, this movement significantly increases the strength and coordination required, making it a challenging exercise for experienced athletes.

name: stalder press
instructions: Start in a handstand with your hands shoulder-width apart on the floor.
Open your legs into a wide straddle and engage your core.
Lean your shoulders forward and lower your hips and straddled legs down beside your arms.
Continue until your legs are low and your feet stay off the ground, supporting your body only on your hands.
Pause for a moment, then compress your hips and press back up through your shoulders until you return to the handstand.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
description: The stalder press is a challenging bodyweight exercise that primarily targets the triceps, while also engaging the shoulders and core. It involves lowering from a handstand into a straddle support on your hands and pressing back up, requiring significant strength, balance, and coordination.

name: elevator
instructions: Hang from a pair of gymnastic rings with your arms straight.
